# Tumnis Guide Detailed Implementation Plan

Status: v1 build manual, September 28, 2026 · Owner: Scott Jordan · Companion to `docs/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` (summary) and `docs/plan/work-packages.yaml` (machine-readable work packages)

This is the test-driven build manual for Tumnis v1: 86 work packages, each with the exact files, interfaces, named spec tests (1133 in total, each with an ID and requirement tags), the red-green-refactor order, fixtures, commands, a done checklist and risks. Every phase opens with an acceptance suite written red on day 1. Part A is the shared vocabulary every work package uses; Part B explains how to work from this document and lists the design points that need Scott's call; Parts C to G are the phases; Parts H to K cover schedule, risks, traceability, decisions and sources.

Code in this document is specification, not finished code: it fixes names, shapes and behavior for the tests. Where a library API could not be confirmed against current documentation, the sketch says "(verify against the pinned version)".

## Part A · Shared reference

Every work package in Parts C to G uses the names, paths, markers and fixtures defined here. When a work package needs something new, it adds it here in the same PR, so this part stays the single inventory.

### A2 · Inside a module

| File | Holds | May import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api.py` | Public functions and DTOs; the only import other modules may use | own module, `tumnis.core`, other modules' `api` |
| `router.py` | FastAPI router under `/v1/<module>`; thin calls into `api.py` | `api.py`, core |
| `mcp.py` | MCP tools; thin calls into `api.py` | `api.py`, core |
| `models.py` | SQLAlchemy tables owned by the module | core |
| `rules.py` | Pure functions, no I/O, time passed in | stdlib, pydantic, own `rules`-only helpers |
| `workflows.py` | DBOS workflows and steps | `api.py`, `adapters`, core |
| `events.py` | Event payload models and subscribers | `api.py`, core |
| `adapters/` | One file per outside dependency, each with `fake.py` | core |
| `migrations/` | Alembic revisions for this module's tables | none at runtime |
| `tests/unit` | Rules and pure code; sockets disabled | anything in the module |
| `tests/integration` | Postgres, DBOS, containers | anything |
| `tests/contract` | Adapter and connector contract suites, schema tests | anything |
| `tests/recordings` | Scrubbed provider payloads + expected canonical records | data only |

### A3 · Conventions

**Test identity.** Every spec test has an ID `T-<WP>-<nn>` (for example `T-P0-18-04`) as the first line of its docstring or in its title. Test functions are named for behavior: `test_agent_cannot_move_backlog_to_done`.

**Markers (pytest).** Registered in `pyproject.toml` under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` with `--strict-markers`:

```toml
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--strict-markers -p pytest_randomly --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket"
xfail_strict = true
markers = [
  "req(*ids): PRD requirement IDs this test proves",
  "wp(id): work package that introduced the test",
  "integration: needs Postgres or containers (sockets allowed)",
  "contract: adapter, connector or schema contract",
  "slow: over 5 seconds",
  "drill: restore drill only, never on PRs",
]
```

Integration tests carry `@pytest.mark.enable_socket` through a module-level `pytestmark`. Spec tests waiting for code carry `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="spec:P0-18")`; the `spec:` prefix is what spec-guard and the traceability job look for. `drill` tests run only when the marker expression names them (`pytest -m drill` in `restore-drill.yml`); the shared fixtures plugin deselects them from every other run, while `--collect-only` (traceability) still lists them (P0-05).

**Vitest.** Titles carry tags in brackets: `test.fails('[P0-25][FR-3.10] replays each queued item once', …)`. `test.fails` is the expected-failure form; it flips to `test` when the code lands.

**Playwright.** Tags through the details object: `test('quick-add from any route', { tag: ['@J2', '@FR-3.3', '@P0-05'] }, async ({ page }) => { test.fail(); … })`. Projects `phone` (375 x 812) and `laptop` (1280 x 800) run every spec.

**Branches and PRs.** `wp/P0-18-spec` then `wp/P0-18-impl` (more `-impl-2` if the WP is L). PR titles `[P0-18] spec: task state machine` and `[P0-18] impl: task state machine`. Labels: `wp:P0-18`, `spec-change` (Scott only), `bug`.

**Commits.** Conventional commits scoped by module: `test(tasks): …`, `feat(tasks): …`, `refactor(core): …`, `fix(search): …`.

**Time.** Rules take `now: datetime` (UTC, aware) and `tz: ZoneInfo`. Nothing in `rules.py` calls `datetime.now()`; a Ruff banned-API rule enforces it.

**Money and units.** Durations in whole minutes (`estimate_minutes`), sizes in bytes, timestamps `timestamptz` UTC.

**Errors.** One problem+json shape: `{type, title, status, detail, code, current?}`; `code` is a stable snake_case string tests assert on (`stale_version`, `idempotency_mismatch`, `transition_not_allowed`).

### A4 · Test layers

| Layer | Runner and command | Scope | Budget | Where it runs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | `uv run pytest -m "not integration and not contract"` | `rules.py`, pure code, sockets disabled | 3 min (PRD: backend rules under 30 s) | GitHub-hosted |
| Contract | `uv run pytest -m contract` + `make gen && git diff --exit-code` + Schemathesis | Schemas, adapters, connectors | 2 min | GitHub-hosted |
| Integration | `uv run pytest -m integration -n auto` | Postgres, DBOS, MinIO, SFTP, clamd, RLS, workflows | 10 min | GitHub-hosted |
| Frontend | `npm run test` (Vitest) | Components, machines, stores, lib | inside Unit budget | GitHub-hosted |
| End to end | `npx playwright test` | Journeys and acceptance, phone and laptop | 10 min | GitHub-hosted, against compose.test with fakes |
| Skills | `uv run python -m profiles.harness run` | Hermes skills, hostile set | 5 min | Homelab self-hosted runner |
| Security | pip-audit, npm audit, Trivy, Semgrep, gitleaks | Dependencies, image, code, secrets | 5 min | GitHub-hosted |
| Performance | k6, Lighthouse CI, bundle check, query counts | NFR budgets | 5 min | Homelab self-hosted runner (stable hardware) |
| Drill | `scripts/drill/restore_drill.sh` | REL-1 | 60 min | Homelab, manual + quarterly |

### A5 · Fixture catalogue

**Backend (`backend/tests/conftest.py` and module conftests)**

| Fixture | Scope | Provides |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pg_container` | session | `PostgresContainer("pgvector/pgvector:pg18")` with owner and app roles created |
| `db_template` | session | Database migrated to head, used as `TEMPLATE` |
| `db` | function | Fresh database `CREATE DATABASE t_<uuid> TEMPLATE db_template`; dropped after |
| `app_role_session` / `owner_session` | function | SQLAlchemy async sessions as each role |
| `workspace` | function | A workspace (`WorkspaceHandle`: `id`, `name`, `ctx`) + user + membership (P0-13); enters the workspace context |
| `two_workspaces` | function | A and B with seeded rows each (`row_factory.minimal_row` for tables the seed leaves empty), for isolation tests |
| `pgbouncer` | session | PgBouncer in transaction mode (pool size 1) in front of `pg_container`; `.libpq(role, dbname)` (P0-06) |
| `clock` | function | `FixedClock` set to 2026-03-09T12:00Z (US DST start week) with `advance()` |
| `dbos` | function | DBOS destroyed, configured on `db`, system tables reset with truncate, launched |
| `worker_killer` | function | Runs a workflow in a subprocess worker and kills it at a named step |
| `app` / `client` | function | FastAPI app with fakes + `httpx.AsyncClient(transport=ASGITransport(app))` |
| `session_client` | function | Client signed in (password + TOTP) with CSRF token handled |
| `key_client(scopes, projects=None)` | function | Client with a fresh API key of those scopes |
| `task_token_client(run)` | function | Client with a task token bound to a run (phase 2) |
| `fakes` | function | Handle to every adapter fake for scripting and assertions |
| `recordings(provider)` | function | Loads `tests/recordings/<provider>/*.json` with expected records |
| `minio`, `sftp_server`, `clamd` | session | Disposable containers (integration only) |
| `fake_runner` | function | In-process runner double speaking the runner protocol over `/ws/runner` |
| `seed` / `load_fixture` | function | Seed set or 2,000-task load set in `db` |
| `query_counter` | function | Counts SQL statements for N+1 assertions |

**Frontend (`frontend/src/test/`)**: `renderWithProviders(ui, {route, queryClient})`, MSW `server` with per-test `server.use(...)`, `vi.useFakeTimers()` helpers, `resetIdb()` over fake-indexeddb, `makeTask()`/`makeProject()` factories generated from zod schemas.

**Playwright (`frontend/e2e/fixtures.ts`)**: `seededApp` (resets the compose.test stack to the seed set through `POST /v1/test/reset`, available only when `TUMNIS_ADAPTERS=fake`), `signedInPage` (TOTP computed from the seed secret), `page.clock` for time travel (`install`, `setFixedTime`, `fastForward`, `runFor`), `fakes` (REST handle to script adapter fakes in the test stack). Until P0-04 and P0-13 fill them, `seededApp` and `signedInPage` are stubs that throw on first use inside the test body (after `test.fail()`), never during fixture setup. Shared helpers, without assertions, live beside them (P0-05): `seedUser()`, `totp(secret, at)`, `listTasks`, `projectIdByName`, `boardColumns`, `recordedWrites`, `quickAddDialog`, `openQuickAdd`, `quickAdd`, `projectCard`, `section`, `taskCards`, `markStartTime`.

### A7 · Data model inventory

Base columns on every tenant table: `id uuid default uuidv7()`, `workspace_id uuid not null`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `version int`, `deleted_at`, `created_by` (actor ref). Every tenant table is created in the `public` schema with P0-06's `create_tenant_table` helper; `created_by` is `text` checked by `ACTOR_CHECK`. Exceptions (allow-listed in the table-registry test): DBOS system tables, `audit_log` (append-only, own columns), `idempotency_keys` (workspace-scoped, no version or deleted_at), `outbox` (workspace-scoped, no version), the global identity and throttle tables (`users`, `auth_throttle`, `deployment_marker`) reached only through SECURITY DEFINER functions, and the ops tables `ops_backup_runs`, `ops_status`, `ops_drill_markers`. A12 lists every column and table added by the work packages; where A12 and this table differ, A12 wins.

### A9 · Queues and schedules (DBOS)

Queues are registered in `tumnis/worker.py` with the DBOS queue API (`DBOS.register_queue(name, worker_concurrency=…, global_concurrency=…, partition_concurrency=…, limiter={"limit": n, "period": s})`; enqueue options through `SetEnqueueOptions(deduplication_id=…, queue_partition_key=…, priority=…)`), per the [DBOS queue tutorial](https://docs.dbos.dev/python/tutorials/queue-tutorial). Confirm the exact signatures against the pinned DBOS version in P0-07.

| Queue | Limits | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `events` | worker 8, polled every 0.2 s | Outbox subscribers (P0-07) |
| `runs` | partition by project, 2 per partition | `dispatch_run` (P2-04), enrichment runs (P1-08) |
| `human` | none | approvals, questions (P2-05) |
| `sync` | limiter per provider | connector_sync, folder_sync (P1-15, P3-02) |
| `decisions` | limiter 1,200 per 60 s | triage_item, label (P1-07, P3-06) |
| `extract` | worker 1 to 2, listened to only by `worker-extract` | extract_document (P1-16) |
| `focus` | none | focus_session (P2-15) |
| `maintenance` | worker 1 | housekeeping (P0-19), backups check (P0-28), audit verify (P0-15) |

Static schedules register in `worker.py` after `DBOS.launch()` with `DBOS.apply_schedules([...])`, per the [DBOS scheduled workflows guide](https://docs.dbos.dev/python/tutorials/scheduled-workflows); the older `@DBOS.scheduled` decorator is not used. `DBOS.recv` is only called in a workflow body (R-30).

| Schedule | Cron (UTC) | Workflow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| planner tick | `*/5 * * * *` | `planner_tick` (P1-11) |
| day-close tick | `*/5 * * * *` | `day_close_tick` checks each workspace's local day end (P0-19) |
| housekeeping | `17 * * * *` | trash purge, idempotency expiry, archive compression (P0-19) |
| backup freshness | `*/15 * * * *` | WAL and base-backup age check (P0-28) |
| audit verify | `23 3 * * *` | `audit_verify` checks and anchors every workspace's audit chain (P0-15) |
| connector syncs | per connection | `connector_sync` (P1-09, P3-02) |
| folder scans | `*/15 * * * *` | `folder_sync` for shares, S3, SFTP (P1-15) |
| runner sweep | `* * * * *` | marks runners offline after 3 missed heartbeats (P1-04) |
| connector sync tick | `* * * * *` | enqueues due `connector_sync` runs (P3-02) |
| unattended tick | `*/5 * * * *` | starts green-light tasks inside the window (P4-04) |

### A13 · Cross-work-package contracts (R-01 to R-38)

These contracts cross work packages. The WP named as owner defines each one fully; every later WP uses the same name and shape. The work packages cite them as R-01 to R-38.

**Shared contracts**

- **R-01 Tables live in `public`.** Every tenant table is created with P0-06's `create_tenant_table` helper in the `public` schema, plain names as in A7 (no `decisions.`, `agents.`, `planning.`, `knowledge.` schemas). `created_by` is `text` with P0-06's `ACTOR_CHECK` and default `app.current_actor()`.
- **R-02 Schema versions are integers.** Every payload model (events, runner messages, packets, enrichment, planning, digests) declares `schema_version: Literal[1] = 1` as a model field and registers with P0-11's `@versioned("<family>", "<name>", 1)`. No string versions like `"runner/v1"`.
- **R-03 Review items (owner P0-18).** `review_items.kind` is `text`, validated against a registry, no Postgres enum. P0-18 ships `register_review_kind(ReviewKindSpec(kind, owner_module, payload_schema, actions, impact_scope))` and `add_review_item(kind: str, *, target, project_id, payload, dedupe_key=None) -> UUID`. Later WPs register their kinds. The "which project does this belong to" kind is `project_match` everywhere.
- **R-04 Review decisions (owner P1-13).** `POST /v1/review/{id}/decide` body `{action, payload?, snooze_until?, version}` with `action` in `accept | edit | reject | snooze | answer | approve | deny`; each kind's `actions` lists which apply and the payload schema per action. Keyboard: Enter = the kind's primary action (accept, approve or answer), `o` = open target, `e` edit, `r` reject/deny, `s` snooze.
- **R-05 Live updates.** `/ws` messages are `{entity, id}`; the review entity name is `review_item`. `/review?kind=` is a string validated against the kind registry, not a closed zod enum.
- **R-06 `task.updated` (owner P0-18)** payload `{task_id, changed_fields: list[str], doc}`. Later WPs only add fields.
- **R-07 `human.decided` (A8)** payload superset: `{item_kind, item_id, target_type, target_id, decision, reason?, previous?, payload?, decision_id?}`.
- **R-08 Task labels.** `tasks.label` is nullable from P0-18; `NULL` means pending. `label_source` in `user | jev | agent | fallback`.
- **R-09 Undo (owner P0-24).** Server-side change log `task_changes(task_id, change_id, actor, before jsonb, after jsonb)` built in P0-24; `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/undo {change_id, version}`. AI changes (P1-07, P1-08) write change rows and use the same route.
- **R-10 Task status API** is `tasks.api.change_status(s, actor, task_id, to, version)` (P0-18). No `update_status`.
- **R-11 Estimates.** One constant `MAX_ESTIMATE_MINUTES = 960` (plan default) in `tumnis/core/limits.py`, used by P0-18 and P1-08.
- **R-12 Time helper.** `tumnis/core/clock.py` owns `local_to_utc(day, local_time, tz)`: a nonexistent local time (DST gap) shifts forward by the gap length (02:30 on a spring-forward day becomes 03:30 local), an ambiguous one takes the first occurrence (fold=0). P0-19 and P1-10 both use it; their tests assert those results.
- **R-13 Brief accessor (owner P0-17).** `knowledge.api.get_brief(project_id) -> DocumentDTO`.
- **R-14 Settings route (owner P0-08).** `GET/PUT /v1/settings/workspace` (timezone, subtask_threshold_min, and later keys), versioned writes, with tests.
- **R-15 Migrations.** P0-12 owns the first revisions for `documents` (knowledge) and `events` (calendar). P0-17 adds `role` and `body_md` in knowledge `0002`. P1-09 extends calendar with a `0002` revision.
- **R-16 Test locations.** Core tests live in `backend/tumnis/core/tests/{unit,integration}`; cross-module suites (meta, isolation, acceptance) in `backend/tests/`. Every path in a spec table starts with `backend/`, `frontend/`, `daemon/` or `profiles/`.
- **R-17 Fixture ownership.** `minio`, `sftp_server` and `clamd` fixtures are created in P0-02 (session scope, integration only). Later WPs reuse them.
- **R-18 Cookies.** `__Host-tumnis_session` and `__Host-tumnis_csrf`; the frontend reads `__Host-tumnis_csrf` and sends `X-CSRF-Token`.
- **R-19 OpenAPI operation IDs** stay `<tag>_<function>` (P0-11). The frontend's `LIVE_MAP` uses the generated names (for example `tasksGetTask`).
- **R-20 Board move.** A drag sends one `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/move {column_id, board_rank, version}`. (The YAML wording "PATCH" is corrected to "one move request".)
- **R-21 Sessions.** `DELETE /v1/auth/sessions` revokes all but the current one; no query parameter.

**Agents, runs and packets**

- **R-22 Run vocabulary (owner P1-04, extended by P2-04).** `RunKind = enrich | plan | task | proposal | stuck | notify`. `RunStatus = queued | running | waiting_on_human | held | succeeded | failed | cancelled | timed_out | runner_lost`. P1-04 defines both enums with all values; P2-02 and later alter behavior, never re-add the column. `run_token_scopes` covers every kind.
- **R-23 Requesting a run (owner P2-04).** `agents.api.request_run(task_id, kind, *, unattended=False, priority=None) -> UUID` creates the runs row and enqueues `dispatch_run(run_id)` with `SetWorkflowID(run_id)` and the project partition key. Stuck (P4-02), proposal (P3-07) and unattended (P4-04) runs all go through it; `kind="stuck"` is allowed for any task label.
- **R-24 One packet (owner P1-17 builder, extended by P2-02).** Module `agents/packet_builder.py`, one `TaskPacket` model with `kind` and integer `schema_version`, route `GET /v1/tasks/{id}/packet` on the agents router. P2-02 extends that module (untrusted blocks with `id="u-<nonce>"` on open and close tags, policy, callback). Proposal (P3-07) and stuck (P4-02) packets are built with `build_packet(kind=...)`, never by hand.
- **R-25 Runner protocol.** Integer `schema_version` per message. `register` carries `protocol_versions: list[int]`; the session uses the highest shared. Protocol 1: per-message `ack{ack_of}`. Protocol 2 adds batched `ack{message_ids}`, `stream`, `cancel`, `upload_artifact`, `archive`, and a `status` message that carries `profile_version`. `workdir_policy: Literal["none", "worktree"]` (protocol 1 sends only "none"). The daemon never builds prompts: it passes the packet's `prompt_text` to Hermes. Health uses P1-04's `health_check`/`health_report` and `check_profile_health`; P2-10 adds fields to those.
- **R-26 Daemon install.** User `tumnis-agent`, home `/home/tumnis-agent`, command `tumnis-daemon run --config /etc/tumnis/daemon.toml`. A `path` code location must be under the agent home, or provisioning adds it to `ReadWritePaths`.
- **R-27 Tokens (owner P0-14).** `auth/tokens.py` with `issue_task_token`, `revoke_task_tokens_for_run`, prefix format as P0-14 defines. A task token expires when its run ends (not at start plus max run time).
- **R-28 Authorization errors.** Missing scope: 403 `insufficient_scope`. A project-limited key or task token touching another project: 404 `not_found` (do not leak existence), on both REST and MCP.
- **R-29 Run time.** Active time cap 60 min (SAF-5 default) excludes time waiting on a human; a wall-clock ceiling of 24 h (plan default) also applies. This is flagged for Scott in Part B.
- **R-30 DBOS rules.** `DBOS.recv` only in a workflow body, never inside a step or an HTTP handler. Schedules register with `DBOS.apply_schedules` in `worker.py`. The `runs` queue is registered with priority enabled (verify the flag against the pinned version). One `WAIT_SLICE_S = 3600`. Timeouts that tests need to reach take a configurable duration (short in tests), not a `FixedClock`.
- **R-31 Keys without a run.** Profile and cron API keys get `tasks:read` and `context:read` by default. Any write made by a key with no run is marked tainted and cannot take a gated action; `request_approval` needs a task token.
- **R-32 Jev rate limit** is enforced in `decisions.api.decide`, keyed on the Jev credential (1,200 per 60 s, FR-11.9), not on workflow counts.
- **R-33 Surface models.** Every MCP tool and REST twin takes P2-01's `WriteInput` or `SurfaceInput` and a `Caller`. `agents.api.check_action(caller, action_class) -> Allowed | ApprovalRequired | Denied` is defined in P2-05.
- **R-34 Delegation.** Depth comes from the task's delegation chain (not from the caller's run). A loop is refused with a review item. `delegate` scope is not blocked at key creation; `master_only` is checked when the tool is called.
- **R-35 Tools inventory** includes `pause_agents` and `record_human_reply` (both master-only).
- **R-36 Knowledge twins.** Upload stays `POST /v1/knowledge/documents` (multipart). The `add_document` REST twin is `POST /v1/knowledge/documents/text`. Search parameter is `q` everywhere. `search_knowledge(q, *, project_id, limit, mode="fts")` defined in P1-17; P3-10 adds `mode="hybrid"`.
- **R-37 Names reused as defined earlier:** `GET /v1/day/{date}/summary`, `GET /v1/metrics/summary`, `POST /v1/test/fakes/{adapter}/script`, `POST /v1/test/tick/{schedule_name}` with schedule `planner-tick`, `notifications.rules.delivery_decision`, P2-15's `LEVEL_EVENTS` and its `block_end` mechanism, one purge route `POST /v1/purges {scope, id, reason}`, `decisions/questions/` as a package from P2-05, note source value `note`, embeddings table `embeddings(chunk_id, project_id, model, embedding vector)`.
- **R-38 XState.** Every guard and action a machine references is declared in `setup({ guards, actions })`.

## Part B · How to use this plan

This is the build manual for Tumnis v1. The summary plan (`docs/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md`) says what gets built in which phase and why; this document says exactly how: files, interfaces, named spec tests, the order to turn them green, and the checks that close each work package. The machine-readable list of work packages is `docs/plan/work-packages.yaml`; IDs, titles, sizes, needs and traces here match it exactly.

### B1 · Map of this document

| Part | Holds | Read it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A · Shared reference | Repo layout, conventions, markers, fixtures, adapters, data model, events, queues, routes, config, additions, cross-WP contracts (R-01 to R-38) | Before any WP; whenever a name is in doubt |
| B · How to use | This guide, the TDD rules, the working loop, and the design points settled while detailing | First |
| C · Phase 0 · Foundation | Acceptance suite detail, M0.1 to M0.6, P0-01 to P0-30 | Weeks 1 to 4 |
| D · Phase 1 · AI core loop | Acceptance suite detail, M1.1 to M1.7, P1-01 to P1-18 | Weeks 5 to 7 |
| E · Phase 2 · Agent layer | Acceptance suite detail, M2.1 to M2.5, P2-01 to P2-18 | Weeks 8 to 11 |
| F · Phase 3 · Capture | Acceptance suite detail, M3.1 to M3.3, P3-01 to P3-14 | Weeks 12 to 14 |
| G · Phase 4 · Hardening | Acceptance suite detail, M4.1, P4-01 to P4-06 | Weeks 15 to 16 |
| H · Schedule and capacity | Week-by-week order, effort per phase, parallel streams, critical path | Planning each week |
| I · Risk register | Risks per WP with early signals and fallbacks | Weekly review |
| J · Traceability | Every PRD requirement, the WPs that build it, and how many spec tests prove it | Gate reviews |
| K · Decisions and sources | What needs Scott's call, with defaults; every source cited | Now, then at each gate |

### B2 · Anatomy of a work package

Every WP uses the same sections in the same order:

| Section | What it gives the implementer |
| --- | --- |
| Header table | Milestone, size, needs, unblocks, traces |
| **Goal.** / **Scope.** | What exists afterwards, and what is explicitly left to another WP |
| **Files** | Every path created or edited, with its purpose |
| **Interfaces** | Typed signatures, models, DDL, message formats the code must match |
| **Spec tests** | Test IDs `T-<WP>-<nn>`, file and function name, layer, what each proves, requirement tags; Given/When/Then for the non-obvious ones |
| **TDD sequence** | The order to remove expected-failure markers, the smallest code for each green, the refactor after |
| **Implementation notes** | Decisions inside the WP, edge cases, library gotchas with sources |
| **Fixtures, fakes and data** | What to add to the shared harness |
| **Commands** | Exactly what to run locally and in CI |
| **Done checklist** | The WP's exit, including manual checks on the homelab or the phone |
| **Risks and fallbacks** | What could go wrong and the way out |

Sizes: S up to 1 agent-assisted day, M 1 to 2, L 3 to 4 (ships as two or more PRs). Where a code sketch says "(verify against the pinned version)", the API was not confirmed against current docs and must be checked when the dependency is pinned.

### B3 · TDD rules (binding on humans and agents)

1. **Double loop.** Each phase's acceptance suite is committed red on its first day (outer loop). Each WP's spec tests are committed red before its code (inner loop). A phase closes when its outer loop is green.
2. **Red is committed.** Spec tests land in their own PR as expected failures: `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="spec:<WP>")` with `xfail_strict = true`, `test.fails` in Vitest, `test.fail()` in Playwright. A marked test that starts passing fails the build, so markers come off the moment code works.
3. **Spec tests are locked.** spec-guard fails a PR that edits an assertion or deletes a test in an existing test file unless Scott adds `spec-change`. Removing a `spec:` marker is allowed; generated contract tests are exempt.
4. **Bug fixes prove red.** On `bug` PRs, red-proof runs the new test against the base commit and requires a failure there.
5. **Every test names its requirement** (`@pytest.mark.req`, bracket tags in Vitest, `tag:` in Playwright) and its WP. The traceability job fails when a requirement in a finished phase has no test.
6. **Rules are pure; time is an input.** `rules.py` does no I/O and takes `now` and `tz`; a Ruff banned-API rule forbids `datetime.now` there.
7. **Fakes obey the real contract.** One contract suite per adapter runs against the fake and the real implementation (container or recordings).
8. **Durability is tested by killing.** Every DBOS workflow has a kill-and-resume test.
9. **Real Postgres everywhere.** Integration runs on `pgvector/pgvector:pg18`; the DBOS system database lives on it too.
10. **Sweeps beat checklists.** Meta-tests walk every route, table and MCP tool.
11. **Model behavior is tested on JSON.** Skill tests assert tool calls and JSON, three runs per case, all must pass, on the homelab runner.
12. **Flaky means broken.** Quarantine within a day with an issue, fix within a week. Nightly mutmut reports surviving mutants in `rules.py`.

**Definition of done (every WP):** spec tests merged red first; all green with markers removed; no spec-guard override without Scott's label; requirement and WP tags on every new test; coverage gates hold (80% on rules and the MCP layer, full coverage on planner, focus, threshold and state-machine rules); a new adapter ships with its fake and contract suite; a new module with its import-linter contract; generated OpenAPI, schemas and client committed; the PR preview checked at phone width when UI changed; Part A updated when a name was added.

### B4 · The working loop for one WP

1. Pick the next WP whose `needs` are merged. Read its section here and the requirements it traces.
2. Spec PR (`wp/<WP>-spec`, title `[<WP>] spec: …`): the spec tests from the table, as expected failures, plus any fixtures they need. Scott reviews for intent.
3. Implementation PR(s) (`wp/<WP>-impl`): follow the TDD sequence, one marker at a time; commit each green; refactor while green.
4. CI green including spec-guard and traceability; PR description lists the WP, requirement IDs and the test summary.
5. Scott reviews the diff and the preview (phone width for UI).
6. Merge; Coolify deploys; tick the Done checklist in the PR.

From phase 2, the same loop can run through Tumnis itself: the WP becomes a task on the Tumnis project and the template's coding skill (P2-12) follows these steps.

### B5 · Design points settled while detailing (need Scott's OK)

Writing the work packages at this depth surfaced gaps between the PRD, the architecture doc and how the tools actually behave. Each was settled with the default below so the plan is buildable; each one is also listed in Part K.

| # | Point | Default taken in the plan | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Hermes `mcp serve` is stdio-only and exposes no run tool, so the PRD's "remote endpoint" runner cannot dispatch runs today | The runner daemon is the real transport; the remote-endpoint transport is built behind the AgentAdapter and tested only against a fake until Hermes supports it | P1-04 |
| 2 | TypeSafe ships no Jev MCP server, but FR-11.6 assumes one | A small wrapper MCP server in `profiles/shared/jev-mcp` | P1-05 |
| 3 | Jev returns no reason text, and Noul answers carry no confidence | The one-line label reason is built from companion Noul questions; Nouls route on yes and no probability bands | P1-01, P1-02 |
| 4 | SAF-5's 60-minute run limit would kill runs parked on an approval, which has no deadline | Active-time cap of 60 min excludes time waiting on a human; a 24 h wall-clock ceiling also applies | P2-04, P4-04 |
| 5 | DBOS partition limits are one value per queue | Per-project max concurrent runs is fixed at 2 in v1 (shown read-only) | P2-04 |
| 6 | Coolify API tokens are scoped to a team, not an app | SAF-3 isolation needs one Coolify team per project | P2-10 |
| 7 | FR-8.2 treats a Discord answer like an in-app answer | The master relays answers to questions and focus replies; approvals and results must be decided in the app | P2-16 |
| 8 | FR-15.11 says MinIO notifications are "signed"; MinIO sends a bearer token | Verify the token, then re-check the named object directly, so a forged body can only trigger a stat | P3-13 |
| 9 | FR-4.5 does not define "green light" | An AI task the user queued, with acceptance criteria, untainted, project not paused, kill switch off | P4-04 |
| 10 | FR-5.6 allows drafts, but SAF-1 gates every action on a tainted run | `draft_reply` on a tainted run returns `approval_required` | P3-03 |
| 11 | Profile and cron API keys can act without a run, outside taint gating | Such keys default to read scopes; writes from a key with no run are tainted and cannot take gated actions | P2-02, P2-05 |
| 12 | A proposal run has no task, but runs hang off tasks | A hidden carrier task (`system_role = triage_carrier`) per routed item, excluded from every list, board, search and plan | P3-07 |
| 13 | FR-10.6 says the master captures detours | Tumnis creates the detour task when the user asks; the master only phrases the "back to X?" question, so capture works with the master offline | P4-01 |
| 14 | The local-decisions-only switch is per project, but matching happens before the project is known | Any item whose sender or attendee domain links to a local-only project never goes to Jev | P3-06 |
| 15 | GitHub cannot reach a Coolify on the private network, so GitHub App auto-deploy webhooks fail | The homelab self-hosted runner triggers Coolify deploys and previews through the Coolify API after CI is green | P0-04 |
| 16 | The architecture's task state diagram has no Today to Done path for Human tasks | Kept as drawn: a quick Human task needs Start, then Done. Approving a `today → done` edge for Human tasks is a one-line `spec-change` if that grates in daily use | P0-18 |
| 17 | GitHub status webhooks cannot reach a private server (FR-12.1) | Refresh on open plus polling; webhook verification is built for a future relay | P2-13 |

Technical notes the plan also follows: `/health/*` and `/metrics` sit at the root, not under `/v1`; phone width is 375 px (PRD) rather than the architecture doc's 390 px; `users` is a global identity table reached through SECURITY DEFINER functions; uploads land in a local spool and are scanned before they reach a project folder; "50 MB" is read as 50 MiB; calendar sync uses a date window rather than sync tokens; in a sync conflict Tumnis's own copy takes the conflict name, so files Tumnis did not create are never renamed; the MCP SDK v2 server class is `MCPServer` and `/mcp` is mounted as a raw route to avoid a redirect that breaks POST.

## Part C · Phase 0 · Foundation (weeks 1 to 4)

Phase 0 ships a Tumnis Scott can run on the homelab and use by hand, with every test layer, CI guard and safety baseline in place before any AI code.

**Exit gate.** User can run it on the homelab and manage real projects by hand (PRD). Here that means the A0 suite is green and Scott has run his real projects in it for 3 working days.

### Phase 0 acceptance suite detail

The phase 0 outer loop. P0-05 commits every block below as an expected failure on day 1 of week 1; each later WP removes nothing from these files, it only makes steps pass. The marker comes off when the last WP in "Turns green" merges. A0.4 runs only in the drill workflow, never on a PR.

Shared preconditions for the Playwright blocks: the `compose.test.yaml` stack runs with `TUMNIS_ADAPTERS=fake` and `DEPLOYMENT_ENV=preview`; `seededApp` calls `POST /v1/test/reset` before each test; `signedInPage` signs in as the seed user (`scott@example.test`, password from `backend/fixtures/seed/workspace.yaml`, TOTP computed with `otplib` from the seed secret). Every spec runs in the `phone` (375 x 812) and `laptop` (1280 x 800) projects.

**A0.1 · Capture to dashboard by hand (J2)**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| File | `frontend/e2e/journeys/J2.spec.ts`, test `A0.1 sign in, create project, quick-add, board, today, dashboard` |
| Tags | `@A0.1 @J2 @FR-1.1 @FR-1.2 @FR-2.2 @FR-3.3 @SEC-1 @P0-05` |
| Preconditions | Seed set loaded; browser context has no cookies (the test signs in through the UI, not through `signedInPage`); `page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-03-09T14:00:00Z') })` so "today" is fixed; workspace timezone `America/New_York` from the seed |
| Layer | Playwright, both projects |

Steps:

1. Go to `/`. Expect a redirect to `/login` (no session).
2. Fill email and password, submit. Expect the TOTP step, and no `__Host-tumnis_session` cookie yet (`context.cookies()` has none).
3. Fill the TOTP code computed from the seed secret at the fixed clock time. Expect `/` (dashboard).
4. Assert through `context.cookies()`: `__Host-tumnis_session` has `httpOnly: true`, `secure: true`, `sameSite: 'Lax'`, `path: '/'`; `__Host-tumnis_csrf` exists and is not HttpOnly.
5. Open the project list, press "New project", enter name `Acme rebrand`, client `Acme`, goal `Ship the new logo`, save. Expect the project page `/projects/<id>` with the header showing the name.
6. Go back to `/`. Press `/` (laptop) or tap the quick-add button (phone, located by `getByRole('button', { name: 'Quick add' })`).
7. Type `Send logo drafts to Acme`. In the project typeahead type `acm`, choose `Acme rebrand`. Press Enter.
8. Expect a toast "Added to Acme rebrand" and the quick-add dialog closed.
9. Go to `/projects/<id>?view=tasks`. Expect the task under "Up next".
10. Switch to `?view=board`. Expect the card in the Backlog column.
11. Drag the card to the Today column (laptop: `dragTo`; phone: keyboard drag through the card's move menu, since touch drag is covered in P0-24's component tests).
12. Go to `/`.

Assertions:

- Step 9 and 10 find exactly one card with that title.
- After step 11 the network log has exactly one `POST /v1/tasks/<id>/move` whose body is `{column_id, board_rank, version}` (the Today column's id, a new rank, the version read), with `Idempotency-Key` and `X-CSRF-Token` headers, and no other write to that task.
- Step 12: the Today panel lists `Send logo drafts to Acme` with the project name and whatever label quick-add set (phase 0 has no AI labeling; P0-25 defines the default); the `Acme rebrand` project card shows health "On track" and open count 1.
- At 1280 x 800 the dashboard has no vertical scroll (`document.scrollingElement.scrollHeight <= innerHeight`).

Turns green: P0-13 (steps 1 to 4), P0-17 (step 5), P0-20 and P0-25 (steps 6 to 8), P0-24 (steps 9 to 11), P0-23 (step 12). Marker removed in P0-25 or P0-23, whichever merges last.

**A0.2 · Offline capture**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| File | `frontend/e2e/acceptance/A0.2-offline-capture.spec.ts` |
| Tags | `@A0.2 @FR-3.10 @REL-2 @P0-05` |
| Preconditions | `seededApp`, `signedInPage`; the service worker is registered and active (`await page.evaluate(() => navigator.serviceWorker.ready)`); seed project `Tumnis dogfood` exists |
| Layer | Playwright, both projects |

Steps:

1. Count tasks through the API: `GET /v1/tasks?project_id=<dogfood>` (request fixture with the session) and keep `n0`.
2. `await context.setOffline(true)`.
3. Quick-add `Offline one` and `Offline two` to `Tumnis dogfood`.
4. Expect both in the Tasks view with a pending mark (`getByTestId('pending-mark')` count 2).
5. `await page.reload()` while still offline. Expect the app shell to render from the service worker and both pending items to still show (IndexedDB).
6. `await context.setOffline(false)`, then wait for `offlineQueue` to reach `done` (the page exposes `data-offline-queue-state="idle"` on `<body>`).
7. Reload once more (this is the "replay on app open" path; it must not send anything twice).

Assertions:

- After step 6 the pending marks are gone.
- After step 7 `GET /v1/tasks?project_id=<dogfood>` returns `n0 + 2` tasks, with exactly one `Offline one` and one `Offline two`.
- The fake server log (`GET /v1/test/requests?path=/v1/tasks&method=POST`, fakes only) shows each idempotency key at most twice, and the second request with the same key got the stored response (header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`).

Turns green: P0-10 (stored responses), P0-22 (service worker), P0-25 (queue and replay).

**A0.3 · Tenant isolation over every route**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| File | `backend/tests/acceptance/test_a0_3_tenant_isolation.py::test_workspace_b_cannot_touch_workspace_a` (parametrized over the route inventory), backed by the table-level suite in `backend/tests/isolation/` |
| Markers | `integration`, `req("Hosted readiness", "ADR-0009")`, `wp("P0-05")` |
| Preconditions | `two_workspaces` (A and B, each with seed rows in every tenant table that exists), `key_client` for B with every scope, `session_client` for B |
| Layer | Integration (pytest, real Postgres, app role) |

Steps:

1. Build the route inventory from `app.routes` filtered to `/v1` (the same walker as the route-registry test in P0-10).
2. For each route with a path parameter that names a row (`{id}`, `{project_id}`, `{task_id}` and so on), substitute the ID of a row owned by A.
3. For list routes, call them as B with no filter and with A's IDs in every filter parameter.
4. For each write route, send a valid body (from the route's request model, built by `polyfactory` from the Pydantic model) that targets A's row.
5. After the sweep, read every tenant table as the owner role and compare with a snapshot taken before step 2.

Assertions:

- Every read of A's row as B returns 404 (not 403, so existence does not leak), and every list returns no row whose `workspace_id` is A's.
- Every write targeting A's row returns 404; no A row changed (snapshot equal, `version` unchanged).
- The sweep covers at least one route per module present (guard against an empty inventory passing).

Turns green: P0-06 (RLS on every table), P0-10 (route walker), P0-14 (key and session clients). It stays green as each later WP adds routes, because the inventory is computed.

**A0.4 · Restore drill (drill workflow only)**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| File | `.github/workflows/restore-drill.yml` running `scripts/drill/restore_drill.sh --mode prod`; the thresholds are also encoded in `backend/tests/acceptance/test_a0_4_restore_drill.py`, which reads the drill's recorded `audit_log` row |
| Markers | `drill` (new marker, excluded from every PR job), `req("REL-1")`, `wp("P0-05")` |
| Preconditions | Homelab self-hosted runner; B2 repository 2 configured (P0-28); the running release's Postgres image present |
| Layer | Drill workflow: manual `workflow_dispatch` (input `mode`: `prod` or `rehearsal`) and quarterly `schedule: "41 6 3 1,4,7,10 *"` (3rd day of Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct, 06:41 UTC) |

Steps (driven by the drill script P0-28 owns; the numbers match its step list):

1. Preflight: `pgbackrest --stanza=tumnis --repo=2 info --output=json` shows a full backup and an archive range; a `trap` removes the scratch container and volume on any exit.
2. Marker: `INSERT INTO ops_drill_markers (id, kind) VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), 'marker')` on the source, commit, then read `clock_timestamp()` and `pg_walfile_name(pg_current_wal_lsn())` into `T_MARKER` and `MARKER_WAL`.
3. Fence: after 2 s insert a second row with `kind = 'fence'`, commit, read `FENCE_WAL`. The fence is a commit after the target, so recovery can stop exactly at `T_MARKER`.
4. Wait for archive: poll `pg_stat_archiver.last_archived_wal` every 5 s until it reaches `FENCE_WAL`, with a 15-minute timeout; record `RPO_OBSERVED`.
5. Restore on a new volume (`--mode prod` never touches the production container): `pgbackrest --stanza=tumnis --repo=2 --type=time "--target=$T_MARKER" --target-action=promote restore`, starting the RTO clock.
6. Start the scratch server with `archive_mode=off` and wait until `pg_is_in_recovery()` is false.
7. Checks on the scratch database: marker row present, fence row absent, `tumnis migrate --check` at head, `tumnis audit verify` passes, DBOS system tables present.
8. Stop the clock and run `tumnis drill record --mode "$MODE" --rpo-seconds ... --rto-seconds ... --target "$T_MARKER"` against the source.

Assertions:

- The marker row exists in the restored database and the fence row does not (point-in-time precision).
- `RPO_OBSERVED` is under 15 minutes and the restore through checks is under 3,600 s (RTO 1 h).
- One `audit_log` row with `action = 'drill.completed'` carries both numbers; `test_a0_4_restore_drill.py` reads it and re-checks the thresholds, so they are versioned in code.
- Any failed step exits non-zero, which fails the drill job.

Turns green: P0-28. P0-05 commits the workflow, the test and a stub `restore_drill.sh` that exits 1 until P0-28 lands.

### M0.1 · Harness and walking skeleton (week 1)

Nothing ships until the tests can run, CI can block a merge and a PR can deploy a preview.

#### P0-01 · Repo, toolchain and agent rules

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M0.1 Harness and walking skeleton (week 1) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | none |
| Unblocks | P0-02 and, through it, every WP |
| Traces | ADR-0001, SEC-7 |

**Goal.** The monorepo exists in the architecture layout with all 15 module skeletons, and the toolchain (uv, Ruff, mypy, import-linter, pre-commit, Renovate) enforces the module boundaries from the first commit. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md give a coding agent everything it needs to follow the TDD rules without reading this plan.

**Scope.** In: folder tree per A1, 15 empty module packages with the A2 shape, `backend/pyproject.toml` (tool config only; test config is P0-02), `.importlinter`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `renovate.json`, `Makefile` (targets that later WPs fill), 11 ADR files, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, `frontend/package.json` with ESLint, Prettier and `tsc` only. Out: pytest fixtures and markers (P0-02), CI workflows (P0-03), Dockerfile and compose (P0-04), any runtime code.

**Interfaces**

The module registry is the single list every meta-test and the app factory read:

```python
# backend/tumnis/core/modules.py (P0-08 extends it with flags)
from typing import Final

MODULES: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = (
    "auth", "projects", "tasks", "planning", "agents", "focus", "decisions", "search",
    "knowledge", "integrations", "calendar", "github", "coolify", "notifications", "usage",
)
SUBSCRIBE_ONLY: Final[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"search", "usage"})
MODULE_FILES: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = (
    "api.py", "router.py", "mcp.py", "models.py", "rules.py", "workflows.py", "events.py",
)
MODULE_DIRS: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = ("adapters", "migrations", "tests")
```

`backend/.importlinter` (contract types from the [import-linter docs](https://import-linter.readthedocs.io/en/stable/); wildcard `*` is one segment, `**` any depth):

```ini
[importlinter]
root_package = tumnis
include_external_packages = True

[importlinter:contract:modules-api-only]
name = Modules reach each other only through api.py
type = independence
modules =
    tumnis.modules.auth
    tumnis.modules.projects
    tumnis.modules.tasks
    tumnis.modules.planning
    tumnis.modules.agents
    tumnis.modules.focus
    tumnis.modules.decisions
    tumnis.modules.search
    tumnis.modules.knowledge
    tumnis.modules.integrations
    tumnis.modules.calendar
    tumnis.modules.github
    tumnis.modules.coolify
    tumnis.modules.notifications
    tumnis.modules.usage
ignore_imports =
    tumnis.modules.** -> tumnis.modules.*.api

[importlinter:contract:rules-are-pure]
name = rules.py imports nothing that does I/O
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    tumnis.modules.*.rules
forbidden_modules =
    tumnis.core.db
    tumnis.core.tenancy
    tumnis.core.outbox
    tumnis.core.events
    tumnis.core.cache
    tumnis.core.net
    tumnis.core.adapters
    tumnis.core.audit
    tumnis.modules.*.models
    tumnis.modules.*.workflows
    tumnis.modules.*.adapters
    tumnis.modules.*.router
    tumnis.modules.*.mcp
    sqlalchemy
    psycopg
    dbos
    fastapi
    httpx
    aioboto3
    asyncssh
    redis
    structlog

[importlinter:contract:core-below-modules]
name = core never imports a module or a composition root
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    tumnis.core
forbidden_modules =
    tumnis.modules
    tumnis.app
    tumnis.worker
    tumnis.cli
    tumnis.wiring

[importlinter:contract:module-graph-acyclic]
name = No cycles between modules
type = acyclic_siblings
ancestors =
    tumnis.modules

[importlinter:contract:search-usage-subscribe-only]
name = search and usage call no other module
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    tumnis.modules.search
    tumnis.modules.usage
forbidden_modules =
    tumnis.modules.auth
    tumnis.modules.projects
    tumnis.modules.tasks
    tumnis.modules.planning
    tumnis.modules.agents
    tumnis.modules.focus
    tumnis.modules.decisions
    tumnis.modules.knowledge
    tumnis.modules.integrations
    tumnis.modules.calendar
    tumnis.modules.github
    tumnis.modules.coolify
    tumnis.modules.notifications
```

The composition roots (`tumnis.app`, `tumnis.worker`, `tumnis.cli`, and `tumnis.wiring` from P0-02) sit outside the independence contract on purpose: they import every module's `router`, `mcp`, `workflows` and `events` to wire them. Test files under `backend/tests/` are outside `root_package` and are not analyzed.

Ruff and mypy sections of `backend/pyproject.toml` ([Ruff settings](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/), negated per-file patterns start with `!`):

```toml
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 100
src = ["tumnis", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "W", "F", "I", "B", "UP", "SIM", "RUF", "ASYNC", "S", "DTZ", "TID", "PT", "N", "C4", "RET", "PL"]
ignore = ["PLR0913"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"datetime.datetime.now".msg = "rules.py takes `now` as an argument (AGENTS.md, Time)."
"datetime.datetime.utcnow".msg = "rules.py takes `now` as an argument."
"datetime.datetime.today".msg = "rules.py takes `now` as an argument."
"datetime.date.today".msg = "rules.py takes `today` as an argument."
"time.time".msg = "rules.py takes `now` as an argument."
"time.monotonic".msg = "rules.py takes `now` as an argument."
"random".msg = "rules.py is deterministic; pass the value in."
"uuid.uuid4".msg = "rules.py is deterministic; pass the id in."
"os".msg = "rules.py reads no environment and no files."
"subprocess".msg = "rules.py does no I/O."
"socket".msg = "rules.py does no I/O."

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# The banned-api list applies only to rules files: ignore TID251 everywhere else.
"!tumnis/modules/*/rules*.py" = ["TID251"]
"tests/**" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "S105", "S106"]
"tumnis/modules/*/tests/**" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "S105", "S106"]
"tumnis/modules/*/migrations/**" = ["N999"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
exclude = ["tumnis/modules/.*/migrations/"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["tumnis.core.*", "tumnis.modules.*.rules", "tumnis.modules.*.rules_*", "tumnis.modules.*.api"]
strict = true
```

- T-P0-01-04 to 07. Given a `tmp_path` tree `lintpkg/` built by the helper `make_lint_tree(tmp_path, files: dict[str, str])` that creates `lintpkg/core/`, `lintpkg/modules/<m>/{api,models,rules,router}.py` for all 15 names and writes `.importlinter` by replacing `tumnis` with `lintpkg` in the real file. When `lint-imports --config <tmp>/.importlinter` runs with `PYTHONPATH=<tmp>` (`subprocess.run`, cwd `tmp_path`). Then exit code is 1 and stdout contains the offending edge, for example `lintpkg.modules.tasks.router -> lintpkg.modules.projects.models`; for T-P0-01-05 exit code 0.
- T-P0-01-08. When `ruff check --stdin-filename tumnis/modules/demo/rules.py -` runs from `backend/` with `from datetime import datetime\nx = datetime.now()` on stdin, then the output contains `TID251`; with `--stdin-filename tumnis/modules/demo/api.py` it does not.
- T-P0-01-09. Given every `tumnis/modules/*/rules*.py`, when parsed with `ast`, then every `Import` and `ImportFrom` names a module in `RULES_ALLOWED = {"__future__", "dataclasses", "datetime", "zoneinfo", "enum", "typing", "typing_extensions", "collections", "collections.abc", "itertools", "functools", "math", "decimal", "fractions", "re", "uuid", "bisect", "heapq", "pydantic", "tumnis.core.types"}` or `tumnis.modules.<same module>.rules*`. Catches stdlib I/O (`os`, `pathlib`, `socket`) that import-linter may not see.
- T-P0-01-11. AGENTS.md must contain the headings `## TDD rules`, `## Module boundaries`, `## Where things go`, `## Tests and markers`, `## Adapters and fakes`, `## Time`, `## Commands`, `## Never`.

1. Red: T-P0-01-01 and T-P0-01-02 (remove markers). Green: create the tree and 15 skeletons with a generator script `scripts/new_module.py <name>` (also used by later modules). Refactor: make the generator idempotent.
2. Red: T-P0-01-03. Green: `core/modules.py`. Refactor: have the generator append to `MODULES` and the independence contract.
3. Red: T-P0-01-04, 05. Green: write `.importlinter`, add `import-linter` to dev deps. Refactor: extract `make_lint_tree` into `backend/tests/meta/_lint_tree.py`.
4. Red: T-P0-01-06, 07. Green: the `rules-are-pure` and `module-graph-acyclic` contracts.
5. Red: T-P0-01-08. Green: Ruff banned-api and per-file-ignores.
6. Red: T-P0-01-09. Green: `RULES_ALLOWED` in the test plus `tumnis/core/types.py` (shared pure types such as `ActorRef`, `WorkspaceId`).
7. Red: T-P0-01-10. Green: fix whatever the empty tree trips (docstrings only, so usually nothing). Refactor: add the Makefile `check` target and time it.

**Implementation notes**

- `renovate.json`: `extends: ["config:recommended", ":pinAllExceptPeerDependencies"]`, `lockFileMaintenance.enabled: true`, package rules: `@tiptap/*` and `dbos` get `automerge: false` and label `needs-suite` (their suites guard upgrades), everything else automerges patch releases only after the full pipeline passes. Pin Hermes, skills and MCP servers by version in `profiles/*/VERSION` (SEC-7), tracked by a Renovate regex manager.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` uses `repo: local` hooks that run `uv run ruff check --fix`, `uv run ruff format`, `uv run mypy tumnis`, `uv run lint-imports`, `npm --prefix frontend run lint`, plus `gitleaks protect --staged` and the standard `check-yaml`, `end-of-file-fixer`. Local hooks use the locked tool versions, so pre-commit and CI never disagree.
- Makefile targets (bodies filled as WPs land): `check` (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy`, `lint-imports`, unit pytest with `-n auto`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test -- --run`), `test` (unit + contract), `test-int`, `e2e`, `gen` (P0-11), `seed` (P0-02), `up` and `down` (P0-04), `guards` (P0-03 scripts locally).
- AGENTS.md outline: TDD rules (the 12 operating rules condensed: spec tests first and locked, remove one marker at a time, never edit an assertion in an existing test, bug fixes start with a test named after the issue); Module boundaries (the four boundary rules, the import-linter contracts, "a new module arrives with tests, fakes and its registry entry"); Where things go (the A2 table); Tests and markers (`req`, `wp`, `integration`, `contract`, `slow`, `spec:` xfail reason, T-IDs); Adapters and fakes (template added in P0-09); Time (`now` and `tz` are arguments, `Clock` in code with I/O); Commands (`make check`, `make test-int`, `make e2e`, `make gen`); Never (edit `frontend/src/api/`, call out from the api process, read another module's tables, use `datetime.now()` in rules, store secrets in env vars other than the file paths in A11).
- CLAUDE.md outline: "Read AGENTS.md first"; run `make check` before every commit; the spec PR and impl PR branch names; how to find a WP (`docs/plan/work-packages.yaml` and `docs/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN-DETAILED.md`); never add the `spec-change` label.
- ADR files follow the architecture doc's template; ADR-0010 and ADR-0011 carry `Status: Proposed` until Scott accepts them.
- Keep module `__init__.py` files empty. A re-export in `__init__` would make `from tumnis.modules.tasks import x` bypass the api-only rule.

**Fixtures, fakes and data**

- `backend/tests/meta/_lint_tree.py`: `make_lint_tree(tmp_path, extra: dict[str, str]) -> Path`.
- No database or network. All tests here are unit tests, but T-P0-01-04 to 08 and 10 spawn subprocesses (allowed under the socket block).

**Risks and fallbacks**

- Wildcards in `source_modules` of a forbidden contract may not be supported by the pinned import-linter. Fallback: generate the 15 explicit `tumnis.modules.<m>.rules` lines with `scripts/new_module.py` (verify against the pinned version).
- import-linter may not treat standard-library modules as external packages, so `os` or `socket` in `rules.py` might slip past it. T-P0-01-09 and the Ruff ban cover that gap.
- mypy strict on `api.py` can be noisy with SQLAlchemy result types. Fallback: keep strict on `core` and `rules`, and relax `api.py` to `disallow_untyped_defs` only, recorded in the ADR log.

```toml
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.3"
testpaths = ["tests", "tumnis"]

  "slow: over 5 seconds",
  "drill: restore drill only, never on PRs",

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["tumnis"]
omit = ["tumnis/modules/*/migrations/*", "tumnis/modules/*/tests/*"]
```

Clock:

```python
# backend/tumnis/core/clock.py
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Protocol

class Clock(Protocol):
    def now(self) -> datetime: ...          # always aware, UTC

class SystemClock:
    def now(self) -> datetime:
        return datetime.now(UTC)

class FixedClock:
    def __init__(self, at: datetime) -> None:
        if at.tzinfo is None:
            raise ValueError("FixedClock needs an aware datetime")
        self._at = at.astimezone(UTC)
    def now(self) -> datetime:
        return self._at
    def advance(self, delta: timedelta | None = None, **kw: float) -> datetime:
        self._at += delta or timedelta(**kw)
        return self._at
    def set(self, at: datetime) -> None:
        self._at = at.astimezone(UTC)
```

Adapter registry (P0-09 adds the base class; this is the switch only):

```python
# backend/tumnis/core/adapters/registry.py
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Literal

AdapterMode = Literal["real", "fake"]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AdapterSpec:
    name: str                                   # "decisions.jev", "calendar.google"
    port: type[Any]                             # the Protocol the adapter implements
    real: Callable[..., Any]
    fake: Callable[..., Any] | None

_REGISTRY: dict[str, AdapterSpec] = {}

def register_adapter(name: str, *, port: type[Any], real: Callable[..., Any],
                     fake: Callable[..., Any] | None) -> None: ...
def resolve(name: str, mode: AdapterMode, **deps: Any) -> Any: ...   # KeyError on unknown name
def validate() -> list[str]:                     # human-readable violations, empty when valid
    """Every spec has a fake; the fake is a class or factory whose product satisfies `port`."""
def registered() -> tuple[AdapterSpec, ...]: ...
```

Database helpers ([testcontainers Postgres module](https://testcontainers-python.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modules/postgres/README.html)):

```python
# backend/tests/_pg.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
import psycopg
from psycopg import sql

OWNER, APP = "tumnis_owner", "tumnis_app"
PASSWORDS = {OWNER: "owner-test", APP: "app-test"}

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DbUrls:
    host: str
    port: int
    name: str
    def url(self, role: str, driver: str = "psycopg") -> str:
        return f"postgresql+{driver}://{role}:{PASSWORDS[role]}@{self.host}:{self.port}/{self.name}"
    @property
    def owner(self) -> str: return self.url(OWNER)
    @property
    def app(self) -> str: return self.url(APP)
    def libpq(self, role: str) -> str:
        return f"postgresql://{role}:{PASSWORDS[role]}@{self.host}:{self.port}/{self.name}"

def bootstrap_roles(superuser_dsn: str) -> None:
    """Run deploy/postgres/initdb/01-roles.sql with test passwords (same file as compose)."""

def build_template(base: DbUrls, template: str) -> None:
    """CREATE DATABASE <template> OWNER tumnis_owner; alembic upgrade heads as owner;
    ALTER DATABASE <template> WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false IS_TEMPLATE true."""

def clone(base: DbUrls, template: str, name: str) -> DbUrls:
    with psycopg.connect(base.libpq(OWNER), autocommit=True) as c:
        c.execute(sql.SQL("CREATE DATABASE {} TEMPLATE {} OWNER {}").format(
            sql.Identifier(name), sql.Identifier(template), sql.Identifier(OWNER)))
    return DbUrls(base.host, base.port, name)

def drop(base: DbUrls, name: str) -> None:
    with psycopg.connect(base.libpq(OWNER), autocommit=True) as c:
        c.execute(sql.SQL("DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS {} WITH (FORCE)").format(sql.Identifier(name)))
```

`MinioContainer.get_config()` and the `wait_for_logs` strings: verify against the pinned testcontainers and image versions ([testcontainers MinIO module](https://testcontainers-python.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modules/minio/README.html)). The clamd fixture is slow to start, so only tests that use it pay for it (session scope, created lazily on first use).

The DBOS fixture follows the [DBOS testing guide](https://docs.dbos.dev/python/tutorials/testing) (`DBOS.destroy`, `DBOS(config=...)`, `DBOS.reset_system_database(truncate=True)`, `DBOS.launch()`); `destroy_registry=False` keeps decorated workflows registered between tests (verify against the pinned version).

`fakes` is a function-scoped handle: `Fakes(mode="fake")` builds every registered adapter's fake once per test and exposes them by name (`fakes["decisions.jev"]`) for scripting and assertions. `recordings(provider)` reads `tumnis/modules/*/tests/recordings/<provider>/*.json`, each file `{"raw": {...}, "expected": [...]}`.

```python
class SeedSink(Protocol):
    async def workspace(self, rec: WorkspaceSeed) -> UUID: ...
    async def user(self, ws: UUID, rec: UserSeed) -> UUID: ...
    async def project(self, ws: UUID, rec: ProjectSeed) -> UUID: ...
    async def task(self, ws: UUID, project: UUID, parent: UUID | None, rec: TaskSeed) -> UUID: ...
    async def event(self, ws: UUID, rec: EventSeed) -> UUID: ...
    async def document(self, ws: UUID, project: UUID | None, rec: DocumentSeed) -> UUID: ...

async def load_seed(path: Path, sink: SeedSink, *, anchor: date, clock: Clock) -> SeedResult: ...
```

**Implementation notes**

- One Postgres container per xdist worker keeps teardown simple; with `-n 4` that is four containers. If CI memory is tight, switch to one shared container using the xdist "run once" pattern with a `filelock` and a JSON handoff file.
- `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE` fails if any session is connected to the template, which is why `build_template` sets `ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false` after migrating.
- The template is migrated by running Alembic in-process as the owner role (`alembic.command.upgrade(cfg, "heads")`, `heads` because every module is its own branch; see P0-06).
- `asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"` keeps async fixtures function-scoped; the session fixtures above are all synchronous on purpose.
- The DBOS system database belongs to the app role and lives beside the app database in the same cluster, so pgBackRest covers it (architecture: DBOS state).
- Vitest config ([Vitest config](https://vitest.dev/config/)):

```ts
// frontend/vitest.config.ts

    include: ['src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}'],
    restoreMocks: true,
    coverage: { provider: 'v8', include: ['src/**'], exclude: ['src/api/**', 'src/test/**'] },
  },
}));
```

```ts

afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers());
afterAll(() => server.close());
```

- Every layer keeps its harness self-tests, so no job ever collects zero tests (pytest exits 5 on an empty collection).

**Risks and fallbacks**

- testcontainers needs Docker on the GitHub runner (present on `ubuntu-latest`). On the homelab runner, run Docker rootless and set `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true` if the reaper cannot start.
- `DBOS.reset_system_database` or `destroy_registry` may differ in the pinned DBOS version. Fallback: drop and recreate the per-worker system database in the fixture.
- Template cloning copies the template's size every test; with pgvector extensions and few rows it stays small. If it grows past 1 s per clone, move per-test isolation to transaction rollback for tests that do not need DBOS or LISTEN.

#### P0-03 · CI pipeline and TDD guards

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M0.1 Harness and walking skeleton (week 1) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P0-02 |
| Unblocks | P0-05 and the merge rules for every later WP |
| Traces | Quality rules 1, 2, 4 |

**Goal.** GitHub Actions runs the architecture's eight jobs plus three guards on every PR, and branch protection requires all of them. The guards make the TDD model mechanical: spec-guard stops a PR from weakening a locked test, red-proof proves a bug-fix test fails on the base commit, and traceability fails when a finished phase has a requirement no passing test names.

**Scope.** In: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/ci/spec_guard.py`, `scripts/ci/ts_tests.mjs`, `scripts/ci/red_proof.py`, `scripts/ci/traceability.py`, `scripts/ci/pytest_trace.py` (collection plugin), `scripts/ci/coverage_gates.py`, `scripts/ci/branch_protection.sh`, `.github/required-checks.txt`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`. Out: the Security job's tool configs (P0-16), the Performance job's real content (P0-29), the Skills job's real content (P1-05), nightly and release workflows (P0-27, P0-30).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | new | 8 jobs + spec-guard, red-proof, traceability |
| `.github/required-checks.txt` | new | One job name per line; the protection script and a meta-test read it |
| `scripts/ci/spec_guard.py` | new | Locked-test diff check |
| `scripts/ci/ts_tests.mjs` | new | Extracts Vitest and Playwright test blocks with the TypeScript compiler API |
| `scripts/ci/red_proof.py` | new | Runs new bug tests against the base commit |
| `scripts/ci/traceability.py` | new | Requirement matrix and gate |
| `scripts/ci/pytest_trace.py` | new | pytest plugin: dumps markers, T-IDs and xfail reasons at collection |
| `scripts/ci/coverage_gates.py` | new | 80% on rules and MCP; 100% on planner, focus, threshold, state-machine rules |
| `scripts/ci/branch_protection.sh` | new | Applies required checks to `main` with `gh api` |
| `backend/tests/ci/test_spec_guard.py`, `test_red_proof.py`, `test_traceability.py`, `test_ci_config.py` | new | Spec tests for the guards |
| `backend/tests/ci/_gitrepo.py` | new | Builds throwaway git repos in `tmp_path` |
| `docs/plan/work-packages.yaml` | edit | Add `status: planned|active|done` to each phase (read by traceability) |

**Interfaces**

spec-guard (Python sketch; the TypeScript side gives the same `TestBlock` map through `ts_tests.mjs`):

```python
# scripts/ci/spec_guard.py
import ast, copy, fnmatch, json, subprocess, sys
from dataclasses import dataclass

TEST_GLOBS = ("**/test_*.py", "**/*_test.py", "frontend/src/**/*.test.ts", "frontend/src/**/*.test.tsx",
              "frontend/e2e/**/*.spec.ts", "profiles/tests/cases/*.yaml")
EXEMPT_GLOBS = ("backend/tests/contract/generated/**", "frontend/src/api/**")
GENERATED_HEADER = ("# @generated", "// @generated")

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Violation:
    path: str
    test: str
    kind: str        # deleted_file | deleted_test | edited_test | added_skip_or_xfail | edited_pytestmark
    detail: str

def is_spec_xfail(dec: ast.expr) -> bool:
    """True for pytest.mark.xfail(..., reason="spec:...") in any import spelling."""
    if not isinstance(dec, ast.Call):
        return False
    name = ast.unparse(dec.func)
    if name not in ("pytest.mark.xfail", "mark.xfail", "xfail"):
        return False
    for kw in dec.keywords:
        if kw.arg == "reason" and isinstance(kw.value, ast.Constant) and str(kw.value.value).startswith("spec:"):
            return True
    return False

def is_weakening_decorator(dec: ast.expr) -> bool:
    name = ast.unparse(dec.func if isinstance(dec, ast.Call) else dec)
    return name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] in ("skip", "skipif", "xfail") and not is_spec_xfail(dec)

def locked_blocks(src: str) -> dict[str, ast.AST]:
    """Test functions and methods, state-machine rules, and any helper whose body asserts."""
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    out: dict[str, ast.AST] = {}
    def visit(node: ast.AST, prefix: str) -> None:
        for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
            if isinstance(child, ast.ClassDef):
                visit(child, f"{prefix}{child.name}.")
            elif isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
                asserts = any(isinstance(n, ast.Assert) or (isinstance(n, ast.Call) and
                              ast.unparse(n.func).endswith("raises")) for n in ast.walk(child))
                if child.name.startswith("test") or asserts or any(
                        ast.unparse(d).split("(")[0].endswith(("rule", "invariant")) for d in child.decorator_list):
                    out[f"{prefix}{child.name}"] = child
    visit(tree, "")
    pm = next((n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.Assign)
               and any(ast.unparse(t) == "pytestmark" for t in n.targets)), None)
    if pm is not None:
        out["<pytestmark>"] = pm
    return out

def normalize(node: ast.AST) -> str:
    """Drop spec xfail decorators (and spec xfail entries in pytestmark), then dump without positions."""
    node = copy.deepcopy(node)
    if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
        node.decorator_list = [d for d in node.decorator_list if not is_spec_xfail(d)]
    if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and isinstance(node.value, (ast.List, ast.Tuple)):
        node.value.elts = [e for e in node.value.elts if not is_spec_xfail(e)]
    return ast.dump(node, annotate_fields=True, include_attributes=False)

def compare_python(path: str, base_src: str, head_src: str) -> list[Violation]:
    base, head = locked_blocks(base_src), locked_blocks(head_src)
    out: list[Violation] = []
    for name, b in base.items():
        h = head.get(name)
        if h is None:
            out.append(Violation(path, name, "deleted_test", "present on base, missing on head"))
            continue
        if isinstance(h, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            added = [d for d in h.decorator_list if is_weakening_decorator(d)
                     and ast.dump(d) not in {ast.dump(x) for x in b.decorator_list}]
            if added:
                out.append(Violation(path, name, "added_skip_or_xfail", ast.unparse(added[0])))
                continue
        if normalize(b) != normalize(h):
            out.append(Violation(path, name, "edited_test", unified_diff(ast.unparse(b), ast.unparse(h))))
    return out

def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    args = parse(argv)                      # --base SHA --head SHA --repo PATH --labels a,b --pr N
    if "spec-change" in args.labels and label_added_by_owner(args.pr, "spec-change"):
        print_report(violations := collect(args), waived=True)
        return 0
    violations = collect(args)              # walks `git diff --name-status -M base...head`
    print_report(violations, waived=False)  # markdown to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    return 1 if violations else 0
```

`collect` rules: status `D` on a test file present at base is `deleted_file`; status `R` compares the old path's blocks against the new path's blocks (a move with no edits passes); status `M` runs `compare_python` or the TypeScript comparison; status `A` is never a violation. A path is skipped when it matches `EXEMPT_GLOBS` or its first line is a generated header. `label_added_by_owner` reads `gh api repos/{repo}/issues/{pr}/events` and accepts the label only when a `labeled` event for it has `actor.login` in `SPEC_CHANGE_ACTORS` (Scott's login, from repo variables).

TypeScript extraction (`scripts/ci/ts_tests.mjs`): parse with `ts.createSourceFile`, walk `CallExpression`s whose callee text is `test`, `it`, `test.fails`, `test.fail`, `test.skip`, `test.only`, `it.fails` or `it.skip` (and nested `describe` titles for the key), and emit `{"<describe> > <title>": {"text": <printed call>, "fails": bool, "skip": bool}}`. Normalization before comparing: `test.fails(` becomes `test(`, and an expression statement `test.fail();` as the first statement of a Playwright body is removed. Adding `.skip` or `.fails` to an existing test is `added_skip_or_xfail`.

red-proof:

```python
# scripts/ci/red_proof.py
ISSUE_TEST = re.compile(r"test_issue_(\d+)_\w+")

def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    args = parse(argv)                          # --base --head --pr --issues 123,124
    new_tests = added_tests(args.base, args.head)   # same extractor as spec-guard, status A or new names in M
    if not new_tests:
        return fail("A `bug` PR must add at least one test.")
    named = [t for t in new_tests if (m := ISSUE_TEST.search(t.name)) and m.group(1) in args.issues]
    if not named:
        return fail("At least one new test must be named test_issue_<n>_... for an issue this PR fixes.")
    with worktree(args.base) as base_dir:           # git worktree add --detach <tmp> <base>
        for path in {t.path for t in new_tests} | changed_conftests(args.base, args.head):
            copy_head_version(path, base_dir)       # tests and conftests only, never source
        results = run_pytest(base_dir, [t.nodeid for t in new_tests],
                             extra=["-p", "no:randomly", "-o", "xfail_strict=false", "--runxfail",
                                    "--junitxml", "red.xml"])
    passing_on_base = [r for r in results if r.outcome == "passed"]
    not_run = [r for r in results if r.outcome in ("error", "skipped")]
    report(results)
    if passing_on_base:
        return fail(f"red-proof failed: {len(passing_on_base)} new test(s) already pass on the base commit")
    if not_run:
        return fail("new test(s) did not run on base (collection error or skip); make them fail on behavior")
    return 0
```

Frontend bug tests use the same flow with `npx vitest run --reporter=json -t "<title>"` in the base worktree.

traceability:

```python
# scripts/ci/traceability.py
PRD_ID = re.compile(r"^(J[1-8]|FR-\d+\.\d+|SEC-\d+|REL-\d+|PERF-\d+|SAF-\d+|SAAS-\d+)$")

@dataclass
class TestRef:
    id: str                 # nodeid or "<file> > <title>"
    reqs: set[str]
    wp: str | None
    expected_failure: bool  # spec xfail, test.fails, test.fail()

def first_phase_by_requirement(plan: dict) -> dict[str, int]:
    out: dict[str, int] = {}
    for phase in plan["phases"]:
        items = phase.get("acceptance", []) + [wp for m in phase["milestones"] for wp in m["wps"]]
        for item in items:
            traces = item["traces"] if isinstance(item["traces"], list) else item["traces"].split(", ")
            for rid in (t.strip() for t in traces):
                if PRD_ID.match(rid):
                    out[rid] = min(out.get(rid, 99), phase["id"])
    return out

def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    plan = yaml.safe_load(Path("docs/plan/work-packages.yaml").read_text())
    known = prd_ids(Path("docs/PRD.md"))            # first column of every requirement table
    first = first_phase_by_requirement(plan)
    done = {p["id"] for p in plan["phases"] if p.get("status") == "done"}
    tests = pytest_refs() + vitest_refs() + playwright_refs()
    unknown = sorted({r for t in tests for r in t.reqs if PRD_ID.match(r) and r not in known})
    by_req: dict[str, list[TestRef]] = defaultdict(list)
    for t in tests:
        for r in t.reqs:
            by_req[r].append(t)
    missing = sorted(r for r, p in first.items() if p in done
                     and not any(not t.expected_failure for t in by_req.get(r, [])))
    write_markdown(first, by_req, missing, unknown)    # PR comment body + traceability.json artifact
    return 1 if (missing or unknown) else 0
```

`pytest_refs()` runs `pytest --collect-only -q -p scripts.ci.pytest_trace` (collection needs no database), and the plugin writes `trace.json` with each item's `req` args, `wp`, first docstring line (T-ID) and whether it carries a spec xfail. `vitest_refs()` scans titles for `[P0-25][FR-3.10]` tags and `test.fails`; `playwright_refs()` uses `npx playwright test --list --reporter=json` and reads `tags`.
