#### P0-19 · Recurrence, rollover and day close

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M0.4 Projects, tasks and search (week 3) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P0-18 |
| Unblocks | none in the YAML (P1-18 close-the-day reads its data) |
| Traces | FR-3.5, FR-3.6, REL-6 |

**Goal.** Recurring tasks produce their next instance exactly once, on done or on due date passed, with correct local times across daylight-saving changes in both hemispheres. Unfinished Today tasks roll back to the pool at local midnight in the workspace timezone with a visible rollover count. The housekeeping workflows (trash purge, idempotency-key expiry) run on schedule and survive a killed worker.

**Scope.** In: `recurrence_rules`, `day_closes`; `tasks/rules_recurrence.py`; REST for a task's recurrence; the scheduled workflows `day_close_tick` (every 5 minutes, also runs the recurrence tick) and `housekeeping` (hourly at :17). Out: close-the-day screen (P1-18), unattended windows (P4), archive compression (P1-15 and P3), backup freshness (P0-28).

**Interfaces**

```python
# tasks/rules_recurrence.py
class Preset(StrEnum):
    DAILY = "daily"; WEEKDAYS = "weekdays"; WEEKLY = "weekly"; MONTHLY = "monthly"

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RecurrenceSpec:
    preset: Preset | None
    cron: str | None               # 5 fields, evaluated in local wall time
    weekday: int | None = None     # 0 = Monday, weekly only
    month_day: int | None = None   # 1..31, monthly only; clamps to the month's last day
    due_time: time = time(9, 0)    # (plan default) matches the FR-4.7 working-hours start

class InvalidRecurrence(ValueError): code = "invalid_recurrence"

def validate_spec(spec: RecurrenceSpec) -> None: ...
# from tumnis.core.clock (R-12), pure, safe to import from rules:
#   def local_to_utc(day: date, local_time: time, tz: ZoneInfo) -> datetime
#   a nonexistent local time (DST gap) shifts forward by the gap length (02:30 on a
#   spring-forward day becomes 03:30 local); an ambiguous one takes the first occurrence (fold=0)
def next_occurrence(spec: RecurrenceSpec, after: datetime, tz: ZoneInfo) -> datetime: ...  # strictly after, UTC

def successor(spec: RecurrenceSpec, latest: datetime, latest_done: bool,
              trigger: Literal["done", "tick"], now: datetime, tz: ZoneInfo) -> datetime | None: ...
    # done: next_occurrence(spec, max(now, latest), tz)
    # tick: next_occurrence(spec, now, tz) if now >= latest and not latest_done else None
    # callers only ask for the latest instance of a rule

def next_day_close(anchor: datetime, tz: ZoneInfo) -> datetime: ...   # first local midnight after anchor, UTC
def day_close_due(anchor: datetime, now: datetime, tz: ZoneInfo) -> date | None: ...
    # the local date to close, or None; anchor = max(last closed_at, timezone changed_at)
```

```python
# tasks/workflows.py (DBOS; schedules applied after launch)
@DBOS.workflow()
async def day_close_tick(scheduled_time: datetime, context: Any) -> None: ...
    # for each workspace (core.tenancy system listing): if day_close_due(...) enqueue close_day on
    # "maintenance" with deduplication_id f"day_close:{ws}:{day}"; then enqueue recurrence_tick(ws)

@DBOS.workflow()
async def close_day(workspace_id: UUID, day: date) -> int: ...     # returns tasks rolled over

@DBOS.step()
async def roll_over_today(workspace_id: UUID, day: date, now: datetime) -> int: ...
    # one transaction: SELECT … WHERE status='today' FOR UPDATE; apply_transition(…, SYSTEM);
    # INSERT INTO day_closes (day, closed_at, rolled_over) ON CONFLICT (workspace_id, day) DO NOTHING

@DBOS.workflow()
async def housekeeping(scheduled_time: datetime, context: Any) -> None: ...
    # steps: purge_trash (deleted_at older than 30 days (plan default)), expire_idempotency_keys;
    # each step deletes in batches of 1,000 (plan default) until empty

# worker.py, after DBOS.launch()
DBOS.apply_schedules([
    {"schedule_name": "day-close-tick", "workflow_fn": day_close_tick, "schedule": "*/5 * * * *"},
    {"schedule_name": "housekeeping", "workflow_fn": housekeeping, "schedule": "17 * * * *"},
])
```

REST: `GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/tasks/{id}/recurrence` (`PUT` body `{preset|cron, weekday?, month_day?, due_time?, version}`; the task becomes the first instance) and `GET /v1/recurrence?project_id=` for the Schedule rail (P0-24).

| Weekly Sun 02:30, gap | America/New_York | 2026-03-01T12:00Z | 2026-03-08T07:30Z | 03:30 EDT |

| Cron `30 2 * * *` | America/New_York | 2026-03-08T06:00Z | 2026-03-08T07:30Z, then 2026-03-09T06:30Z | 03:30 EDT, then 02:30 EDT |

Day-close vectors (anchor → `next_day_close`):

| Zone | Anchor (UTC) | Next close (UTC) | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| America/New_York | 2026-03-08T03:00Z | 2026-03-08T05:00Z | Mar 8 00:00 EST |
| America/New_York | 2026-03-08T05:00Z | 2026-03-09T04:00Z | 23-hour day |
| America/New_York | 2026-11-01T04:30Z | 2026-11-02T05:00Z | 25-hour day |
| Australia/Sydney | 2026-10-03T15:00Z | 2026-10-04T13:00Z | Oct 5 00:00 AEDT |
| Australia/Sydney | 2026-04-04T14:00Z | 2026-04-05T14:00Z | Apr 6 00:00 AEST |
| America/Santiago | 2026-09-05T12:00Z | 2026-09-06T04:00Z | Midnight does not exist; 01:00 -03 |

- **T-P0-19-04.** The NY weekly rule then continues to 2026-11-08T06:30Z (01:30 EST), never 2026-11-01T06:30Z (the second 01:30).
- **T-P0-19-06.** Cron `0 9 * * *` returns the same instants as the daily rows; cron `0 9 * * 1-5` the same as weekdays. Cron is iterated with [croniter](https://github.com/pallets-eco/croniter) on naive local wall time, then `local_to_utc` converts; if the result is not after `after` (overlap edge), iterate again.
- **T-P0-19-08.** Strategy: a weekly spec, a random `tz` from the two zones, a list of 1 to 40 events drawn from `("done", t)` and `("tick", t)` with increasing `t` over 20 weeks from 2026-03-01T00:00Z. A model keeps instances `[(occurrence, done)]`; `done` applies only to the latest instance. Invariants: occurrences strictly increase; each instance has at most one successor; no occurrence appears twice; every successor is after the event time that created it.
- **T-P0-19-09.** Given a weekly Monday rule whose latest instance was due 2026-03-02 and is open. When the first tick after that runs at 2026-03-24T12:00Z. Then exactly one instance is created, due 2026-03-30; nothing for Mar 9, 16 or 23.
- **T-P0-19-10.** Fixtures `dbos`, `workspace`, `clock`. Given the latest instance is overdue. When `change_status(done)` and `recurrence_tick` run concurrently (two tasks with `asyncio.gather`). Then one successor row; the loser hit the unique index and returned without error.
- **T-P0-19-12.** Given anchor 2026-03-07T13:00Z (a Sydney close). When the workspace switches to America/New_York at 2026-03-08T12:00Z (anchor becomes that instant). Then `day_close_due` is None at 12:05Z (no 08:05 local rollover) and the next close is 2026-03-09T04:00Z. The reverse switch (NY to Sydney at the same instant) gives next close 2026-03-08T13:00Z.
- **T-P0-19-13.** Fixtures `dbos`, `workspace`, `clock` (set to 2026-03-09T03:55Z, tz America/New_York, anchor 2026-03-08T05:00Z). Given 3 Today tasks, one with `rollover_count=2`. When the clock passes 04:00Z and `day_close_tick` runs. Then all 3 are `backlog`, counts are 1, 1, 3, one `task.status_changed` per task with `actor=system`, one `day_closes` row for 2026-03-08. A second tick changes nothing.
- **T-P0-19-15.** Fixture `worker_killer` kills the worker inside `roll_over_today` after the UPDATE but before commit; on restart DBOS reruns the step and counts rise once.
- **T-P0-19-16.** Through `PUT /v1/settings/workspace {timezone: "Australia/Sydney"}` then ticks at fixed times; asserts the close happens at Sydney midnight and not at the old New York midnight.

**TDD sequence**

1. Red T-P0-19-07, then 01 and 02. `validate_spec`, `local_to_utc` in `core/clock.py`, preset iteration over local dates. Refactor: one date iterator with a predicate per preset.
2. Red T-P0-19-03, 04, 05. Confirm fold=0 behaviour; clamp month days.
3. Red T-P0-19-06. Cron path with croniter on naive local time.
4. Red T-P0-19-08, 09. `successor`. Refactor: name the two triggers.
5. Red T-P0-19-11, 12. `next_day_close`, `day_close_due`.
6. Red T-P0-19-19. Migration, recurrence routes, template snapshot in `task_template`.
7. Red T-P0-19-10. `create_successor` inserts with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on the occurrence index.
8. Red T-P0-19-13, 14, 16. `day_close_tick` and `close_day`; timezone anchor from the settings row's `updated_at` (P0-08).
9. Red T-P0-19-15. Make `roll_over_today` a single transactional step; verify with the killer.
10. Red T-P0-19-17, 18. `housekeeping` steps.

**Implementation notes**

- `datetime(…, tzinfo=ZoneInfo(...))` defaults to `fold=0`, which gives the pre-transition offset: a nonexistent 02:30 becomes 03:30 after the jump, an ambiguous 01:30 becomes the first one ([zoneinfo docs](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zoneinfo.html), PEP 495). `core.clock.local_to_utc` implements R-12 this way (`datetime.combine(day, local_time, tzinfo=tz)` then `.astimezone(UTC)`), and the vectors pin it: gaps shift forward by their length, overlaps take the first occurrence.
- Never feed aware datetimes to croniter; its DST handling has changed across releases. Naive local in, `local_to_utc` out.
- Schedules use the current DBOS API: define the workflow with `(scheduled_time, context)` and register with `DBOS.apply_schedules` after `DBOS.launch()`; the old `@DBOS.scheduled` decorator is gone ([DBOS scheduled workflows](https://docs.dbos.dev/python/tutorials/scheduled-workflows)). Each firing is exactly once per scheduled time. Verify against the pinned version.
- Day close is local midnight (plan default). Only `today` rolls over; `in_progress`, `waiting_on_human` and `in_review` stay put, because the diagram's rollover edge starts at Today. A missed day (worker down) closes once; `rollover_count` rises by one, not by the number of missed days.
- The timezone anchor stops a mid-day timezone change from rolling Today over in the morning. It needs the timezone setting's change time; if P0-08 does not keep `updated_at` on `workspace_settings` rows, add it there.
- The workspace listing for ticks uses the P0-06 system context (assumed `core.tenancy.all_workspace_ids()`); each child workflow then enters that workspace's context.
- Successor instances copy `task_template` (title, label, estimate, first action, acceptance criteria, priority, project) and set `due_on` to the occurrence's local date, `source='recurrence'`, status `backlog`.
- Trash purge hard-deletes tasks with `deleted_at` older than 30 days (plan default) and their comments and links through `ON DELETE CASCADE`.

- `clock` fixture (A5) plus a `tz_workspace(tz)` helper that sets the workspace timezone setting.
- Seed: one weekly recurring task in the seed set (Friday invoice run) so previews show the Schedule rail.

**Risks and fallbacks**

- croniter behaviour changes: the cron path is small and pinned by vectors. Fallback: `cronsim`, which iterates local wall time too.
- `apply_schedules` differs in the pinned DBOS version: fall back to the decorator form the version supports; the tests do not depend on how the schedule is registered, only on the workflows.

#### P0-20 · Search

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M0.4 Projects, tasks and search (week 3) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P0-18 |
| Unblocks | P0-25 |
| Traces | FR-3.9 |

**Goal.** One Postgres full-text index serves global search, the project typeahead and the task typeahead, ranked by text match, recency and project match. The index is fed only by events, so `search` imports no other module and a failing subscriber cannot break task writes.

**Scope.** In: `search_index` with a stored generated `tsvector` and GIN index; subscribers for task and project events; query parsing (phrases, prefix); `GET /v1/search`, `GET /v1/typeahead/projects`, `GET /v1/typeahead/tasks`. Out: the MCP `search` tool (P2-01), results and linked email and note excerpts (indexed by the WPs that create them: P2-04, P3-03), knowledge chunks (P1-17), semantic search (P3-10).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/search/{models,rules,api,router,events}.py` | new | Module per A2 |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/search/migrations/0001_search_index.py` | new | Table, generated column, GIN, RLS |
| `backend/fixtures/search/corpus.yaml` | new | Ranking corpus with expected orders |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/search/tests/unit/test_parse.py` | new | Query parsing |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/search/tests/integration/test_index_events.py`, `test_ranking.py`, `test_typeahead.py` | new | Behaviour |

**Interfaces**

```sql
CREATE TABLE search_index (
  -- P0-06 base columns
  entity_type text NOT NULL CHECK (entity_type IN ('task', 'project')),
  entity_id   uuid NOT NULL,
  project_id  uuid,
  title       text NOT NULL,
  body        text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  source_updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL,         -- recency input; the base updated_at is row maintenance
  tsv tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        setweight(to_tsvector('english', title), 'A') ||
        setweight(to_tsvector('simple',  title), 'B') ||
        setweight(to_tsvector('english', body),  'C') ||
        setweight(to_tsvector('simple',  body),  'D')) STORED
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_search_ws_entity ON search_index (workspace_id, entity_type, entity_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_search_tsv ON search_index USING gin (tsv);
```

```python
# search/rules.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ParsedQuery:
    phrases: tuple[str, ...]      # from "double quotes"
    terms: tuple[str, ...]        # complete words, english config
    prefix: str | None            # last unquoted token when the query does not end in a space

MAX_TERMS: Final = 8              # (plan default)
PROJECT_BOOST: Final = 2.0        # (plan default)
RECENCY_DAYS: Final = 14.0        # (plan default) score / (1 + age_days / 14)

def parse_query(q: str) -> ParsedQuery: ...   # strips tsquery operators & | ! ( ) : * < > ' \
def tsquery_parts(p: ParsedQuery) -> list[tuple[str, str]]: ...  # (sql_fn, arg) pairs ANDed with &&

# search/api.py
class SearchHit(BaseModel):
    entity_type: Literal["task", "project"]; entity_id: UUID; project_id: UUID | None
    title: str; snippet: str; score: float
async def search(s: AsyncSession, q: str, *, scope: Literal["all", "tasks", "projects"] = "all",
                 project_id: UUID | None = None, cursor: str | None = None, limit: int = 20,
                 now: datetime) -> Page[SearchHit]: ...
async def typeahead_projects(s, q: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[SearchHit]: ...
async def typeahead_tasks(s, q: str, project_id: UUID | None, limit: int = 8) -> list[SearchHit]: ...
```

Ranking SQL (one statement; `:now` is frozen in the cursor so page 2 ranks like page 1):

```sql
WITH q AS (SELECT phraseto_tsquery('english', :p0) && plainto_tsquery('english', :terms)
                  && to_tsquery('simple', :prefix || ':*') AS query)
SELECT entity_type, entity_id, project_id, title,
       ts_headline('english', body, q.query, 'MaxFragments=1,MaxWords=12') AS snippet,
       ts_rank_cd(tsv, q.query)
         * CASE WHEN project_id = :project_id THEN :boost ELSE 1.0 END
         / (1 + extract(epoch FROM (:now - source_updated_at)) / 86400.0 / :recency_days) AS score
FROM search_index, q
WHERE tsv @@ q.query AND deleted_at IS NULL
ORDER BY score DESC, entity_id
LIMIT :limit;
```

The query builder only emits the parts that exist (no phrase, no prefix, and so on). Subscribers: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.status_changed`, `project.created`, `project.updated`, `project.archived`.

**Implementation notes**

- `to_tsvector(regconfig, text)` with a literal config is immutable, so it is allowed in a stored generated column ([text search controls](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/textsearch-controls.html)).
- Two configs: `english` stems full words ("invoices" matches "invoice"); `simple` keeps raw lexemes so a prefix like `runn:*` matches "running", which stems to `run` under `english`. Concatenating the vectors offsets positions, so phrase adjacency still works within each half.
- Never interpolate user text into `to_tsquery`; always bind it, and only after `parse_query` removed operators. `plainto_tsquery` and `phraseto_tsquery` accept raw text safely.
- Payloads carry the text (`doc` on task events, `name` and `goal` on project events), because `search` may not call other modules. Cap `body` at 8 KB (plan default).
- `ts_headline` is costly; it runs only on the `LIMIT` rows because it sits in the select list of the limited query.
- Hosted mode with many workspaces may want `btree_gin` and a composite `(workspace_id, tsv)` GIN index; not needed for one workspace. The table-registry rule on `workspace_id` first applies to btree composites.

| Field | Value |

**Goal.** Per-workspace usage counters rise exactly once per event, even when the relay delivers an event twice, so hosted metering has trustworthy numbers from day one.

**Scope.** In: `usage_counters`, `usage_ledger`, a counter map from event names to counters, one subscriber, `usage.api.report`, `GET /v1/usage`. Out: billing (non-goal), the `/metrics` export (P0-27), counters for later events (each emitting WP adds its line to the map).

| Path | Change | Purpose |

| `backend/tumnis/modules/usage/{models,rules,api,router,events}.py` | new | Module |

**Interfaces**

```python
# usage/rules.py
CounterFn = Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], int]
COUNTERS: Final[Mapping[str, tuple[tuple[str, CounterFn], ...]]] = MappingProxyType({
    "task.created":    (("tasks_created", lambda p: 1),),
    "project.created": (("projects_created", lambda p: 1),),
    # added by later WPs: run.finished -> runs, run_minutes (ceil(duration_s / 60));
    # decision.made -> decisions; items.ingested -> ingested_items (len(item_ids))
})
def increments(event_name: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[tuple[str, int]]: ...
def usage_day(occurred_at: datetime) -> date: ...    # UTC date (plan default)

# usage/api.py
class UsageRow(BaseModel): day: date; counter: str; value: int
async def record(s: AsyncSession, env: EventEnvelope) -> int: ...   # rows incremented; 0 on replay
async def report(s: AsyncSession, day_from: date, day_to: date) -> list[UsageRow]: ...
```

```sql
-- usage_ledger: one row per (event, counter); the guard against double delivery
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_usage_ledger ON usage_ledger (workspace_id, event_id, counter);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_usage_counters ON usage_counters (workspace_id, day, counter);
-- record(), one transaction:
WITH ins AS (
  INSERT INTO usage_ledger (workspace_id, event_id, counter, day, amount)
  VALUES (:ws, :event_id, :counter, :day, :amount)
  ON CONFLICT (workspace_id, event_id, counter) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING day, counter, amount)
INSERT INTO usage_counters (workspace_id, day, counter, value)
SELECT :ws, day, counter, amount FROM ins
ON CONFLICT (workspace_id, day, counter)
DO UPDATE SET value = usage_counters.value + EXCLUDED.value, version = usage_counters.version + 1;
```

**Implementation notes**

- DBOS deduplication (`event_id:subscriber`) already stops most doubles; the ledger covers the rest (a manual dead-letter retry after a success, a relay replay after the dedup window). Both layers are cheap.
- Keep the ledger for 400 days (plan default) and purge in `housekeeping` (P0-19) in a later WP; noted, not built here.
- Storage metering (bytes) waits for `document.added` to carry a size (P1-16).

### M0.5 · Web app (weeks 3 to 4)

The phone is a test viewport from the first screen, so every component test runs at 375 px as well as 1280 px. Order of work: P0-22 first; then P0-23, P0-24 and P0-26 in parallel; P0-25 last.

#### P0-22 · Frontend shell and data layer

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M0.5 Web app (weeks 3 to 4) |
| Size | L (3 to 4 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl + impl-2 |
| Needs | P0-11 |
| Unblocks | P0-23, P0-24, P0-26 |
| Traces | ADR-0003, ADR-0004, FR-7.1, PERF-2, UX 11 |

**Goal.** An installable PWA shell, served by the api, with typed routes whose search params can never be invalid, one write path that always carries an idempotency key and a version, optimistic updates that roll back on 409, and live invalidation over `/ws`. Every later screen plugs into this without inventing its own data plumbing.

**Scope.** In: Vite, React, TypeScript; TanStack Router (file routes) and Query; the generated client, Query options and zod schemas (openapi-ts, P0-11); `lib/fetch.ts`, `lib/ws.ts`, `lib/live-map.ts`; the XState Store `uiStore`; the app shell (nav, skip link, bottom bar on the phone); service worker; styling system; backend ETag middleware, `/ws` endpoint and SPA serving; the bundle budget script. Out: screens (P0-23 to P0-26), offline queue (P0-25), push (P4-05).

Router context and routes ([search params guide](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/search-params)). With Zod 4 the schema goes straight into `validateSearch` and `.catch()` supplies the fallback; the `@tanstack/zod-adapter` `fallback()` helper is only for Zod 3.

The write path. Reads use the generated Query options; every write goes through `apiWrite`, and an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule bans importing generated write functions from `src/api` anywhere else.

```ts
// lib/fetch.ts
export const CSRF_COOKIE = '__Host-tumnis_csrf'   // R-18; set by P0-13, readable by JS, sent back as X-CSRF-Token
type Base<TOut> = { method: 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE'; path: string
                    body?: Record<string, unknown>; idempotencyKey: string; schema?: z.ZodType<TOut> }
export type WriteRequest<TOut> =
  | (Base<TOut> & { kind: 'create' })
  | (Base<TOut> & { kind: 'update'; version: number })     // updates cannot compile without a version

export class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(public status: number, public problem: Problem) { super(problem.title) }
}
export class ConflictError<T = unknown> extends ApiError {
  get current(): T { return this.problem.current as T }     // server's row (REL-2)
}

export async function apiWrite<TOut>(req: WriteRequest<TOut>): Promise<TOut> {
  const headers = new Headers({ 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json' })
  headers.set('Idempotency-Key', req.idempotencyKey)
  const csrf = readCookie(CSRF_COOKIE)
  if (csrf) headers.set('X-CSRF-Token', csrf)
  const body = req.kind === 'update' ? { ...req.body, version: req.version } : req.body
  const res = await fetch(`/v1${req.path}`, {
    method: req.method, headers, credentials: 'same-origin',
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
  })
  if (res.status === 409) throw new ConflictError(409, await readProblem(res))
  if (res.status === 401) { onUnauthorized(); throw new ApiError(401, await readProblem(res)) }
  if (!res.ok) throw new ApiError(res.status, await readProblem(res))
  const json = res.status === 204 ? undefined : await res.json()
  return req.schema ? req.schema.parse(json) : (json as TOut)
}

// One idempotency key per logical write: stamped before mutate, so Query retries reuse it.
export function useWrite<TVars extends { idempotencyKey?: string }, TOut, TSnap>(
  opts: UseMutationOptions<TOut, Error, TVars & { idempotencyKey: string }, TSnap>,
) {
  const m = useMutation(opts)
  return {
    ...m,
    mutate: (v: TVars) => m.mutate({ ...v, idempotencyKey: v.idempotencyKey ?? crypto.randomUUID() }),
  }
}
```

Optimistic update with rollback ([optimistic updates](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/optimistic-updates); recent v5 passes a `context` with `client` to every callback, verify against the pinned version):

```ts
export function useUpdateTask() {
  return useWrite({
    mutationFn: (v: UpdateTaskVars & { idempotencyKey: string }) =>
      apiWrite({ kind: 'update', method: 'PATCH', path: `/tasks/${v.id}`, body: v.patch,
                 version: v.version, idempotencyKey: v.idempotencyKey, schema: zTaskOut }),
    onMutate: async (v, ctx) => {
      const key = tasksGetTaskQueryKey({ path: { id: v.id } })
      await ctx.client.cancelQueries({ queryKey: key })
      const previous = ctx.client.getQueryData<TaskOut>(key)
      ctx.client.setQueryData<TaskOut>(key, (old) => (old ? { ...old, ...v.patch } : old))
      return { key, previous }
    },
    onError: (err, _v, snap, ctx) => {
      if (!snap) return
      if (err instanceof ConflictError) {
        ctx.client.setQueryData(snap.key, err.current)   // show the server's record, not ours
        uiStore.trigger.showConflict({ entity: 'task' })
      } else {
        ctx.client.setQueryData(snap.key, snap.previous)
      }
    },
    onSettled: (_d, _e, v, _s, ctx) =>
      ctx.client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: tasksGetTaskQueryKey({ path: { id: v.id } }) }),
  })
}
```

Live invalidation. Generated query keys look like `[{ _id: 'tasksGetTask', baseUrl, path: { id }, query }]` ([Hey API TanStack Query plugin](https://heyapi.dev/openapi-ts/plugins/tanstack-query)). OpenAPI operation IDs stay `<tag>_<function>` (P0-11, R-19), so `tasks_get_task` is generated as `tasksGetTask`; the names below follow that rule and T-P0-22-11 fails if any does not exist in `src/api`.

```ts
// lib/live-map.ts
export type LiveEntity = 'task' | 'project' | 'review_item' | 'settings' | 'api_key' | 'dead_letter'
export const LIVE_MAP: Record<LiveEntity, { details: string[]; lists: string[] }> = {
  task:        { details: ['tasksGetTask'],
                 lists: ['tasksListTasks', 'tasksGetBoard', 'projectsListProjects', 'searchSearch', 'searchTypeaheadTasks'] },
  project:     { details: ['projectsGetProject'], lists: ['projectsListProjects', 'searchTypeaheadProjects'] },
  review_item: { details: [], lists: ['tasksGetReviewCount'] },          // R-05 entity name
  settings:    { details: ['settingsGetWorkspace'], lists: [] },
  api_key:     { details: [], lists: ['authListKeys'] },
  dead_letter: { details: [], lists: ['coreListDeadLetters'] },
}
export const NOT_LIVE = ['healthLive', 'healthReady', 'auditListAudit', 'usageGetUsage', 'tasksListReviewKinds'] as const

// lib/ws.ts
export type LiveMessage = { entity: LiveEntity; id: string }
export function matchesLive(queryKey: readonly unknown[], msg: LiveMessage): boolean {
  const head = queryKey[0] as { _id?: string; path?: Record<string, unknown> } | undefined
  if (!head?._id) return false
  const m = LIVE_MAP[msg.entity]
  if (m.lists.includes(head._id)) return true
  return m.details.includes(head._id) && Object.values(head.path ?? {}).includes(msg.id)
}
export function connectLive(qc: QueryClient, url = liveUrl()): () => void {
  let ws: WebSocket | undefined, attempt = 0, stopped = false, timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>
  const open = () => {
    ws = new WebSocket(url)
    ws.onopen = () => { if (attempt > 0) void qc.invalidateQueries(); attempt = 0 }   // catch up after a drop
    ws.onmessage = (e) => {
      const msg = parseLiveMessage(e.data)          // zod; unknown shapes ignored
      if (msg) void qc.invalidateQueries({ predicate: (q) => matchesLive(q.queryKey, msg) })
    }
    ws.onclose = () => {
      if (stopped) return
      const delay = Math.min(30_000, 500 * 2 ** attempt++) * (0.5 + Math.random() / 2)
      timer = setTimeout(open, delay)
    }
  }
  open()
  return () => { stopped = true; clearTimeout(timer); ws?.close() }
}
```

Backend pieces:

```python
# core/etag.py: pure ASGI middleware for GET and HEAD with a 200 JSON body
def strong_etag(body: bytes) -> str: return '"' + hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()[:32] + '"'
# If-None-Match equal (weak comparison, list of tags, or "*") -> 304 with ETag, no body.
# Cache-Control: private, no-cache on /v1 so the browser revalidates and gets 304s.

# core/live.py
LIVE_CHANNEL: Final = "tumnis_live"
def mark_changed(session: AsyncSession, entity: str, id: UUID) -> None: ...   # after_flush collects models with __live_entity__
async def emit_marked(session: AsyncSession) -> None: ...   # called by core.db.transaction() just before COMMIT:
    # SELECT pg_notify('tumnis_live', '{"ws": "...", "entity": "task", "id": "..."}') per changed row
class LiveHub:                                   # one per api process
    async def start(self, direct_dsn: str) -> None: ...   # asyncpg connection, add_listener(LIVE_CHANNEL, cb)
    def subscribe(self, workspace_id: UUID) -> asyncio.Queue[LiveMessage]: ...
    def unsubscribe(self, workspace_id: UUID, q: asyncio.Queue[LiveMessage]) -> None: ...

@router.websocket("/ws")
async def live_socket(ws: WebSocket) -> None: ...
    # 1. Origin must equal the configured app origin, else close(1008)
    # 2. session cookie -> auth.api.authenticate_session, else close(1008)
    # 3. accept; forward {entity, id} for this workspace only; ping every 25 s (plan default)
```

9. Red T-P0-22-13, 14. `core/live.py`, hub, socket endpoint.
10. Red T-P0-22-17. Shell, skip link, nav, styling tokens; service worker last (it can mask stale bundles while developing).

**Implementation notes**

- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 with Radix primitives (plan default for architecture open question 2; Scott confirms in week 1). Tokens in CSS variables so dark mode and the Tauri client share them. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` in every transition.
- File routes come from `@tanstack/router-plugin/vite` with `autoCodeSplitting: true`, so each route's component is its own chunk and the entry stays small.
- `queryClient` defaults: `staleTime: 5 * 60_000` (plan default; the socket, not a timer, marks data stale), `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, `retry` 1 for queries.
- The openapi-ts config: `input: '../schemas/openapi.json'`, `output: 'src/api'`, plugins `@hey-api/client-fetch`, `zod`, `@tanstack/react-query`. Configure the client once with `credentials: 'same-origin'` and a response interceptor that routes 401 to `/login` ([client docs](https://heyapi.dev/openapi-ts/clients/fetch), verify against the pinned version).
- `apiWrite` owns writes so the version rule is enforced by the type system; generated write functions stay available only to `lib/fetch.ts` and tests.
- The live socket is a notification channel only: `{entity, id}`, never data, so RLS keeps guarding every byte through the refetch. Check `Origin` because browsers send cookies on cross-site WebSocket handshakes.
- `pg_notify` payloads must stay under 8,000 bytes; ours are about 120. NOTIFY is delivered at commit, and PgBouncer transaction mode is fine for NOTIFY; LISTEN needs the direct URL (`DATABASE_DIRECT_URL`), as in the architecture's deployment table ([asyncpg `add_listener`](https://magicstack.github.io/asyncpg/current/api/index.html#asyncpg.connection.Connection.add_listener)).
- Service worker via [vite-plugin-pwa](https://vite-pwa-org.netlify.app/guide/) `generateSW`: precache the shell and assets; `navigateFallback: '/index.html'`; `navigateFallbackDenylist: [/^\/v1\//, /^\/ws/, /^\/mcp/, /^\/health/, /^\/metrics/]`; no runtime caching of `/v1`. `registerType: 'autoUpdate'`.
- ETags are a body hash, which covers the row `version` the architecture names and also lists. The body is still built; the saving is bytes on the phone link, which is where the cold-open target lives.

**Fixtures, fakes and data**

- `src/test/render.tsx`: `renderWithProviders(ui, { route, queryClient, viewport })`; `viewport: 'phone' | 'laptop'` sets `window.innerWidth` and a `matchMedia` mock so layout branches render (jsdom has no layout).
- `src/test/factories.ts`: `makeTask`, `makeProject`, `makeProblem`, built from generated zod schemas with sensible defaults.
- `src/test/msw/handlers.ts`: default handlers for every GET used by the shell (`projectsListProjects`, `tasksListTasks`, `tasksGetReviewCount`, `tasksListReviewKinds`, auth session probe); tests override with `server.use(...)` ([MSW `http` API](https://mswjs.io/docs/api/http)).

**Risks and fallbacks**

- TanStack Query callback signatures shifted within v5 (the `context` argument). If the pinned version lacks it, use `useQueryClient()` in the hook; the tests do not change.
- The bundle budget fails once Radix and zod land: generated zod schemas are the usual culprit. Fallback: import per-schema modules, and validate responses only in dev and test builds.
- WebSocket through Coolify's proxy drops idle connections: the 25 s ping keeps it alive; reconnect plus full invalidation covers the rest.

```ts
// components/project/grouping.ts
export type Group = 'today' | 'up_next' | 'waiting_on_you' | 'waiting_on_agent' | 'done_recently'
export const DONE_RECENT_DAYS = 7                          // (plan default)
export function groupOf(t: TaskLite, now: Date, tz: string): Group | null {
  switch (t.status) {
    case 'waiting_on_human': case 'in_review': return 'waiting_on_you'
    case 'in_progress': return t.label === 'ai' ? 'waiting_on_agent' : 'today'
    case 'today': return 'today'
    case 'backlog': return 'up_next'
    case 'done': return localDaysBetween(t.completed_at!, now, tz) < DONE_RECENT_DAYS ? 'done_recently' : null
  }
}
export function groupTasks(tasks: TaskLite[], now: Date, tz: string): Record<Group, TaskLite[]>

// components/project/sorting.ts: FR-3.7 plain list
export function sortByDue(a: TaskLite, b: TaskLite): number   // due asc, no due last, then priority desc, then title

// components/board/move.ts: one write per drag
export type MovePlan = { taskId: string; columnId: string; boardRank: string; version: number }
export function planMove(board: BoardOut, taskId: string, toColumnId: string, toIndex: number): MovePlan {
  const target = board.columns.find((c) => c.id === toColumnId)!.cards.filter((c) => c.task_id !== taskId)
  const before = target[toIndex - 1]?.board_rank ?? null
  const after = target[toIndex]?.board_rank ?? null
  return { taskId, columnId: toColumnId, boardRank: between(before, after), version: versionOf(board, taskId) }
}
```

Board drag with the current dnd-kit React package ([multiple sortable lists](https://dndkit.com/react/guides/multiple-sortable-lists), [`useSortable`](https://dndkit.com/react/hooks/use-sortable); keyboard and pointer sensors are defaults, verify against the pinned version):

```tsx
function BoardCard({ card, index, columnId }: CardProps) {
  const { ref, isDragging } = useSortable({ id: card.task_id, index, group: columnId, type: 'card', accept: 'card' })
  return <article ref={ref} data-dragging={isDragging} tabIndex={0} aria-roledescription="draggable task">…</article>
}

<DragDropProvider
  onDragEnd={(event) => {
    const { source } = event.operation
    if (event.canceled || !isSortable(source)) return
    const plan = planMove(board, String(source.id), String(source.group), source.index)
    moveTask.mutate(plan)            // one POST /v1/tasks/{id}/move through apiWrite, optimistic
  }}
>
```

Undo:

Every task write (`create_task`, `update_task`, `change_status`, `move_task`, trash) writes one `task_changes` row in the same transaction and returns its id as `change_id` on `TaskOut` (R-09). AI changes (P1-07, P1-08) write rows the same way and are undone through the same route.

```ts
// lib/undo.ts: the session's list of change ids, in memory only; the before-state lives on the server
export type UndoEntry = { changeId: string; label: string; taskId: string; afterVersion: number; at: number }
export const undoStore = createStore({
  context: { entries: [] as UndoEntry[] },
  on: {
    push: (c, e: { entry: UndoEntry }) => ({ entries: [...c.entries, e.entry].slice(-50) }),   // (plan default) 50
    drop: (c, e: { changeId: string }) => ({ entries: c.entries.filter((x) => x.changeId !== e.changeId) }),
  },
})
export async function undo(entry: UndoEntry): Promise<void>   // POST /v1/tasks/{taskId}/undo {change_id, version: afterVersion}
```

```python
# tasks/rules.py
UNDO_FIELDS: Final = frozenset({"status", "column_id", "board_rank", "title", "label", "priority",
    "due_on", "estimate_minutes", "first_action", "acceptance_criteria", "parent_id", "deleted"})
    # never: rollover_count, started_at, completed_at, actual_minutes (derived or history)

# tasks/models.py: task_changes (P0-06 base columns plus)
#   task_id uuid, change_id uuid (unique per workspace), actor text, before jsonb, after jsonb, undone_at timestamptz
#   before/after hold only UNDO_FIELDS that the write changed

# tasks/api.py
async def record_change(s: AsyncSession, actor: Actor, task_id: UUID,
                        before: Mapping[str, Any], after: Mapping[str, Any]) -> UUID: ...   # called by every task write
async def undo_task(s: AsyncSession, actor: Actor, task_id: UUID, change_id: UUID, version: int) -> TaskOut: ...
    # session (human) only; the change must belong to the task and not be undone yet (409 already_undone);
    # version must equal the current row, else 409 stale_version "changed since";
    # applies the change's `before` without the transition table; recomputes completed_at for the restored status;
    # marks undone_at, records the undo as its own change row; emits task.updated and, when status changes,
    # task.status_changed with via="undo"
```

**Implementation notes**

- A drag sends one move request, `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/move {column_id, board_rank, version}` (R-20), which lets the server run the transition check when the column's status differs. T-P0-24-04 pins exactly one request per drag.
- Undo is server-side (R-09) because many inverse moves are not legal transitions (done back to in progress) and because AI changes must be undoable from any device. It is session-only, guarded by the version and the change id, and cannot touch history fields, so the P0-18 invariant "rollover count never falls" still holds. It is not an audit event (SEC-3 does not list task edits).
- Delete means trash (`deleted_at`); agents never hard-delete (UX 9). Undo of delete clears `deleted_at`.
- The composer and every task mutation call `uiStore`-free hooks; view state lives in the URL (`view`, `task`), device state in `uiStore` (last view, rail section), server data in Query. Nothing is stored twice (architecture Frontend).
- Nested subtasks come from the server board layout (`GET /v1/projects/{id}/board`), so the board and the backend rule never disagree.
- Keyboard: `j`/`k` move focus in the Tasks view, `Enter` opens the drawer, `s` starts, `d` marks done, shortcut hints shown in tooltips (UX 7) (plan default key choices).
- Touch drag uses a 250 ms press delay (plan default) so scrolling the board on the phone does not start drags.

**Fixtures, fakes and data**

- MSW handlers for `tasksGetBoard`, `tasksListTasks?project_id=`, `tasksListRecurrence`, `tasksUndoTask`, `tasksMoveTask` (with a mode that answers 409). Names follow R-19.
- `makeBoard({ columns, cards })` factory producing ranks with `n_keys` semantics from `lib/rank.ts`.
- Seed has a Hybrid parent with one card subtask and one nested subtask (P0-18) for the board screenshot.

#### P0-25 · Quick-add and offline queue

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M0.5 Web app (weeks 3 to 4) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P0-24, P0-20 |
| Unblocks | P0-29, P1-07 |
| Traces | FR-3.3, FR-3.9, FR-3.10, J2 |

**Goal.** Capture takes under 3 seconds from any screen and never loses or duplicates a task: `/` opens quick-add, the project comes from a typeahead (defaulting to the current project), and every save goes through one offline queue that persists to IndexedDB and replays with its idempotency key. A keystroke opens global search anywhere.

**Scope.** In: `QuickAddDialog`, `ProjectTypeahead`, `SearchPalette`, the `offlineQueue` machine, `lib/idb.ts`, pending marks, replay on reconnect and on app open; the composer switches to the queue. Out: Jev labels and streamed enrichment (P1-07, P1-08), desktop hotkey (v1.1), Background Sync (Safari lacks it; replay on open covers it).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frontend/src/machines/offlineQueue.ts`, `offlineQueue.test.ts` | new | Machine and tests |
| `frontend/src/lib/idb.ts` | new | `idb` wrapper; in-memory fallback |
| `frontend/src/lib/queueSender.ts` | new | `sendQueued(item)` mapping HTTP outcomes; Web Locks |
| `frontend/src/components/quickadd/{QuickAddDialog,ProjectTypeahead,QuickAddHost,PendingMark}.tsx` | new | UI |

**Interfaces**

```ts
// machines/offlineQueue.ts (XState v5: https://stately.ai/docs/setup, https://stately.ai/docs/promise-actors)
export type QueueItem = { idempotencyKey: string; kind: 'create_task'; body: TaskCreate
                          createdAt: number; attempts: number; problem?: Problem }
export type SendResult = { outcome: 'ok'; taskId: string } | { outcome: 'conflict'; problem: Problem }
                       | { outcome: 'retry'; problem?: Problem }
type Ctx = { items: QueueItem[]; online: boolean }
type Ev =
  | { type: 'ENQUEUE'; item: QueueItem } | { type: 'ONLINE' } | { type: 'OFFLINE' }
  | { type: 'RETRY' } | { type: 'DISCARD' } | { type: 'EDIT'; body: TaskCreate }

export const offlineQueueMachine = setup({
  types: { context: {} as Ctx, events: {} as Ev, input: {} as { online: boolean } },
  actors: {
    loadItems: fromPromise<QueueItem[]>(() => idbQueue.all()),
    sendHead: fromPromise<SendResult, QueueItem>(({ input }) => sendQueued(input)),
  },
  actions: {
    append: assign({ items: ({ context, event }) =>
      event.type === 'ENQUEUE' ? [...context.items, event.item] : context.items }),
    persistNew: (_, params: { item: QueueItem }) => { void idbQueue.put(params.item) },
    setItems: assign({ items: (_, params: { items: QueueItem[] }) => params.items }),
    markOnline: assign({ online: true }),
    markOffline: assign({ online: false }),
    dropHead: assign({ items: ({ context }) => context.items.slice(1) }),
    forgetHead: ({ context }) => { void idbQueue.delete(context.items[0].idempotencyKey) },
    bumpAttempts: assign({ items: ({ context }) =>
      [{ ...context.items[0], attempts: context.items[0].attempts + 1 }, ...context.items.slice(1)] }),
    recordProblem: assign({ items: ({ context }, params: { problem: Problem }) =>
      [{ ...context.items[0], problem: params.problem }, ...context.items.slice(1)] }),
    resetHead: assign({ items: ({ context }) =>
      [{ ...context.items[0], attempts: 0, problem: undefined }, ...context.items.slice(1)] }),
    // EDIT: a new body needs a new idempotency key (the server rejects the old key with a new body)
    replaceHeadWithNewKey: enqueueActions(({ context, event, enqueue }) => {
      if (event.type !== 'EDIT') return
      const old = context.items[0]
      const next: QueueItem = { ...old, body: event.body, idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID(),
                                attempts: 0, problem: undefined }
      enqueue.assign({ items: [next, ...context.items.slice(1)] })
      enqueue(() => { void idbQueue.delete(old.idempotencyKey).then(() => idbQueue.put(next)) })
    }),
    announceSynced: () => {},        // provided by the host: toast + invalidate task lists
  },
  guards: {
    hasItems: ({ context }) => context.items.length > 0,
    isOnline: ({ context }) => context.online,
    sentOk: (_, params: { result: SendResult }) => params.result.outcome === 'ok',
    sentConflict: (_, params: { result: SendResult }) => params.result.outcome === 'conflict',
  },
  delays: {
    backoff: ({ context }) => {
      const n = context.items[0]?.attempts ?? 0
      return n === 0 ? 0 : Math.min(30_000, 1_000 * 2 ** n)   // (plan default) cap 30 s
    },
  },
}).createMachine({
  id: 'offlineQueue',
  context: ({ input }) => ({ items: [], online: input.online }),
  on: {
    ENQUEUE: { actions: ['append', { type: 'persistNew', params: ({ event }) => ({ item: event.item }) }] },
    ONLINE: { actions: 'markOnline' },
    OFFLINE: { actions: 'markOffline' },
  },
  initial: 'loading',
  states: {
    loading: {
      invoke: { src: 'loadItems',
        onDone: { target: 'routing', actions: { type: 'setItems', params: ({ event }) => ({ items: event.output }) } },
        onError: 'idle' },                           // IndexedDB unavailable: run in memory
    },
    routing: { always: [{ guard: 'hasItems', target: 'queued' }, { target: 'idle' }] },
    idle: { on: { ENQUEUE: { target: 'queued', actions: ['append',
      { type: 'persistNew', params: ({ event }) => ({ item: event.item }) }] } } },
    queued: {
      on: { ONLINE: { target: 'syncing', actions: 'markOnline' } },
      after: { backoff: { guard: 'isOnline', target: 'syncing' } },
    },
    syncing: {
      invoke: {
        src: 'sendHead', input: ({ context }) => context.items[0],
        onDone: [
          { guard: { type: 'sentOk', params: ({ event }) => ({ result: event.output }) },
            target: 'afterSend', actions: ['forgetHead', 'dropHead'] },
          { guard: { type: 'sentConflict', params: ({ event }) => ({ result: event.output }) },
            target: 'conflict',
            actions: { type: 'recordProblem', params: ({ event }) =>
              ({ problem: (event.output as { problem: Problem }).problem }) } },
          { target: 'queued', actions: 'bumpAttempts' },
        ],
        onError: { target: 'queued', actions: 'bumpAttempts' },     // network failure or VPN down
      },
    },
    afterSend: { always: [{ guard: 'hasItems', target: 'syncing' }, { target: 'done' }] },
    done: {
      entry: 'announceSynced',
      on: { ENQUEUE: { target: 'queued', actions: ['append',
        { type: 'persistNew', params: ({ event }) => ({ item: event.item }) }] } },
      after: { 1500: 'idle' },                                    // (plan default) "Synced" shows briefly
    },
    conflict: {
      on: {
        RETRY: { target: 'queued', actions: 'resetHead' },
        DISCARD: { target: 'routing', actions: ['forgetHead', 'dropHead'] },
        EDIT: { target: 'queued', actions: 'replaceHeadWithNewKey' },
      },
    },
  },
})
```

Every guard and action the machine names is declared in `setup` (R-38); no inline guard or `assign` sits in the config. `replaceHeadWithNewKey` uses `enqueueActions` so the new key is computed once and both the context update and the IndexedDB swap use it ([enqueueActions](https://stately.ai/docs/actions#enqueue-actions), verify against the pinned version). A unit test (T-P0-25-14) walks the machine config and fails if any referenced guard, action, actor or delay name is missing from `setup`.

```ts
// lib/queueSender.ts
export async function sendQueued(item: QueueItem): Promise<SendResult> {
  return navigator.locks
    ? navigator.locks.request('tumnis-offline-queue', () => sendOnce(item))   // one tab replays at a time
    : sendOnce(item)
}
async function sendOnce(item: QueueItem): Promise<SendResult> {
  if (!(await idbQueue.has(item.idempotencyKey))) return { outcome: 'ok', taskId: '' }  // another tab sent it
  try {
    const task = await apiWrite({ kind: 'create', method: 'POST', path: '/tasks', body: item.body,
                                  idempotencyKey: item.idempotencyKey, schema: zTaskOut })
    await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [{ _id: 'tasksListTasks' }], exact: false })
    return { outcome: 'ok', taskId: task.id }
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof ApiError && [400, 403, 404, 409, 422].includes(e.status)) return { outcome: 'conflict', problem: e.problem }
    return { outcome: 'retry', problem: e instanceof ApiError ? e.problem : undefined }   // 401, 408, 429, 5xx, network
  }
}

// lib/idb.ts (https://github.com/jakearchibald/idb)
const db = openDB<TumnisDB>('tumnis', 1, { upgrade(d) {
  d.createObjectStore('offlineQueue', { keyPath: 'idempotencyKey' }).createIndex('createdAt', 'createdAt') } })
export const idbQueue = {
  all: async () => (await db).getAllFromIndex('offlineQueue', 'createdAt'),
  put: async (i: QueueItem) => { await (await db).put('offlineQueue', i) },
  delete: async (k: string) => { await (await db).delete('offlineQueue', k) },
  has: async (k: string) => (await (await db).count('offlineQueue', k)) > 0,
}
```

Host wiring (`QuickAddHost` in `AppShell`): one actor for the app, `window` `online`/`offline` events and `visibilitychange` (visible sends `ONLINE`), `announceSynced` provided through `machine.provide({ actions })`. `usePendingTasks(projectId?)` reads `snapshot.context.items` with `useSelector` from `@xstate/react` and renders them as rows with a pending mark ("Waiting to sync").

**Implementation notes**

- One path for every capture: online saves also go through the queue, so the offline path is exercised all day, not only when the VPN drops. IDB writes take milliseconds and do not threaten the 500 ms round trip.
- Replay also runs on app open because Safari has no Background Sync (architecture Frontend). `visibilitychange` covers an iPhone waking the PWA.
- The idempotency key is born at enqueue and never changes for that body; the server returns the stored response for 24 hours (REL-2). Items older than 23 hours (plan default) show a warning, because a replay after key expiry could duplicate if the first attempt actually landed.
- Web Locks keep two tabs from replaying the same item at once ([Web Locks API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Locks_API)); the `has` check inside the lock skips items another tab already sent.
- 401 is retryable: the item waits while the user signs in again, then `ONLINE` is sent after login.
- Hotkeys ignore `input`, `textarea`, `select` and `[contenteditable]` targets and respect IME composition (`event.isComposing`).
- `playwright` offline mode: `context.setOffline(true)` ([BrowserContext.setOffline](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-set-offline)); A0.2 uses it.

**Fixtures, fakes and data**

- `src/test/setup.ts` imports `fake-indexeddb/auto`; `resetIdb()` deletes the `tumnis` database between tests.
- `locksPolyfill()` in `src/test/` implementing `navigator.locks.request` with a promise chain.
- MSW handler `http.post('/v1/tasks', …)` with a per-key store that replays the first response for a repeated key, mirroring the backend.

- `navigator.locks` missing (older Safari): idempotency keys still prevent duplicates; only duplicate sends are possible, which the server absorbs.

#### P0-26 · Settings v0

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M0.5 Web app (weeks 3 to 4) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P0-22, P0-14, P0-15 |
| Unblocks | none |

**Goal.** Every phase 0 setting is reachable and usable on the phone: account and second factor, sessions, API keys, the audit log with CSV export, the dead-letter queue, the workspace timezone and the default subtask threshold. Forms validate with the generated zod schemas, so the browser and the server agree on the rules.

**Scope.** In: `/settings/$section` for `account`, `sessions`, `keys`, `audit`, `dead-letters`, `workspace`; React Hook Form with generated zod; the timezone picker. Out: providers, thresholds, calendars, working hours, focus and connectors (their phases), passkeys (P0-13 or P4).

```ts
// lib/timezones.ts (Intl.supportedValuesOf: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/supportedValuesOf)
export function ianaZones(): string[] {
  const zones = typeof Intl.supportedValuesOf === 'function' ? Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') : FALLBACK_ZONES
  return zones.includes('UTC') ? zones : ['UTC', ...zones]
}
export const browserZone = (): string => Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone

// components/settings/WorkspaceSection.tsx (React Hook Form + resolvers: https://github.com/react-hook-form/resolvers)
const schema = zWorkspaceSettingsIn.extend({
  timezone: zWorkspaceSettingsIn.shape.timezone.refine((z) => ianaZones().includes(z), 'Pick a timezone from the list'),
})
const form = useForm<z.infer<typeof schema>>({ resolver: zodResolver(schema), defaultValues: loaded })
const save = useWrite({
  mutationFn: (v: WorkspaceSettingsIn & { version: number; idempotencyKey: string }) =>
    apiWrite({ kind: 'update', method: 'PUT', path: '/settings/workspace', body: omit(v, 'version', 'idempotencyKey'),
               version: v.version, idempotencyKey: v.idempotencyKey, schema: zWorkspaceSettingsOut }),
})
```

**Implementation notes**

- The generated zod schemas carry the server's `Field` constraints (min, max, patterns) through OpenAPI, so bounds are not duplicated in the UI. The timezone refine is the one client-side addition; the server still validates with `zoneinfo` (P0-08).
- `Intl.supportedValuesOf` returns canonical zones; some engines omit `UTC`, hence the prepend. A saved alias the list lacks (for example `US/Eastern`) displays as-is with a note.
- Key secrets never enter the Query cache: the create mutation returns the secret to the dialog through `onSuccess` state and the list is refetched by invalidation.
- Destructive actions (revoke key, discard dead letter, sign out others) confirm in a dialog and are not undoable; undo (UX 9) covers task actions.
- Changing the timezone takes effect for day close through the anchor rule in P0-19.

**Interfaces**

```python
# core/telemetry.py (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/python/propagation/)
def setup_tracing(service: Literal["api", "worker"], exporter: SpanExporter | None = None) -> TracerProvider: ...
    # exporter None and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT unset: a provider with no exporter (IDs still generated)
def current_carrier() -> dict[str, str]: ...          # propagate.inject into a dict: {"traceparent": "00-…"}
@contextmanager
def span_from_carrier(name: str, carrier: Mapping[str, str], **attrs: str) -> Iterator[Span]: ...
    # ctx = propagate.extract(carrier); tracer.start_as_current_span(name, context=ctx)

# core/events.py: subscriber wrapper
async def run_subscriber(env: EventEnvelope, subscriber: str) -> None:
    with span_from_carrier(f"event {env.name} -> {subscriber}", env.trace_context,
                           **{"tumnis.event_id": str(env.event_id)}):
        await SUBSCRIBERS[(env.name, subscriber)](env)

# core/logging.py (https://www.structlog.org/en/stable/standard-library.html)
def add_trace_ids(_, __, event_dict: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ctx = trace.get_current_span().get_span_context()
    if ctx.is_valid:
        event_dict["trace_id"] = format(ctx.trace_id, "032x")
        event_dict["span_id"] = format(ctx.span_id, "016x")
    return event_dict
SHARED = [structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars, structlog.processors.add_log_level,
          structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso", utc=True), add_trace_ids, redact]   # redact from P0-16
# structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter renders uvicorn, sqlalchemy and dbos records with the same chain.
```

@router.get("/metrics", include_in_schema=False)
async def metrics(request: Request) -> Response:
    require_bearer(request, token=settings.metrics_token)   # hmac.compare_digest; 401 otherwise
    await refresh_scrape_gauges(owner_or_app_session)        # one query per source, no per-workspace loop
    return Response(generate_latest(REGISTRY), media_type=CONTENT_TYPE_LATEST)

-- queue depth and workflows by status (DBOS system schema; verify table and column names against the pinned DBOS)
SELECT queue_name, count(*) FROM dbos.workflow_status
 WHERE status = 'ENQUEUED' AND queue_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY queue_name;
SELECT status, count(*) FROM dbos.workflow_status
 WHERE created_at > (extract(epoch FROM now()) - 86400) * 1000 GROUP BY status;

Alert rules (thresholds are plan defaults unless tied to REL-1):

```yaml
# deploy/prometheus/alerts.yml
groups:
  - name: tumnis
    rules:
      - alert: TumnisQueueBacklog
        expr: max by (queue) (tumnis_queue_depth) > 100
        for: 10m
        labels: { severity: warning }
        annotations: { summary: "Queue {{ $labels.queue }} has had more than 100 waiting items for 10 minutes" }
      - alert: TumnisDeadLettersGrowing
        expr: delta(tumnis_dead_letters{status="open"}[30m]) > 0
        labels: { severity: warning }
        annotations: { summary: "Dead letters are growing" }
      - alert: TumnisWalArchiveStale        # archive_timeout is 60 s; REL-1 allows 15 min
        expr: time() - tumnis_wal_last_archived_timestamp_seconds > 300
        for: 5m
        labels: { severity: critical }
        annotations: { summary: "No WAL segment archived for over 5 minutes" }
      - alert: TumnisWalArchiveFailing
        expr: increase(tumnis_wal_archive_failed_total[15m]) > 0
        labels: { severity: critical }
        annotations: { summary: "WAL archiving is failing" }
      - alert: TumnisBackupMissing
        expr: time() - max by (repo) (tumnis_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds) > 26 * 3600
        labels: { severity: critical }
        annotations: { summary: "No successful backup to {{ $labels.repo }} in 26 hours" }
      - alert: TumnisCertificateExpiring   # from the homelab blackbox exporter
        expr: probe_ssl_earliest_cert_expiry{job="tumnis-tls"} - time() < 14 * 86400
        labels: { severity: warning }
        annotations: { summary: "Tumnis TLS certificate expires within 14 days" }
      - alert: TumnisAuditChainBroken
        expr: tumnis_ops_check_ok{check="audit_chain"} == 0
        labels: { severity: critical }
        annotations: { summary: "Audit hash chain verification failed" }
      - alert: TumnisAuditChainNotVerified
        expr: time() - tumnis_ops_check_timestamp_seconds{check="audit_chain"} > 26 * 3600
        labels: { severity: warning }
        annotations: { summary: "Audit chain has not been verified in 26 hours" }
```

```yaml
# deploy/prometheus/alerts.test.yml (https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/unit_testing_rules/)
rule_files: [alerts.yml]
evaluation_interval: 1m
tests:
  - interval: 1m
    input_series:
      - series: 'tumnis_queue_depth{queue="events"}'
        values: '150+0x20'
      - series: 'tumnis_queue_depth{queue="runs"}'
        values: '3+0x20'
    alert_rule_test:
      - eval_time: 9m
        alertname: TumnisQueueBacklog
        exp_alerts: []
      - eval_time: 12m
        alertname: TumnisQueueBacklog
        exp_alerts:
          - exp_labels: { severity: warning, queue: events }
            exp_annotations: { summary: "Queue events has had more than 100 waiting items for 10 minutes" }
  - interval: 1m
    input_series:
      - series: 'tumnis_wal_last_archived_timestamp_seconds'
        values: '0+60x30'          # archived every minute: healthy
    alert_rule_test:
      - eval_time: 30m
        alertname: TumnisWalArchiveStale
        exp_alerts: []
  - interval: 1m
    input_series:
      - series: 'tumnis_wal_last_archived_timestamp_seconds'
        values: '0+0x30'           # stuck at t=0
    alert_rule_test:
      - eval_time: 10m
        alertname: TumnisWalArchiveStale
        exp_alerts: []             # stale since 5m, "for" not yet satisfied
      - eval_time: 12m
        alertname: TumnisWalArchiveStale
        exp_alerts:
          - exp_labels: { severity: critical }
            exp_annotations: { summary: "No WAL segment archived for over 5 minutes" }
  - interval: 1m
    input_series:
      - series: 'tumnis_ops_check_ok{check="audit_chain"}'
        values: '1 1 0 0'
    alert_rule_test:
      - eval_time: 1m
        alertname: TumnisAuditChainBroken
        exp_alerts: []
      - eval_time: 3m
        alertname: TumnisAuditChainBroken
        exp_alerts:
          - exp_labels: { severity: critical, check: audit_chain }
            exp_annotations: { summary: "Audit hash chain verification failed" }
  # plus one firing and one quiet case each for DeadLettersGrowing, WalArchiveFailing,
  # BackupMissing, CertificateExpiring and AuditChainNotVerified
```

**Implementation notes**

- The architecture sends trace context as the packet's `correlation_id` to the daemon later; store the W3C `traceparent` now and derive `correlation_id` from its trace ID so the two stay one value.
- DBOS may replay a subscriber on recovery; spans from both attempts share the trace, which is what you want when reading a retry.
- Scrape-time queries run as the app role; DBOS system tables sit outside RLS. Keep `/metrics` workspace-agnostic: hosted mode drops per-workspace labels (none exist now).
- `route` label from the matched route template keeps cardinality bounded.
- `SENTRY_DSN` is a new deployment variable (Part A addition); unset means the SDK stays off.

- `span_exporter` fixture: `InMemorySpanExporter` wired through `setup_tracing`, cleared per test.

**Goal.** Postgres archives WAL every minute to a local pgBackRest repository and an encrypted Backblaze B2 repository that the backup key cannot delete from, and a scripted drill proves a point-in-time restore meets the 15-minute RPO and 1-hour RTO. The drill is the test.

**Scope.** In: the Postgres image with pgBackRest and supercronic, archive settings, stanza setup, both repositories, backup schedules, `ops_backup_runs`, the backup-freshness rule and workflow, the drill script and its workflow, the B2 no-delete check, the `rclone copy` check and the folder backup script. Out: scheduling the folder backup (P1-15, when Tumnis-made folders exist), Object Lock (fallback only).

**Interfaces**

```ini
# deploy/postgres/conf.d/archive.conf
wal_level = replica
archive_mode = on
archive_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=tumnis archive-push %p'
archive_timeout = 60s
max_wal_senders = 3
```

```ini
# deploy/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf   (https://pgbackrest.org/configuration.html)
[global]
repo1-path=/var/lib/pgbackrest
repo1-retention-full=4                # (plan default) four weekly fulls, about 28 days
repo1-bundle=y
repo2-type=s3
repo2-path=/tumnis/pgbackrest
repo2-s3-endpoint=s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com   # set per account region
repo2-s3-region=us-west-004
repo2-s3-bucket=tumnis-backups
repo2-s3-uri-style=host
repo2-cipher-type=aes-256-cbc
# No repo2-retention-*: pgBackRest never expires repo2. A B2 lifecycle rule removes files
# older than 35 days (architecture Backup and recovery).
compress-type=zst
process-max=2
start-fast=y
archive-async=y
spool-path=/var/spool/pgbackrest
log-level-console=info

[tumnis]
pg1-path=/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

Secrets (`repo2-s3-key`, `repo2-s3-key-secret`, `repo2-cipher-pass`) live in `/etc/pgbackrest/conf.d/secrets.conf`, a root-owned file mounted read-only from the host like the master key (SEC-6); pgBackRest reads `conf.d` through its default `config-include-path`.

```
# deploy/pgbackrest/crontab (supercronic, UTC)
7 3 * * 0     /usr/local/bin/run-backup.sh 1 full
7 3 * * 1-6   /usr/local/bin/run-backup.sh 1 diff
37 */6 * * *  /usr/local/bin/run-backup.sh 1 incr
27 3 * * 0    /usr/local/bin/run-backup.sh 2 full
27 3 * * 1-6  /usr/local/bin/run-backup.sh 2 diff
```

```bash
# deploy/pgbackrest/run-backup.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
repo="$1"; type="$2"; started="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
if pgbackrest --stanza=tumnis --repo="$repo" --type="$type" backup; then ok=true; else ok=false; fi
psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d tumnis -c \
  "INSERT INTO ops_backup_runs (repo, type, started_at, finished_at, ok) VALUES ('$repo', '$type', '$started', now(), $ok)"
[ "$ok" = true ]
```

```python
# core/backups.py (pure)
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BackupFacts:
    now: datetime
    wal_last_archived_at: datetime | None
    wal_failed_since_last_success: bool
    last_ok: Mapping[tuple[int, str], datetime]      # (repo, type) -> finished_at of last success

WAL_MAX_AGE: Final = timedelta(minutes=5)            # (plan default) inside the 15-minute RPO
BACKUP_MAX_AGE: Final = timedelta(hours=26)          # daily diff plus slack (plan default)
FULL_MAX_AGE: Final = timedelta(days=8)              # weekly full plus slack (plan default)

def backup_findings(f: BackupFacts) -> list[str]: ...   # e.g. ["wal_stale", "repo2_diff_missing"]; [] when healthy
```

The drill, step by step (`scripts/drill/restore_drill.sh`, `--mode prod` quarterly against the real B2 repository, `--mode rehearsal` nightly against a MinIO repository in `compose.test.yaml`):

1. **Preflight.** `pgbackrest --stanza=tumnis --repo=2 info --output=json` shows at least one full backup and an archive range; `docker` and the Postgres image of the running release are present. Set a `trap` that removes the scratch container and volume on any exit.
2. **Marker.** On the source: `INSERT INTO ops_drill_markers (id, kind) VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), 'marker')`, commit, then `SELECT clock_timestamp(), pg_walfile_name(pg_current_wal_lsn())` into `T_MARKER`, `MARKER_WAL`.
3. **Fence.** Sleep 2 s, insert a second row with `kind='fence'`, commit, read `FENCE_WAL` the same way. The fence gives recovery a commit after the target time, so recovery can stop exactly at the target.
4. **Wait for archive (RPO).** Poll `SELECT last_archived_wal FROM pg_stat_archiver` every 5 s until it is `>=` `FENCE_WAL`, with a 15-minute timeout; a timeout fails the drill (RPO missed). Record `RPO_OBSERVED = archive time - T_MARKER`.
5. **Loss.** `--mode rehearsal`: `docker compose -p tumnis-drill rm -sf postgres` and remove its volume. `--mode prod`: the production container is never touched; the scratch restore runs on a new volume with no access to the live data, which is the same situation from the restore's point of view.
6. **Restore (start the RTO clock).** `START=$(date +%s)`; `docker run --rm -v drill_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data -v /etc/pgbackrest:/etc/pgbackrest:ro <image> pgbackrest --stanza=tumnis --repo=2 --type=time "--target=$T_MARKER" --target-action=promote restore`.
7. **Start the scratch server** with archiving off so it never pushes WAL into the production stanza: `docker run -d --name tumnis-drill-pg -v drill_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data -v /etc/pgbackrest:/etc/pgbackrest:ro <image> postgres -c archive_mode=off -c port=5433`. The read-only `/etc/pgbackrest` mount (config plus `conf.d/secrets.conf`) is required: the `restore_command` that `pgbackrest restore` wrote calls `pgbackrest archive-get`, which must reach repo2 to replay WAL up to the target. Wait for `pg_isready` and for `SELECT pg_is_in_recovery()` to return false.
8. **Checks.** The marker row exists; the fence row does not (point-in-time precision); `tumnis migrate --check` against the scratch database reports head; `tumnis audit verify` passes; seed or real row counts are non-zero; DBOS system tables are present.
9. **Stop the clock.** `RTO = $(date +%s) - START`; fail if over 3,600 s.
10. **Record.** `tumnis drill record --mode "$MODE" --rpo-seconds "$RPO_OBSERVED" --rto-seconds "$RTO" --target "$T_MARKER"` against the source: one `audit_log` row (`action='drill.completed'`, details with both numbers) and `ops_status` row `check='restore_drill'`.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/restore-drill.yml
name: restore-drill
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs: { mode: { type: choice, options: [prod, rehearsal], default: prod } }
  schedule:
    - cron: "41 6 3 1,4,7,10 *"        # quarterly, 3rd day, 06:41 UTC
jobs:
  drill:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: scripts/drill/b2_no_delete_check.sh
      - run: scripts/drill/restore_drill.sh --mode "${{ inputs.mode || 'prod' }}"
```

- **T-P0-28-03.** With the backup key and the AWS CLI pointed at the B2 S3 endpoint: put `drill/probe-<ts>`; `list-object-versions` gives its `VersionId`; `delete-object --version-id <id>` must fail with `AccessDenied` (the key lacks `deleteFiles`). A delete without a version id succeeds as a hide marker, because hiding needs only `writeFiles` ([B2 key capabilities](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-key-capabilities)); the script then checks the version still exists, since a hidden file is recoverable. Exit non-zero if the version is gone.
- **T-P0-28-04.** rclone configured through `RCLONE_CONFIG_MINIO_*` environment variables. Write `a.txt` in a temp source; `rclone copy src minio:bkt/t`; delete `a.txt` at the source; `rclone copy` again; `rclone lsf minio:bkt/t` still lists `a.txt` ([rclone copy](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/)).
- **T-P0-28-08.** Rows: all fresh → `[]`; WAL archived 6 min ago → `wal_stale`; failures since last success → `wal_failing`; repo 2 diff 27 h old → `repo2_diff_missing`; repo 1 full 9 days old → `repo1_full_missing`.
- **T-P0-28-09.** Fixture facts from a fake source; after `backup_freshness_check` runs, `/health/ready` reports module `backups` as `degraded` (still 200 overall) and `tumnis_ops_check_ok{check="backups"}` is 0.

**Implementation notes**

- `archive_timeout = 60s` makes a quiet database ship a segment every minute ([pgBackRest user guide](https://pgbackrest.org/user-guide.html)); each forced segment is 16 MB before compression, which zstd shrinks sharply on an idle server.
- Never start a restored cluster with archiving on: it would push a new timeline into the production stanza. Step 7 forces `archive_mode=off`.
- Open question 3 (pgBackRest with a no-delete key) is answered by the first rehearsal against B2: pgBackRest must never need to delete in repo2. Risky paths are expire (disabled by having no retention) and cleanup of an aborted backup; if a backup aborts and the next one fails on a delete, switch to Object Lock per the fallback.
- `ops_*` tables have no `workspace_id`; add them to the table-registry allow-list with a comment, like the audit log.
- Restoring into the production image keeps the drill honest about extensions (pgvector) and the Postgres major version.

- `compose.test.yaml` gains a `minio` service and a pgBackRest `repo2` pointing at it for rehearsal mode (path-style URIs, a self-signed cert trusted in the container).
- T-P0-28-04 reuses the session-scoped `minio` fixture that P0-02 creates (R-17); this WP adds no fixture.

- B2 region endpoint or URI style differs: set `repo2-s3-uri-style=path`; rehearsal against MinIO already uses path style.

**Interfaces**

```js
// perf/k6/lib.js (thresholds: https://grafana.com/docs/k6/latest/using-k6/thresholds/)
const baseline = JSON.parse(open('../baseline.json'))       // init context only
export const NFR_MS = { quick_add: 500, dashboard_projects: 300, dashboard_today: 300, typeahead: 100 }
// NFR: quick-add 500 ms (PRD); the others are (plan default) API shares of the 1 s first paint
export function limitMs(name) {
  return Math.min(NFR_MS[name], Math.round(baseline[name].p95_ms * 1.2))   // PERF-2: 20% regression fails
}
export const headers = () => ({ Authorization: `Bearer ${__ENV.TUMNIS_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' })

// perf/k6/quickadd.js
import http from 'k6/http'
import { check } from 'k6'
import { uuidv4 } from 'https://jslib.k6.io/k6-utils/1.4.0/index.js'
import { limitMs, headers } from './lib.js'
export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    quick_add: { executor: 'constant-arrival-rate', rate: 5, timeUnit: '1s', duration: '60s', preAllocatedVUs: 10 },
  },
  thresholds: {
    'http_req_duration{name:quick_add}': [`p(95)<${limitMs('quick_add')}`],
    'http_req_duration{name:typeahead}': [`p(95)<${limitMs('typeahead')}`],
    http_req_failed: ['rate<0.01'],
  },
}
export default function () {
  const base = __ENV.BASE_URL
  const t = http.get(`${base}/v1/typeahead/projects?q=ac`, { headers: headers(), tags: { name: 'typeahead' } })
  check(t, { 'typeahead 200': (r) => r.status === 200 })
  const r = http.post(`${base}/v1/tasks`,
    JSON.stringify({ project_id: __ENV.PROJECT_ID, title: `k6 ${uuidv4()}` }),
    { headers: { ...headers(), 'Idempotency-Key': uuidv4() }, tags: { name: 'quick_add' } })
  check(r, { 'created': (res) => res.status === 201 })
}
```

LCP 2.5 s and CLS 0.1 are the "good" Core Web Vitals thresholds, and total blocking time stands in for INP in a lab run ([web.dev vitals](https://web.dev/articles/vitals)); the PRD names a Core Web Vitals budget without numbers, so these are the plan defaults.

```ts
// frontend/e2e/perf/timing.spec.ts (sketch)
test('dashboard first paint under 1 s on LAN', { tag: ['@P0-29', '@NFR-Performance', '@PERF-2'] },
  async ({ signedInPage: page, seededApp }) => {
    test.skip(test.info().project.name !== 'laptop')
    await seededApp.reset('load')                              // 10 projects, 2,000 tasks
    await page.goto('/')                                       // warm: service worker installed
    await page.reload()
    const ms = await page.evaluate(() => new Promise<number>((resolve) => {
      const NAME = 'tumnis:dashboard-ready'
      const seen = performance.getEntriesByName(NAME, 'mark')[0]
      if (seen) return resolve(seen.startTime)
      const o = new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
        const hit = list.getEntries().find((e) => e.name === NAME)   // ignore every other mark
        if (hit) { o.disconnect(); resolve(hit.startTime) }
      })
      o.observe({ type: 'mark', buffered: true })
    }))
    expect(ms).toBeLessThan(1000)
  })
```

- **T-P0-29-02.** Phone project. First visit installs the service worker; close the page. Open a new page in the same context with network emulation (CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions`, 50 ms latency (plan default for the VPN), Chromium only). Start the timer at `goto('/')`; press `/` every 100 ms until the quick-add input is focused; type "x" and read it back. Elapsed under 3,000 ms.
- **T-P0-29-06.** With `baseline.quick_add.p95_ms = 100`, the builder gives `p(95)<120`; a synthetic k6 summary with p95 125 fails the check script, 118 passes; an NFR lower than 1.2 x baseline wins.
- **T-P0-29-07.** Parametrized over `GET /v1/projects`, `GET /v1/tasks?status=today&order=today&limit=5`, `GET /v1/tasks?project_id={p}`, `GET /v1/projects/{p}/board`, `GET /v1/typeahead/projects?q=ac`. Fixtures `seed`, `load_fixture`, `query_counter`. Count at seed size equals count at load size, and each is at most its ceiling in a dict in the test (projects list 3: `set_config`, projects, stats aggregate).

**Implementation notes**

- The Performance job runs on the homelab self-hosted runner (A4) so numbers are comparable run to run; GitHub-hosted runners vary too much for a 20% rule.
- p95 is the plan's reading of "round trip under 500 ms"; the PRD gives no percentile.
- The load fixture must match A0.6 exactly: 10 projects and 2,000 tasks with realistic titles.
- Lighthouse needs a signed-in page: `lhci-login.cjs` signs in with the seed password and TOTP secret through Puppeteer before collection.
- A new baseline is a reviewed change, never an automatic update; a slower baseline needs Scott's label.

k6 run -e BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 -e TUMNIS_KEY=$KEY -e PROJECT_ID=$P perf/k6/quickadd.js
k6 run -e BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 -e TUMNIS_KEY=$KEY perf/k6/dashboard.js
