**Interfaces**

```python
# integrations/api.py
class ConnectionStatus(StrEnum):
    pending_auth = "pending_auth"; ok = "ok"; syncing = "syncing"
    degraded = "degraded"          # last run failed, retrying with backoff
    auth_required = "auth_required"  # refresh failed; user must reconnect
    disabled = "disabled"

class ConnectionOut(BaseModel):
    id: UUID; kind: ConnectorKind; provider: str; account_label: str
    status: ConnectionStatus; status_detail: str | None
    last_success_at: datetime | None; next_sync_at: datetime | None
    settings: ConnectionSettings          # never credentials
    version: int

class ConnectionSettings(BaseModel):
    backfill_days: int = 30               # Data flow rule 3
    sync_every_min: int | None = None     # None = provider default
    allowlist: list[str] = []             # chat channels (P3-05), bucket prefixes (P3-13)
    extra: dict[str, Any] = {}

async def create_connection(ws: WorkspaceCtx, provider: str, settings: ConnectionSettings) -> ConnectionOut: ...
async def start_oauth(ws: WorkspaceCtx, connection_id: UUID) -> OAuthStart: ...   # returns {workflow_id}; UI polls for authorize_url
async def complete_oauth(ws: WorkspaceCtx, state: str, code: str, iss: str | None) -> None: ...
async def request_sync(ws: WorkspaceCtx, connection_id: UUID) -> None: ...
async def disconnect(ws: WorkspaceCtx, connection_id: UUID, reason: str) -> None: ...  # audited; content kept until purge (P3-09)

# integrations/rules.py (pure)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProviderLimit: requests: int; period_s: int
PROVIDER_LIMITS: Mapping[str, ProviderLimit]   # granola 90/60 (docs say about 100), inbox_zero 60/60, slack 45/60, google_drive 300/60 (plan defaults)
DEFAULT_SYNC_MIN: Mapping[str, int]            # inbox_zero 5 (PRD), granola 30, chat 5, google_drive 10 (PRD), s3 15 (PRD) (others plan defaults)

def backfill_start(now: datetime, settings: ConnectionSettings, provider_cap_days: int | None) -> datetime: ...
def next_sync_at(now: datetime, last: datetime | None, every_min: int, failures: int) -> datetime: ...  # backoff on failures
def status_after(prev: ConnectionStatus, outcome: SyncOutcome) -> ConnectionStatus: ...
```

Sync page contract (extends P0-12's `Connector` protocol from the architecture):

```python
class SyncPage(BaseModel):
    items: list[RawItem]           # raw provider payloads, one per canonical source object
    tombstones: list[str] = []     # external_ids deleted at the provider
    next_cursor: Cursor | None     # None = caught up
    scope: str = "default"         # e.g. mailbox id, channel id; one cursor per scope

class Cursor(BaseModel):          # opaque to the framework, owned by the connector
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow")
    schema_version: Literal[1] = 1                  # integer versions (R-02)
```

Workflow shape (DBOS; API per the [DBOS queue tutorial](https://docs.dbos.dev/python/tutorials/queue-tutorial) and [workflow communication](https://docs.dbos.dev/python/tutorials/workflow-communication), verify against the pinned version):

```python
# Registered in worker.py after DBOS.launch() (static schedules, see A9):
# DBOS.apply_schedules([{"schedule_name": "connector-sync-tick", "workflow_fn": connector_sync_tick,
#                        "schedule": "* * * * *", "context": None}])
@DBOS.workflow()
def connector_sync_tick(scheduled: datetime, context: object) -> None:
    for c in due_connections_step(scheduled):     # status in (ok, degraded) and next_sync_at <= now
        with SetEnqueueOptions(deduplication_id=f"sync:{c.id}", queue_partition_key=c.provider):
            DBOS.enqueue_workflow("sync", connector_sync, c.workspace_id, c.id)

@DBOS.workflow()
def connector_sync(workspace_id: UUID, connection_id: UUID) -> SyncOutcome:
    scopes = list_scopes_step(workspace_id, connection_id)
    for scope in scopes:
        while True:
            cursor = load_cursor_step(workspace_id, connection_id, scope)
            page = fetch_page_step(workspace_id, connection_id, scope, cursor)   # outbound call, retried by the adapter base
            done = persist_page_step(workspace_id, connection_id, page)          # one transaction: upserts, raw payloads, cursor, outbox
            if done: break
    return finish_step(workspace_id, connection_id)
```

`persist_page_step` writes the canonical records (P0-12 upsert), raw payloads, tombstones (`deleted_at`), the new cursor in `sync_state` and one `items.ingested{connection_id, item_ids}` event, all in one transaction. A crash after the transaction resumes at the next `fetch_page_step` with the saved cursor. A crash inside it rolls back and the step reruns.

OAuth connect as a workflow, because the api cannot call out inside a request. The wait for the browser redirect happens in the workflow body, never inside a step or the HTTP handler (R-30):

```python
OAUTH_WAIT_S = 900        # plan default; configurable so tests use a short value (R-30)

@DBOS.workflow()
def connect_oauth(workspace_id: UUID, connection_id: UUID) -> OAuthOutcome:
    # step: protected-resource and authorization-server discovery, dynamic registration (or CIMD),
    # PKCE verifier, state; client_info and verifier stored encrypted on the connection
    url = oauth_prepare_step(workspace_id, connection_id)
    DBOS.set_event("authorize_url", url)                          # the UI polls GET .../oauth/url
    msg = DBOS.recv("oauth_callback", timeout_seconds=OAUTH_WAIT_S)   # workflow body only
    if msg is None:
        return oauth_expired_step(workspace_id, connection_id)   # status back to pending_auth
    # step: reads the code the callback handler stored, exchanges it with the verifier,
    # persists tokens through ConnectionTokenStorage (encrypted, P0-08), deletes the stored code
    return oauth_exchange_step(workspace_id, connection_id, msg["pending_id"])
```

The callback handler (`GET /v1/connections/oauth/callback`) makes no outbound call and never waits: it looks up the pending authorization by `state`, stores the `code` (and `iss`) encrypted in `oauth_pending(connection_id, workflow_id, state_hash, code_enc, iss, expires_at)`, calls `DBOS.send(workflow_id, {"pending_id": …}, topic="oauth_callback")` and redirects the browser to the connection page. After connect, the SDK's `OAuthClientProvider` runs non-interactively on the stored tokens (refresh only); if it ever asks for its redirect or callback handler, the handler raises `ReauthRequired` and the connection goes to `auth_required`.

REST (all `/v1`, session only): `GET/POST /connections`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /connections/{id}`, `POST /connections/{id}/oauth/start`, `GET /connections/{id}/oauth/url` (poll for the authorize URL), `GET /connections/oauth/callback` (browser redirect target; stores the code and sends to the waiting workflow), `POST /connections/{id}/sync`.

**Implementation notes**
- The MCP SDK's `OAuthClientProvider` is an httpx auth hook; pass it on an HTTP client built by `core.net` so every provider URL goes through the SSRF guard (SEC-5). If the pinned SDK cannot take an injected client, wrap its transport; do not bypass the guard.
- `ConnectionTokenStorage` implements the SDK's four-method `TokenStorage` protocol against `connections.credentials_enc` (tokens) and `connections.settings.extra.oauth_client` (registered client info, also encrypted). Persist `client_info`: losing it forces a new registration and a new consent.
- The callback route validates `state` against `oauth_pending`, stores the code and calls `DBOS.send(workflow_id, {"pending_id": …}, topic="oauth_callback")`; it never calls `recv` (R-30). A stale or unknown `state` returns 400 and is audited as `connector.oauth_state_mismatch`. The discovery, registration and exchange logic reuses the SDK's OAuth helpers where the pinned version exposes them as functions, and plain httpx calls through `core.net` otherwise.
- Rate limits are per provider account, not per workspace; Granola documents about 100 requests per minute, so the default is 90 (plan default) to leave headroom for the agent's own direct use, if any.
- Cadence: `next_sync_at = last + every_min`, with failure backoff `min(60, every_min * 2**failures)` minutes plus jitter (plan default). The tick runs every minute; a manual "Sync now" sets `next_sync_at = now`.
- Rule 3: backfill is 30 days, configurable per connection; the first sync pages backwards from now to `backfill_start`, then switches to forward sync. The cursor records the phase.
- Never log payloads or tokens: `persist_page_step` logs counts only (SEC-6 redaction filter already drops bodies).
- `items.ingested` carries IDs only; subscribers read records through `integrations.api`.
- The `connection_auth` review kind is registered with P0-18's `register_review_kind` (owner `integrations`, actions `accept` = reconnect, primary, and `snooze`; R-03, R-04) and raised with `add_review_item("connection_auth", …, dedupe_key=f"conn_auth:{connection_id}")`, so repeated failures never stack items.

**Fixtures, fakes and data**
- `fakes.oauth_server` (ASGI app mounted in the fake transport): metadata, DCR, authorize (auto-approve), token with rotating refresh.
- `FakeSource(pages: list[SyncPage], fail_on: dict[int, Exception])` registered as provider `fake`.
- Seed: none; connections are created per test through `create_connection`.

**Risks and fallbacks**
- The SDK's OAuth provider assumes an interactive client in one process: the DBOS event and recv bridge keeps it in one workflow; if the SDK version cannot resume after a worker restart mid-authorization, the user simply clicks Connect again (the workflow times out after 15 minutes, plan default).
- A provider without refresh tokens: covered by P3-01's fallback; the connection shows `auth_required` when the access token expires instead of failing silently.
- DBOS partition limiter semantics differ from expectations: the token bucket in `core.ratelimit` is the source of truth and the partition only spreads load.

**Interfaces**

Mapping table (provider field names are the ones P3-01's recordings show; the names below are the expected shape and the mapper test is the arbiter):

| Canonical field | Source (Inbox Zero tool result) | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Thread.external_id` | `read_thread.threadId` | Prefixed with the mailbox: `<emailAccountId>:<threadId>` so two mailboxes never collide |
| `Thread.subject` | first message `subject` | Stripped of `Re:`/`Fwd:` prefixes for display; raw kept |
| `Thread.participants` | union of `from`, `to`, `cc` over messages | Lowercased emails; names kept separately |
| `Thread.provider_url` | `read_thread` link field, else built from mailbox + thread | Opened only from the drawer's secondary link |
| `Message.external_id` | `<emailAccountId>:<messageId>` | |
| `Message.message_key` | RFC 5322 `Message-ID` header if present, else `sha256(from, date, subject, first 200 chars)` | Same email in two mailboxes gets one key (P3-06) |
| `Message.sent_at` | `date` / `internalDate` | Parsed to UTC |
| `Message.body_text` | plain-text body | Truncated by the provider ("truncated plain-text bodies" per docs); `truncated: true` flag kept |
| `Message.body_html_sanitized` | HTML body if present | `core.sanitize` (nh3 allow-list); remote images replaced by a placeholder (SEC-4) |
| `Message.labels` | `labelIds` / labels | Stored, never written back |
| `tainted`, `source` | constant | `true`, `"email"` (SAF-1) |
| `Person` | each address | Upsert on workspace + primary email (P0-12) |

Cursor, one scope per mailbox:

```python
class InboxZeroCursor(Cursor):
    phase: Literal["backfill", "forward"]
    since: datetime            # forward: newest sent_at seen minus 10 minutes overlap (plan default)
    until: datetime | None     # backfill: page boundary moving backwards to backfill_start
    page_token: str | None     # provider pagination token within one search, if the tool returns one
    reconcile_after: datetime  # next deletion reconcile time (every 60 min, plan default)
```

`draft_reply`:

```python
# integrations/mcp.py: surface models per P2-01 (R-33)
class DraftReplyIn(WriteInput):                  # WriteInput carries idempotency_key and optional schema_version
    context_item_id: UUID                        # must target a Message or Thread in the caller's project scope
    body_text: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=20_000)   # plan default

class DraftReplyOut(BaseModel):
    schema_version: Literal[1] = 1
    status: Literal["created", "pending", "approval_required"]
    draft_request_id: UUID
    provider_draft_id: str | None = None
    provider_url: str | None = None

async def draft_reply(caller: Caller, inp: DraftReplyIn) -> DraftReplyOut: ...
# 1. scope drafts:write and project scope come from the SurfaceOp registration (P2-01);
# 2. match await agents.api.check_action(caller, "create_draft"):          # P2-05
#      ApprovalRequired -> return status "approval_required", nothing created (a tainted run, SAF-1)
#      Denied           -> error with its code (for example run_token_required for a key with no run, R-31)
#      Allowed          -> continue
# 3. enqueue create_draft_workflow; 4. wait on DBOS.get_event(wf_id, "draft", timeout_seconds=20)
#    (plan default; get_event, not recv, R-30) -> created or pending

register_op(SurfaceOp(name="draft_reply", description="Create a reply draft in the source mailbox. Never sends.",
    scope="drafts:write", input_model=DraftReplyIn, output_model=DraftReplyOut, rest_method="POST",
    rest_path="/v1/context-items/{context_item_id}/draft-reply", write=True, updates_existing=False,
    project_arg=None, project_resolver=project_of_context_item, handler=draft_reply))
```

The client class exposes no method whose name contains `send`, and the allow-list excludes rule tools; `create_draft` is the only write.

**Implementation notes**
- Inbox Zero's `search_inbox` returns metadata and snippets; `read_thread` returns truncated plain-text bodies ([Inbox Zero MCP reference](https://docs.getinboxzero.com/api-reference/mcp)). So each sync page is one search plus one `read_thread` per new or changed thread. Keep the count per page small (20 threads, plan default) to stay inside the rate limit.
- Query syntax for "since" depends on the backing mailbox (Gmail-style `after:`); take it from the recordings, not from guesswork, and keep it in one function.
- Never call `create_rule`, `update_rule`, `delete_rule` or anything not on the allow-list, even though the `mcp:write` scope permits rule edits. The allow-list is the enforcement; a contract test lists the allowed names.
- Draft body is plain text written by the agent; Tumnis does not add quoted history. The draft appears in the user's mail client, where sending stays with the human (FR-14.9).
- Mailbox never decides the project (Data flow rule 2): the connector stores no project on Messages; P3-06 does matching.
- Store `body_text` in full as returned; Jev gets only the first 2,000 characters (P3-06).

- `fakes.inbox_zero.drafts` list for assertions.

**Risks and fallbacks**
- Tool argument names differ between Inbox Zero versions: the fake raises on unknown calls, and the nightly probe (P3-01) catches a live change; pin the Inbox Zero version in the homelab compose.
- Truncated bodies lose the actionable sentence: the mapper keeps the snippet plus truncated text; Jev only needs the first 2,000 characters anyway. If recall suffers, raise it with Inbox Zero rather than scraping the mailbox directly.
- Deletion reconcile costs calls: reconcile only threads updated in the last 7 days (plan default); older deletions are caught by the retention purge (P3-09) or never matter.

#### P3-04 · Granola connector

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.1 Verify, then connect (week 12) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P3-02 |
| Unblocks | P3-07 |
| Traces | SAAS-2, Integrations: Granola |

**Goal.** Pull each Granola note soon after its meeting ends, plus a periodic poll, into canonical Notes with extracted action items and a link to the matching calendar Event, respecting the Basic plan's 30-day window, and show a recording-consent notice that must be acknowledged before the connection is made.

**Scope.** In: Granola client and mapper, action-item extraction, note-to-event linking rule, the post-meeting pull workflow, the periodic poll, consent notice. Out: project matching (P3-06 uses the linked event and attendees), transcripts (off by default, a per-connection setting).

| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/adapters/granola/{client,mapper,connector,fake}.py` | new | Allow-list `get_account_info`, `list_meetings`, `get_meetings`, `get_meeting_transcript` (only when enabled) |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/rules.py` | edit | `extract_action_items`, `link_note_to_event`, `granola_window_start`, `post_meeting_schedule` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/workflows.py` | edit | `granola_after_meeting` workflow; subscriber on `calendar.synced` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/events.py` | edit | Subscriber registration |

| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/tests/recordings/granola/*.json` | edit | `expected` blocks |

**Interfaces**

| Canonical field | Source (Granola tool result) | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Note.external_id` | meeting `id` | |
| `Note.title` | `title` | |
| `Note.start_at`, `end_at` | meeting date and time fields | UTC; if only a date and duration are given, derived; the recording decides |
| `Note.attendees` | `attendees` | Emails lowercased; each upserts a Person |
| `Note.body_text` | summarized notes plus private notes (`get_meetings`) | Markdown kept as text; private notes prefixed with a heading so agents see which is which |
| `Note.action_items` | parsed from the summarized notes | `extract_action_items` |
| `Note.event_id` | none from Granola | `link_note_to_event` against canonical Events |
| `Note.provider_url` | meeting link field if present | |
| `tainted`, `source` | constant | `true`, `"note"` (SAF-1, design decision 14; source value per R-37) |

```python
# integrations/rules.py
class ActionItem(BaseModel):
    text: str
    owner: str | None = None       # "@Scott", "Scott:" or "(Scott)" patterns
    due_hint: str | None = None    # raw phrase such as "by Friday"; never parsed into a date here

def extract_action_items(markdown: str) -> list[ActionItem]: ...
# Sections whose heading matches /^(action items|next steps|to-?dos?|follow[- ]ups?)$/i (plan default list);
# bullets and checkboxes inside them; nested bullets join to their parent with "; ".

def link_note_to_event(note: NoteTimes, events: Sequence[EventLite], *, slack_min: int = 15,
                       min_jaccard: float = 0.5) -> UUID | None: ...
# Candidates overlap [start - slack, end + slack]; score = attendee Jaccard; ties by smallest start gap;
# returns None if best Jaccard < min_jaccard. (slack and threshold are plan defaults)

def granola_window_start(now: datetime, plan: Literal["basic", "paid", "unknown"], backfill_days: int) -> datetime: ...
# basic: max(now - 30 days, now - backfill_days); paid: now - backfill_days; unknown: treated as basic

POST_MEETING_OFFSETS = (timedelta(minutes=5), timedelta(minutes=15), timedelta(minutes=45), timedelta(minutes=120))
# plan default; the default of settings.granola_post_meeting_offsets, seconds in tests (R-30)

def post_meeting_schedule(event_end: datetime, offsets: Sequence[timedelta] = POST_MEETING_OFFSETS) -> list[datetime]: ...
# event end plus each offset, then stop; the periodic poll covers the rest
```

```python
class GranolaCursor(Cursor):
    since: datetime                 # newest meeting start seen minus 1 day overlap (notes are edited after meetings)
    plan: Literal["basic", "paid", "unknown"] = "unknown"   # from get_account_info or tool availability
```

Consent: `POST /v1/connections` for `provider="granola"` stores the connection in `pending_auth`; `POST /v1/connections/{id}/oauth/start` returns 422 `consent_required` unless `POST /v1/connections/{id}/consent` was called, which records `consent_ack_at`, the acknowledging user and the notice version, and writes audit `connector.consent_acknowledged`.

Notice text (v1, stored with a version number): "Granola records and summarizes meetings. Before you connect it, make sure the people in your meetings know they may be recorded, as required where you and they are. Tumnis will store meeting notes on your server and send parts of them to your project agents."

**Implementation notes**
- Granola's tools on the Basic plan: `list_meetings`, `get_meetings`, `get_account_info`; `get_meeting_transcript` and folder tools are paid-only ([Granola MCP help](https://docs.granola.ai/help-center/sharing/integrations/mcp)). Transcripts are not fetched unless the connection setting `fetch_transcripts` is on (plan default off), which keeps stored text to the minimum (Data flow rule 6).
- Detect the plan from `get_account_info` if it reports one, else from a failed paid-tool call recorded in P3-01; store it on the cursor.
- The post-meeting workflow sleeps durably (`DBOS.sleep`), so a restart does not lose the schedule ([DBOS workflow tutorial](https://docs.dbos.dev/python/tutorials/workflow-tutorial), verify against the pinned version).
- Notes change after the meeting (users edit summaries); the 1-day overlap on the cursor re-reads recent notes and the upsert updates in place. Action items are re-extracted; P3-07 dedupes proposals against what was already proposed from the same note.
- The event link helps P3-06 match the project by the event's attendees and title; the link is advisory and stored on the Note, not a hard foreign key.

**Risks and fallbacks**
- Provider rate limits make history sync slow: sync only allow-listed channels, newest first, with small pages; backfill 30 days is the ceiling.
- Discord chosen and no author emails: accept keyword and channel matching; Jev's `unknown` path sends the rest to review.

### M3.2 · From item to proposal (week 13)

Routing stays in Tumnis and reasoning stays in Hermes, and each side is tested on its own.

#### P3-06 · Matching and actionability

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.2 From item to proposal (week 13) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P3-03, P1-02 |
| Unblocks | P3-07 |
| Traces | FR-14.8, FR-11.4, Data flow rules 2, 6 |

**Goal.** For every ingested Message, Thread and Note, decide in under a second and without an agent which project it belongs to and whether it asks for something, then either start a proposal run, file it as context only, or ask the human. The routing logic is a pure decision table; the decisions go through P1-02's provider layer so they are logged, cached, thresholded and calibrated.

**Scope.** In: the `triage_item` workflow on the `decisions` queue, subscribed to `items.ingested`; the pure `route_item` table; input builders for P1-01's catalogue points `project_match`, `actionability` and `duplicate` (the question definitions already exist in the `decisions/questions/` package); local-only pre-routing; logical-message dedupe across mailboxes; the `triage_items` result table; review kinds `project_match` (R-03) and `actionability_check`, registered with P0-18's `register_review_kind`. The Jev rate limit is not this WP's job: `decisions.api.decide` enforces it on the Jev credential (R-32). Out: the proposal run and review UI (P3-07), calibration (P3-08).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/rules.py` | edit | `route_item`, `TriageInputs`, `TriageRoute`, `match_fields`, `prefer_local` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/models.py` | edit | `triage_items(item_type, item_id, message_key, project_id, route, match_conf, actionable_prob, provider, decided_at, reviewed_by)` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/workflows.py` | edit | `triage_item` workflow and steps |

**Interfaces**

The questions are P1-01's catalogue points (`project_match` Choice with `unknown`, `actionability` Noul, `duplicate` Nouls `dup_1` to `dup_5`); this WP only builds their inputs, using exactly the whitelisted field names and caps P1-01 declares, so P1-01's outbound snapshot tests keep guarding them.

```python
# integrations/rules.py (pure)
def match_inputs(item: CanonicalItem) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """project_match inputs: kind, sender_email, sender_name, subject, thread_subject, participants,
    body_head (first 2,000 characters, never attachments). Notes use the title as subject and
    attendees as participants. Project options come from decide's catalogue, not from here."""

def actionability_inputs(item: CanonicalItem) -> dict[str, Any]:     # kind, sender_email, subject, body_head
def local_only_hint(item: CanonicalItem, projects: Sequence[ProjectLite]) -> UUID | None:
    """A local-decisions-only project whose linked domains or people match any sender, participant or
    attendee; decide(..., project_id=hint) then routes the question to the local fallback."""

class TriageRoute(StrEnum):
    proposal_run = "proposal_run"            # matched and actionable
    context_only = "context_only"            # matched, not actionable: linked for digest only
    review_project = "review_project"        # review kind project_match: which project? (R-03)
    review_actionable = "review_actionable"  # review kind actionability_check: matched, is this actionable?
    duplicate_item = "duplicate_item"        # same logical message already triaged: reuse that result
    skip = "skip"                            # tombstoned, archived project, own outgoing mail with no request

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TriageInputs:
    already_triaged_route: TriageRoute | None     # same message_key seen before
    deleted: bool
    match: DecisionResult | None                  # None = decisions unavailable
    match_threshold: float
    project_archived: bool
    project_paused: bool                          # SAF-4 per-project pause
    actionable: DecisionResult | None
    actionable_threshold: float
    from_self_only: bool                          # outgoing mail where the user wrote the last message

def route_item(i: TriageInputs) -> TriageRoute: ...
```

Decision table (rows evaluated top to bottom; first match wins). `conf` is the confidence P1-02 returns, already stricter for fallback answers:

| # | Condition | Route | Review item kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `deleted` | skip | none |
| 2 | `already_triaged_route` is set | duplicate_item (copy project and route; start no second run) | none |
| 3 | `match is None` (Jev and fallback both down) | review_project | `project_match` |
| 4 | `match.answer == "unknown"` or `match.conf < match_threshold` | review_project | `project_match` |
| 5 | `project_archived` | skip (stored, linked to project, no run) | none |
| 6 | `from_self_only` | context_only | none |
| 7 | `actionable is None` | review_actionable | `actionability_check` |
| 8 | `actionable.prob >= actionable_threshold` and not `project_paused` | proposal_run | none |
| 9 | `actionable.prob >= actionable_threshold` and `project_paused` | review_actionable (held until resume) | `actionability_check` |
| 10 | `actionable.prob <= 1 - actionable_threshold` | context_only | none |
| 11 | otherwise (uncertain band) | review_actionable | `actionability_check` |

Workflow:

```python
@DBOS.workflow()
def triage_item(workspace_id: UUID, item_type: str, item_id: UUID) -> TriageRoute:
    item = load_item_step(...)                                   # canonical record + message_key
    prior = prior_triage_step(workspace_id, item.message_key)    # row lock on message_key
    projects = candidate_projects_step(workspace_id)
    hint = local_only_hint(item, projects)
    subject = SubjectRef(type=item.subject_type, id=item.id)          # "message" or "note"
    match = decide_step("project_match", match_inputs(item), subject=subject, project_id=hint)
    project = resolve_project(match)                                   # None on unknown or below threshold
    actionable = decide_step("actionability", actionability_inputs(item), subject=subject,
                             project_id=project.id if project else hint)
    # decide_step wraps decisions.api.decide (P1-02): local-only check, cache, Jev limiter on the
    # Jev credential (R-32), primary, fallback, threshold routing and the decision log
    route = route_item(TriageInputs(...))
    apply_route_step(workspace_id, item, route, project)          # triage_items row, ContextItem, review item or proposal-run enqueue
    return route
```

Enqueue from the `items.ingested` subscriber: one `triage_item` per Thread (email and chat: the thread, using its newest message) and per Note, on the `decisions` queue with dedup ID `triage:<item_type>:<item_id>:<content_version>` so an edited note is re-triaged but a replayed event is not. The queue carries no stand-in rate limit for Jev; a burst of items simply waits inside `decide` for the credential's limiter (R-32).

Review kinds (registered in `integrations/review_kinds.py` with `register_review_kind`, R-03; actions per R-04, primary first):

| Kind | Actions | Payload per action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_match` | `answer` (primary, Enter), `reject`, `snooze` | answer: `{project_id}`; reject: not work, keep as context only |
| `actionability_check` | `accept` (primary, Enter: it is actionable, start the proposal run), `reject` (context only), `snooze` | none |

`duplicate` is exposed for P3-07 as `integrations.api.check_duplicates(proposal: ProposalDraft, project_id) -> list[DuplicateHit]`: candidates are the top 5 open tasks in the project from `search.api.search` on the proposal title and first action (plan default), each asked as one `duplicate` Noul; hits at or above the `duplicate` threshold are returned.

**Implementation notes**
- Matching is Jev's job (Data flow rule 2); the mailbox, calendar or chat workspace never decides the project. `local_only_hint` looks at links only to choose the provider, never the answer.
- Why pre-route by link: the local-only switch is per project, but the project is not known before matching. Any hint that the item belongs to a local-only project keeps it off Jev entirely. This is the plan's reading of Data flow rule 6; Scott confirms it in the PR.
- Thresholds come from P1-02's `thresholds` rows for `project_match`, `actionability` and `duplicate`, with their conservative defaults, so most items go to review until P3-08 calibrates.
- Decisions are cached for 24 hours by P1-02; the cache key includes the candidate project list hash so adding a project invalidates the match cache naturally.
- `from_self_only`: the last message in the thread is from one of the user's connected addresses; a request the user made of someone else does not become the user's task (plan default).
- Chat threads: triage on the thread, not on each message, and only when the thread's newest message is new (content version); a busy channel therefore does not flood Jev.
- Latency budget: two decisions at 70 to 500 ms each (FR-11.2) keep triage under a second; the proposal run itself is asynchronous.

- `expected_route` added to the `meta` of every Inbox Zero, Granola and chat recording.
- Jev fake scripts keyed by question ID and a hash of the fields; vLLM fake mirrors them.
- Seed: "Clinic" project with local-only on and a linked domain, for T-P3-06-08 and the A3 suite.

**Risks and fallbacks**

- Too many `project_match` items at first: the review queue groups them by sender domain so one decision can teach Tumnis (user adds the domain to the project's links from the item, which future matches see as a candidate hint).
- Candidate list grows past Jev's 255-option Choice limit (FR-11.2): only active, unarchived projects are candidates; if still over, pre-filter by linked-domain hits and recency (plan default top 50).

#### P3-07 · Proposal runs and bulk review

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.2 From item to proposal (week 13) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P3-06, P3-04, P2-04 |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-6.2, FR-14.2, FR-13.3, J4, J5 |

**Goal.** Close the capture loop: a matched, actionable item starts a short proposal run on the project's agent, which posts proposed tasks linked to the item; Tumnis dedupes them against open tasks and shows them in the review queue grouped by source, where one keystroke accepts one and one chord accepts a whole meeting or thread. Accepted proposals become tainted tasks carrying the ContextItem, and reach the project digest.

**Scope.** In: the triage carrier task and the proposal run through `agents.api.request_run` (R-23) with a packet from `build_packet(kind="proposal")` (R-24), proposal-mode `create_task`, `proposals` table and lifecycle, duplicate check, the `proposal` review kind registered with `register_review_kind` (R-03) and the UI for it and for P3-06's `project_match` and `actionability_check` kinds, bulk accept per source, the project Inbox view content, `get_context_item` in the task drawer, human-time measurement for the exit gate. Out: triage (P3-06), the proposal skill's prompt quality beyond its skill test (tuned in the profile repo).

| `profiles/tests/cases/proposals_*.yaml` | new | Skill cases |

**Interfaces**

```sql
-- proposals (integrations); base columns plus:
project_id uuid not null, run_id uuid, context_item_id uuid not null,
source_key text not null,            -- 'thread:<id>' | 'note:<id>'; groups bulk accept (FR-6.2)
title text not null, label text not null, estimate_minutes int, first_action text not null,
acceptance_criteria text, parent_ref text,  -- optional grouping inside one run
status text not null check (status in ('pending','accepted','rejected','rejected_duplicate','snoozed')),
duplicate_of_task_id uuid, duplicate_prob real,
tainted boolean not null default true, accepted_task_id uuid, decided_by text, decided_at timestamptz
-- unique (workspace_id, run_id, title) so a retried run does not double-post
```

Requesting the run (R-23). `request_run` takes a task, and a proposal run has none of its own, so `start_proposal_run` first creates one hidden carrier task per routed item: title "Triage: <thread subject or meeting title>", label AI, `source="triage"`, `system_role="triage_carrier"`, linked to the item's ContextItem (so P2-08's `derive_taint` makes it tainted). Then:

```python
run_id = await agents.api.request_run(carrier.id, RunKind.PROPOSAL)     # P2-04; no hand-built enqueue
# request_run creates the runs row and enqueues dispatch_run(run_id) with SetWorkflowID(run_id) and the
# project partition key. When the run reaches a terminal status, a run.finished subscriber closes the carrier.
```

The packet is `build_packet(RunKind.PROPOSAL, task_id=carrier.id, run_id=…, token=…, nonce=…)` inside `dispatch_run`, with P2-02's schema and nothing hand-built (R-24): the `TaskRunRequest` body carries the carrier task, the project brief and passages, and the linked item as a nonce'd untrusted block (`<untrusted-data id="u-<nonce>" source="email" …>` … `</untrusted-data id="u-<nonce>">`); `policy` lists P2-02's action classes with `gated` and `allowed` (every action on this tainted run resolves to approval required through `check_action`, except `create_task` in proposal mode, which only writes proposals and is not an action class); `callback` carries `mcp_url`, `rest_base_url` and the task token; `tainted` is true. P3-07 adds one field to the proposal body in `packet_builder.py`: `open_tasks` (id, title, status; up to 50 most recent open tasks in the project, plan default) so the agent can dedupe (J5). The task token's scopes are P2-02's `run_token_scopes(RunKind.PROPOSAL, …)`. The run's active-time cap is the project's (SAF-5); proposal runs normally finish in well under a minute.

```python
# tasks/api.py create_task (P2-01 op handler (caller, inp)), new branch
if caller.run_id and (await agents.api.get_run(caller.run_id)).kind == RunKind.PROPOSAL:
    return await integrations.api.create_proposal(caller, ProposalDraft.from_create_task(inp))
    # requires context_item_ids in the input; label, first_action; estimate for Human and Hybrid (same rule as tasks)

# integrations/api.py
async def create_proposal(caller: Caller, draft: ProposalDraft) -> ProposalOut: ...   # taint per P2-08; runs check_duplicates; emits proposal.posted
async def accept_proposals(user: User, ids: list[UUID] | None, source_key: str | None,
                           edits: dict[UUID, ProposalEdit], idempotency_key: str) -> list[UUID]: ...
    # one transaction: tasks.api.create_task per proposal (tainted, source="proposal", ContextItem copied),
    # proposal.status=accepted, review items decided, human.decided per proposal
async def reject_proposal(user: User, id: UUID, reason: str | None) -> None: ...
```

Bulk endpoint: `POST /v1/review/bulk {action: "accept", source_key: "note:…", exclude: [ids], idempotency_key}`; `exclude` defaults to proposals flagged as duplicates. Proposals from a different source in the same request are refused with 422 `mixed_sources`.

Review kind (R-03, R-04): `proposal`, owner `integrations`, actions `accept` (primary), `edit`, `reject`, `snooze`; payload for `edit` is `{title?, label?, estimate_minutes?, first_action?, acceptance_criteria?}` and `edit` saves then accepts.

Review UI keyboard map. The single-item keys are P1-13's rule (R-04: Enter is the kind's primary action, `o` open target, `e` edit, `r` reject, `s` snooze); P3-07 adds only the group and selection keys and the project picker:

| Key | Action | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `j` / `k` or arrows | Next / previous item | queue |
| `Enter` | Primary action: accept on `proposal` and `actionability_check`, answer on `project_match` (one keystroke, A3.3) | item |
| `e` | Edit focused proposal inline (title, label, estimate, first action), `Enter` saves and accepts | item |
| `r` | Reject; optional reason field, `Esc` skips the reason | item |
| `s` | Snooze 1 day (plan default) | item |
| `o` | Open the linked context inline (thread, note) | item |
| `x` | Toggle selection | item |
| `Shift+A` | Accept all non-duplicate items in the focused group | group |
| `Shift+R` | Reject all in the focused group | group |
| `p` | Pick project (on `project_match`), typeahead, `Enter` answers | item |
| `1` to `9` | Pick the numbered project suggestion (on `project_match`) | item |
| `u` | Undo last decision (session undo, UX 9) | queue |
| `?` | Show the key map | queue |

Groups: one per `source_key`, header shows source type, title (thread subject or meeting title and time), linked event, taint mark and count. Order: by the group's highest blocking impact (P1-13), ties by age. On the phone, groups collapse to cards with Accept all and per-item swipe or buttons.

**Implementation notes**
- Routing stays in Tumnis (P3-06) and reasoning stays in Hermes: the agent decides what the proposals are; Tumnis only stores, dedupes and shows them.
- Tainted in, tainted out (SAF-1): a proposal and the task it becomes are tainted, so they never run unattended (P4-04) and any run carrying them needs approval for every action.
- The agent's own dedupe (J5) and Tumnis's Noul check are both kept: the agent sees open task titles in the packet; Tumnis double-checks because the agent may miss one and because the check is logged and calibrated.
- Never auto-accept (UX 2, FR-5.8 spirit): even at confidence 1.0; T-P3-07-04 guards it.
- `get_context_item` in the drawer renders sanitized HTML only (SEC-4) and the plain text for notes; remote images stay blocked.
- The review list focuses the first item on load so `Enter` works without a click (A3.3); focus moves to the next item after a decision.
- Keyboard handlers ignore keys while an input is focused, except `Enter` and `Esc` in the inline editor.
- Measuring the exit gate: human seconds per captured task comes from `shown_at` to `decided_at`, only while the tab is visible (Page Visibility API), so a review left open overnight does not count.

- `POST /v1/test/fixtures/proposals` (fakes only) to create a pending proposal for UI tests.
- Skill cases with recorded packets built from the recordings.

**Risks and fallbacks**
- The agent posts vague proposals: the skill test asserts a concrete first action; P3-08 and review rejection feedback flow to the agent through the digest.
- A long email thread produces many proposals: SAF-5's per-run cap stops at 20; the skill is told to merge related asks.
- Bulk accept of a large group is slow: one transaction with batched inserts; a 50-proposal group is a query-count test (plan default bound 12 statements).

#### P3-08 · Calibration page and evaluation script

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.2 From item to proposal (week 13) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P1-02 |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-11.5, Quality: decision quality |

**Goal.** Give Scott evidence to tune thresholds: per decision point, accuracy once 100 labeled outcomes exist, what each threshold would have done, a log of threshold edits, a recheck flag when the model version changes, and an offline script that reproduces the same numbers from a stored set.

**Scope.** In: outcome labeling rules, metric functions in `decisions/rules.py`, the Calibration section in Settings, threshold edit with audit, recheck flag, `tumnis decisions eval`, the `decision_evals` table. Out: automatic threshold changes (never; a human edits them).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/decisions/rules.py` | edit | `label_outcome`, `accuracy`, `sweep`, `MIN_LABELED = 100` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/decisions/models.py` | edit | `thresholds.needs_recheck`, `thresholds_history`, `decision_evals(decision_point, model_version, set_sha256, metrics jsonb, run_at)` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/decisions/api.py`, `router.py` | edit | `GET /v1/decisions/calibration`, `PUT /v1/decisions/thresholds/{point}` (session only) |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/decisions/eval.py` | new | Evaluation engine shared by the page and the CLI |
| `backend/tumnis/cli.py` | edit | `tumnis decisions eval --set <path> [--from-log --since <date>]` |
| `backend/fixtures/decision_eval/*.jsonl` | new | Stored labeled sets per decision point |
| `frontend/src/components/settings/calibration/*` | new | Table and threshold editor |

**Interfaces**

```python
# decisions/rules.py (pure)
class Outcome(StrEnum): auto_applied = "auto_applied"; sent_to_review = "sent_to_review"; overridden = "overridden"; confirmed = "confirmed"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LabeledDecision:
    decision_point: str; model_version: str; provider: str
    answer: str; confidence: float; truth: str      # truth from the human's decision

def label_outcome(row: DecisionLogRow, human: HumanDecision | None, now: datetime,
                  settle_days: int = 7) -> LabeledDecision | None: ...
# review item decided -> truth = human answer; auto-applied then overridden -> truth = override;
# auto-applied, not overridden after settle_days (plan default) -> truth = answer; else None (unlabeled)

def accuracy(rows: Sequence[LabeledDecision], threshold: float) -> Metrics | None: ...
# None if len(rows) < MIN_LABELED (FR-11.5); Metrics(n, auto_rate, auto_precision, review_rate, overall_accuracy)

def sweep(rows: Sequence[LabeledDecision], thresholds: Sequence[float] = (0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95)) -> list[SweepRow]: ...
```

Stored set format (`backend/fixtures/decision_eval/<point>.jsonl`, one line per labeled decision): `{"decision_point", "model_version", "provider", "input_hash", "answer", "confidence", "truth"}`. No input text is stored, only the hash (Data flow rule 6 and SEC-6).

Page (Settings > Calibration): one row per decision point: labeled count, current threshold, auto-apply rate, precision of auto-applied answers, review rate, model version, recheck badge, a sweep table on expand, and an edit field with a required reason.

#### P3-09 · Retention and purge

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.2 From item to proposal (week 13) |
| Size | S (up to 1 agent-assisted day), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P3-02 |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | SAAS-2, FR-5.10, Data flow rule 3 |

**Goal.** Ingested email, chat and notes stay only as long as the user wants: a workspace retention setting purges old content on schedule, one action purges a project's or a source's content with its raw payloads, every purge is audited with a reason, and archived projects are compressed, never purged by retention.

**Scope.** In: retention setting, `retention_purge` scheduled workflow, per-project and per-connection purge actions, tombstoned ContextItems, search and embedding cleanup, audit. Out: archive compression itself (P2-18), hard workspace delete (designed, v1.1 export).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/rules.py` | edit | `purge_cutoff`, `purge_candidates` predicate |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/workflows.py` | edit | `retention_purge` (housekeeping schedule), `purge_scope` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/api.py`, `router.py` | edit | Extends the purge route P2-18 introduced (`POST /v1/purges`, session only, scope `project`): adds scope `connection` and `GET /v1/purges/{id}` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/integrations/models.py` | edit | `context_items.target_purged_at`; `purges(scope, target_id, reason, counts jsonb, status)` |
| `frontend/src/components/settings/retention/*`, `.../connections/PurgeDialog.tsx`, project Settings rail | new or edit | Setting and purge confirmations |

**Interfaces**

```python
class RetentionSetting(BaseModel):
    mode: Literal["keep_until_project_purged", "days"] = "keep_until_project_purged"   # SAAS-2 default
    days: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=7)                                        # minimum 7 is a plan default

def purge_cutoff(now: datetime, s: RetentionSetting) -> datetime | None: ...
def purge_candidates(item: IngestedLite, cutoff: datetime | None, project_archived: bool) -> bool:
    """True if older than cutoff, not archived, not linked to an open task (plan default: keep while a task is open)."""
```

Purge steps (each a DBOS step, idempotent): delete canonical rows (messages, threads, notes) in batches of 500 (plan default); delete their `raw_payloads`; delete search index rows; set `context_items.target_purged_at`; write counts; emit `data.purged` audit with actor, scope, reason and counts.

**Implementation notes**
- SAAS-2's default is keep until the project is purged; the days mode is opt-in.
- Items linked to an open task are kept past the cutoff so a task never loses its context mid-work (plan default; shown in the setting's help text).

- Backups still hold purged content until they expire (35-day B2 lifecycle, architecture); the purge dialog says so.

### M3.3 · Wider knowledge (weeks 13 to 14)

Each new source reuses the storage and connector contract suites, so most tests are new recordings, not new code.

#### P3-10 · Embeddings and hybrid search

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.3 Wider knowledge (weeks 13 to 14) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P1-17 |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-11.10, FR-15.3 |

**Goal.** Add semantic search to the knowledge base without losing what full-text search already does: chunks get vectors from the Embeddings slot, stored in pgvector with an HNSW index, and results from both lists are merged by reciprocal rank fusion with document, heading and page on every hit. A committed eval set with recorded vectors proves the merge is no worse than full-text alone.

**Scope.** In: Embeddings slot adapter (local vLLM default, hosted optional), `embeddings` table and index, embedding in extraction step 8, background re-embed on model change, local-only routing, `mode="hybrid"` added to P1-17's `search_knowledge(q, *, project_id, limit, mode)` (R-36) and used by `passages_for(task)` and the MCP tool, the eval set and `recall_at_k`. Out: reranking (not in the PRD), embedding ingested email or notes (FR-15.3 covers knowledge only).

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/decisions/adapters/embeddings/{vllm.py,hosted.py,fake.py}` | new | Embeddings slot adapters (OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings`) |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/decisions/api.py` | edit | `embed(texts, project_id) -> EmbedResult` with local-only routing |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/models.py` | edit | `embeddings` table, `embedding_models` table |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/migrations/xxxx_embeddings_hnsw.py` | new | Extension check, tables through P0-06's `create_tenant_table` (R-01), the default model's HNSW index |
| `backend/tumnis/cli.py` | edit | `tumnis embeddings index <model>` (owner role, run like `migrate`) creates a new model's partial HNSW index |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/rules.py` | edit | `rrf_merge`, `recall_at_k`, `RRF_K` |

**Interfaces**

DDL. The table is `embeddings(chunk_id, project_id, model, embedding vector)` (R-37): the column is an untyped `vector`, and each model gets a partial expression HNSW index cast to its own dimension, which pgvector supports for mixed dimensions in one column ([pgvector README](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector); HNSW indexes `vector` up to 2,000 dimensions). Both tables are created in `public` with P0-06's `create_tenant_table` (base columns, `created_by text` with `ACTOR_CHECK`, RLS; R-01); the SQL shows the resulting shape. The default model and its dimension are plan defaults (1,024 dimensions).

```sql
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;       -- present in pgvector/pgvector:pg18; migration asserts it

-- create_tenant_table("embedding_models", ...) adds the base columns
CREATE TABLE embedding_models ( /* base columns */
  model text NOT NULL, dims int NOT NULL CHECK (dims BETWEEN 1 AND 2000),
  provider text NOT NULL,                                                 -- 'vllm' | 'hosted:<name>'
  status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('building','active','retired')),
  index_name text,                                                        -- set once its HNSW index exists
  UNIQUE (workspace_id, model)
);

-- create_tenant_table("embeddings", ...)
CREATE TABLE embeddings ( /* base columns */
  chunk_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES chunks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  project_id uuid,                                   -- null = workspace knowledge base; copied for filtering
  model text NOT NULL,
  embedding vector NOT NULL,                         -- untyped; dimension checked against embedding_models.dims on write
  UNIQUE (workspace_id, chunk_id, model)
);
CREATE INDEX embeddings_ws_model_project ON embeddings (workspace_id, model, project_id);

-- one per model, created by the migration for the default model and by `tumnis embeddings index <model>` later
CREATE INDEX embeddings_hnsw_<model_slug> ON embeddings
  USING hnsw ((embedding::vector(1024)) vector_cosine_ops)
  WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64)                -- pgvector defaults, stated explicitly
  WHERE model = '<model>';
```

Vector query (per request, inside the RLS transaction; the cast and the model predicate must match the index exactly so the planner uses it):

```sql
SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search = 100;                      -- plan default (pgvector default 40)
SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order;       -- keeps recall when the project filter drops rows
SELECT e.chunk_id, e.embedding::vector(1024) <=> :q AS distance
FROM embeddings e
WHERE e.model = :active_model AND (e.project_id = :project_id OR e.project_id IS NULL)
ORDER BY e.embedding::vector(1024) <=> :q
LIMIT :candidates;                                   -- 50, plan default; the 1024 comes from embedding_models.dims
```

Fusion (pure):

```python
RRF_K = 60            # plan default: the constant from the original RRF paper (Cormack, Clarke and Buettcher, 2009)
CANDIDATES = 50       # per list, plan default

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Ranked: chunk_id: UUID; rank: int          # 1-based within its list

def rrf_merge(fulltext: Sequence[Ranked], vector: Sequence[Ranked], k: int = RRF_K,
              limit: int = 10) -> list[FusedHit]:
    """score(c) = sum over lists containing c of 1 / (k + rank). Ties break by better best-rank, then chunk_id."""

def recall_at_k(results: Mapping[str, Sequence[UUID]], expected: Mapping[str, set[UUID]], k: int = 5) -> float:
    """Mean over queries of |expected ∩ top_k| / min(k, |expected|)."""

class FusedHit(BaseModel):
    chunk_id: UUID; document_id: UUID; document_title: str
    heading_path: list[str]; page_from: int | None; page_to: int | None
    text: str; score: float; sources: set[Literal["fulltext", "vector"]]
```

Embeddings slot:

```python
class EmbeddingsAdapter(Protocol):
    model: str; dims: int; hosted: bool
    async def embed(self, texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]: ...
    async def health(self) -> Health: ...

# decisions.api.embed routing: project.local_decisions_only or workspace setting "embeddings_local_only"
# -> local adapter only; if the primary is hosted and no local adapter is configured, return EmbedResult(skipped=True)
```

Eval set format:

| File | Line shape |
| --- | --- |
| `corpus.jsonl` | `{"document_id", "title", "project": "acme"|null, "chunks": [{"chunk_id", "ordinal", "heading_path", "page_from", "page_to", "text"}]}` |
| `queries.jsonl` | `{"query_id", "text", "project": "acme", "expected_chunk_ids": [...], "kind": "keyword"|"paraphrase"|"mixed"}` |
| `vectors/chunks.jsonl` | `{"text_sha256", "model", "vector": [...]}` |
| `vectors/queries.jsonl` | `{"text_sha256", "model", "vector": [...]}` |

At least 40 queries (plan default), a third each of keyword, paraphrase and mixed. The fake embeddings adapter looks vectors up by SHA-256 of the exact text and raises on a miss, so a changed chunker shows up as a failing test rather than a silent drop.

**Implementation notes**
- Cosine distance (`<=>`) with `vector_cosine_ops`; most local embedding models are trained for cosine similarity. Keep the operator class and the query operator in one constant so they cannot drift.
- A new model needs its partial HNSW index before re-embedding starts. Creating an index needs the owner role, so the Settings screen shows the `tumnis embeddings index <model>` command (run like `migrate`), and `reembed_all` waits until `embedding_models.index_name` is set. The app role never runs DDL.
- `SET LOCAL` keeps the HNSW settings inside the request transaction, which is safe behind PgBouncer transaction pooling.
- Embeddings are computed in extraction step 8 (architecture); chunk text is sent, never the whole file.
- Data flow rule 6: a hosted embedder is optional and never receives a local-only project's text. The workspace knowledge base follows the workspace setting.
- Fusion ignores raw scores (FTS rank and cosine distance are not comparable); only ranks matter, which is why RRF fits.

- `backend/fixtures/search_eval/` as above, plus `README` describing how vectors were recorded (model, date, command).
- Fixture `load_eval_corpus(db)` inserting documents and chunks directly.
- `FakeEmbeddings(recorded_path, model, dims)`.

#### P3-11 · Google Docs source

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.3 Wider knowledge (weeks 13 to 14) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P3-02, P1-17 |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-15.8, FR-15.9 |

**Goal.** Link Google Docs, Sheets and Slides into a project's knowledge base with the Picker and the non-sensitive `drive.file` scope, keep them in sync through the Drive changes feed, export them to Markdown, XLSX and plain text, and show them read-only with an Open in source link. Folder mode with `drive.readonly` exists for self-hosted mode only.

**Scope.** In: incremental authorization of `drive.file` on an existing Google account connection, Picker flow in the browser, link records, sync via `changes.list`, export and extraction, trust rule, read-only enforcement, folder mode behind the deployment check. Out: write-back (v1.x), Drive files that are not Docs, Sheets or Slides (plan default: ignored in Picker mode; folder mode processes them like uploads).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/adapters/google_drive/{client,connector,mapper,fake}.py` | new | Drive v3 client (files.get, files.export, changes) |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/rules.py` | edit | `export_mime_for`, `drive_trust`, `folder_mode_allowed` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/api.py`, `router.py` | edit | `POST /v1/knowledge/sources/google/picks`, `DELETE /v1/knowledge/sources/google/picks/{id}`, `POST /v1/knowledge/sources/google/folders` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/calendar/api.py` | edit | Expose Google account connections and `request_scope(account, scope)` for incremental auth |
| `frontend/src/components/knowledge/GooglePicker.tsx` | new | Loads the Picker, gets a browser-only token, posts picks |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/tests/recordings/google_drive/*.json` | edit | `expected` blocks |

**Interfaces**

Picker flow (the browser gets its own short-lived token; server tokens never reach the browser):

1. User clicks "Link Google Docs" in the project's Knowledge rail and picks the Google account.
2. If the account's grant lacks `drive.file`, the app starts P3-02's `connect_oauth` for that Google connection with `include_granted_scopes=true` and scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` added (incremental authorization); the user approves once.
3. The component loads `gapi.load('picker', …)` and asks Google Identity Services for a browser token with scope `drive.file` and `login_hint` = the account email, using the same OAuth client ID as the server.
4. It builds the Picker: `new google.picker.PickerBuilder().addView(docsView).setOAuthToken(browserToken).setDeveloperKey(API_KEY).setAppId(PROJECT_NUMBER).setCallback(onPick).build()`, where `docsView` is a `DocsView` with `setMimeTypes('application/vnd.google-apps.document,application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet,application/vnd.google-apps.presentation')` ([Google Picker web guide](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/picker/guides/web-picker)). `setAppId` with the Cloud project number is what grants the app access to picked files.
5. On `google.picker.Action.PICKED`, the component posts `{connection_id, project_id, files: [{id, name, mimeType}]}` to `POST /v1/knowledge/sources/google/picks`; the browser token is discarded.
6. The worker's sync reads each picked file with the server grant, which now has `drive.file` access to it because the same app was granted the file.

```python
EXPORT_MIME = {   # FR-15.9, verified against Google's export formats reference
    "application/vnd.google-apps.document": "text/markdown",
    "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet",
    "application/vnd.google-apps.presentation": "text/plain",
}
def export_mime_for(mime_type: str) -> str | None: ...

def drive_trust(file: DriveFileMeta, connected_emails: set[str]) -> Trust:
    """trusted if any owner email is a connected account; otherwise tainted (FR-15.9, SAF-1)."""

def folder_mode_allowed(deployment_mode: str) -> bool:   # False in hosted mode
```

Mapping (Drive file to Document, via P1-17's document model):

| Document field | Drive source | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | constant | `synced` |
| `external_id` | `file.id` | unique with connection |
| `title` | `file.name` | |
| `source_revision` | `file.version` | Docs editor files have no `headRevisionId`; `version` increases on every change (verify in recordings) |
| `provider_url` | `file.webViewLink` | Open in source |
| `trust` / `tainted` | `drive_trust(owners)` | |
| `read_only` | constant | `true` (FR-15.8) |
| body | `files.export(mimeType=EXPORT_MIME[...])` | then P1-16's extraction (XLSX through Docling, Markdown and text directly) |

Cursor: `{"start_page_token": str}` per connection from `changes.getStartPageToken`; each sync pages `changes.list(pageToken=…)` until a response carries `newStartPageToken`, which becomes the saved cursor ([Drive changes guide](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/manage-changes)). A change for a file not linked to any project is ignored. A change with `removed: true` or `file.trashed` moves the Document to trash (FR-15.8). A change whose `version` equals the stored `source_revision` is skipped.

| T-P3-11-02 | `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/tests/integration/test_google_scopes.py::test_picker_mode_requests_only_drive_file` | integration | Incremental auth URL adds only `drive.file`; calendar scopes unchanged; never `drive.readonly` | FR-15.9 |

**Implementation notes**
- `drive.file` is non-sensitive and grants per-file access to what the user picked, so hosted mode needs no Google security assessment; `drive.readonly` is restricted ([Drive API scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/api-specific-auth)).
- The browser token is requested only for the Picker and never stored or sent to Tumnis. Verify in P3-01's Drive learning step that a server grant from the same OAuth client can read files picked through a browser token (same Cloud project, same user); if it cannot, fallback: the server issues a short-lived access token for `drive.file` only, obtained through a dedicated second grant, and the Picker uses that.
- Sheets export to XLSX keeps every tab; CSV export covers the first sheet only ([export formats](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/ref-export-formats)).
- Use `fields=` masks on every call (`id,name,mimeType,version,webViewLink,owners(emailAddress),trashed`) to keep payloads small.
- Folder mode (self-hosted only): a linked folder's children are listed with `q="'<folderId>' in parents"`; new children become documents in that project.

#### P3-12 · Obsidian source

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.3 Wider knowledge (weeks 13 to 14) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P3-02, P1-17 |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-15.10 |

**Goal.** Read an Obsidian vault as files, from a read-only mounted folder or a Git remote, and turn its notes into knowledge-base Documents mapped to projects by folder, frontmatter key or tag, with wikilinks kept as links between Documents, embeds and attachments processed, excluded folders skipped and web clippings tainted.

**Scope.** In: vault parser (pure), mapping rules, mounted-folder path (watch plus scan), Git path with a read-only deploy key, attachment handling through P1-16's pipeline. Out: the Mac daemon path (P1), write-back (v1.x), the Local REST API plugin (not the sync path, per FR-15.10).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/obsidian/parse.py` | new | Pure parser |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/obsidian/rules.py` | new | `map_note_to_project`, `is_excluded`, `note_trust` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/adapters/obsidian/{folder.py,git.py,fake.py}` | new | Two vault readers behind one interface |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/models.py` | edit | `document_links(from_document_id, to_document_id, to_target text, kind link|embed, heading, block)` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/tests/fixtures/vault/` | new | Fixture vault |
| `frontend/src/components/knowledge/ObsidianSetup.tsx` | new | Connection form and mapping preview |

**Interfaces**

Parsing rules (Obsidian syntax per [Obsidian Help: internal links](https://help.obsidian.md/links), [embeds](https://help.obsidian.md/embeds) and [tags](https://help.obsidian.md/tags); verify against current help pages):

| Construct | Pattern | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frontmatter | YAML between a leading `---` line and the next `---` | Parsed with a safe YAML loader; invalid YAML keeps the note, flags `frontmatter_error` |
| Tags | frontmatter `tags` (list or string) plus inline `#tag`, `#area/sub`: letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `/`, at least one non-digit; not inside code spans, code blocks, URLs or headings' `#` markers | Lowercased set on the Document |
| Headings | ATX `#` to `######` outside code blocks | Heading path for chunks (P1-16 chunker keeps it) |
| Wikilink | `[[Target]]`, `[[Target#Heading]]`, `[[Target#^block]]`, `[[Target\|Alias]]` | `document_links` row, kind `link`; target resolved by Obsidian's shortest-path rule (unique basename, else relative path) |
| Embed | `![[Target]]` with the same suffixes; `![[image.png\|300]]` | kind `embed`; a note embed links; an attachment embed enqueues the file for extraction |
| Markdown links | `[text](relative/path.md)` | Treated like a wikilink when the path is inside the vault |
| Excluded | `.obsidian/`, `.trash/`, the vault's templates folder (from `.obsidian/templates.json` if present, else `Templates/`) plus user excludes | Never read |
| Clippings | folder `Clippings/` by default, configurable | tainted |

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ParsedNote:
    path: str; title: str; frontmatter: Mapping[str, Any]; tags: frozenset[str]
    headings: tuple[tuple[int, str], ...]; links: tuple[Link, ...]; embeds: tuple[Link, ...]
    body: str                                   # frontmatter removed

def parse_note(path: str, text: str) -> ParsedNote: ...

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VaultMapping:
    folders: Mapping[str, str]                  # "Clients/Acme" -> project slug
    frontmatter_key: str = "tumnis_project"
    tag_prefix: str = "tumnis/"
    unmapped: Literal["workspace", "ignore"] = "workspace"
    clippings_folder: str = "Clippings"
    extra_excludes: tuple[str, ...] = ()

def map_note_to_project(note: ParsedNote, m: VaultMapping, known_projects: set[str]) -> str | None | Literal["ignore"]: ...
# precedence: frontmatter key, then #tumnis/<project> tag, then the longest matching folder prefix (plan default order)
def note_trust(path: str, m: VaultMapping) -> Trust: ...   # tainted under the clippings folder, else trusted

class VaultReader(Protocol):
    async def list_files(self) -> list[FileStat]: ...     # relative paths, size, mtime, content hash
    async def read(self, path: str) -> bytes: ...
    async def refresh(self) -> None: ...                  # git: fetch + reset; folder: no-op
```

Git path: clone into `/data/obsidian/<connection_id>/` owned by the worker; `refresh` runs `git fetch --depth 1 origin <branch>` then `git reset --hard FETCH_HEAD`, with `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -i <keyfile> -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile=<pinned>"`. On connect, `git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/tumnis-write-probe` must fail with a permission error; if it succeeds, the key can write and the connection is refused with `writable_deploy_key` (plan default check; GitHub rejects receive-pack for read-only deploy keys, verify on the homelab). Cadence 15 minutes (plan default).

Folder path: the vault is mounted read-only into the worker (`/vaults/<name>:ro`); `watchfiles` watches it for changes and a full scan every 15 minutes backs it up.

**Implementation notes**
- No Obsidian process is needed; the vault is plain files (FR-15.10).
- Wikilink resolution follows Obsidian's rule: a bare name resolves to the unique note with that basename; if several exist, Obsidian uses paths, so unresolved ambiguous links are stored with `to_document_id = null` and the raw target, and resolved on the next scan when possible.
- Attachments go through the same pipeline as uploads (type allow-list, 50 MB, ClamAV, extraction; SEC-10).
- Use `yaml.safe_load` only; frontmatter can contain anything.
- Hosted mode supports the Git path only (Hosted readiness): the folder option is hidden when `DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted`.

**Risks and fallbacks**
- Syncthing writes partial files during sync: debounce watch events 5 seconds (plan default) and skip files whose size changed between stat and read.
- Very large vaults: the first scan is batched, and extraction runs on `worker-extract` without starving other queues.
- Wikilink edge cases (non-Latin names, `.md` suffix in links): the parse table grows with each bug, each fix starting from a failing row.

#### P3-13 · S3 buckets as a source

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.3 Wider knowledge (weeks 13 to 14) |
| Size | S (up to 1 agent-assisted day), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | P1-14, P3-02 |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-15.11 |

**Goal.** Sync documents that already live in an S3-compatible bucket prefix into a project's knowledge base without re-uploading, using a read-only key that Tumnis checks where the provider allows it, indexing only the latest version, detecting changes by ETag and last-modified, and accepting MinIO bucket notifications only when they carry the configured token.

**Scope.** In: linked-source connector over P1-14's S3 client, key capability checks (Backblaze B2, MinIO), prefix-to-project mapping, change detection, versioned-bucket handling, MinIO webhook endpoint. Out: writing to the bucket (never for a linked source), project folders on S3 (P1-14, P1-15).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/adapters/s3_source/{connector,capability,fake}.py` | new | Listing, capability check |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/rules.py` | edit | `s3_change`, `capabilities_acceptable` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/router.py` | edit | `POST /v1/webhooks/minio/{connection_id}` (no session; token auth) |
| `frontend/src/components/knowledge/S3SourceSetup.tsx` | new | Endpoint, region, bucket, prefix map, path-style toggle, trust toggle |

**Interfaces**

```python
class KeyCapabilities(BaseModel):
    checked: bool                       # False when the provider offers no check
    can_read: bool | None; can_list: bool | None
    can_write: bool | None; can_delete: bool | None
    bucket_scoped: bool | None; prefix: str | None
    source: Literal["b2_authorize_account", "minio_account_info", "none"]

def capabilities_acceptable(c: KeyCapabilities) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    """Refuse if checked and (can_write or can_delete or not bucket_scoped); unchecked is accepted with a warning."""

def s3_change(prev: FolderFileLite | None, obj: S3ObjectLite) -> Literal["new", "changed", "unchanged", "deleted"]: ...
# changed if ETag differs, or ETag equal but last_modified newer and size differs (multipart ETags are not content hashes)
```

Capability checks:

| Provider | How | Refuse when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backblaze B2 | Call `b2_authorize_account` (native API v4, Basic auth with the same key ID and application key) and read the key's allowed capabilities, bucket and name prefix ([B2 authorize account](https://www.backblaze.com/apidocs/b2-authorize-account); verify the response path `apiInfo.storageApi.allowed` against the pinned API version) | `writeFiles` or `deleteFiles` present, or no bucket restriction |
| MinIO | Admin "account info" API for the key's own account, which reports its policy (verify that a non-admin key may call it on the pinned MinIO version) | Policy allows `s3:PutObject` or `s3:DeleteObject` on the prefix |
| AWS S3 and others | No check without IAM permissions | Accepted with a visible "Tumnis could not verify this key is read-only" warning |

Change detection: `ListObjectsV2` on the prefix every 15 minutes (FR-15.11), compared with `folder_files` rows for the connection. On versioned buckets `ListObjectsV2` returns only current versions, so only the latest is indexed; a delete marker shows as the key missing, which moves the Document to trash.

MinIO notifications: MinIO's webhook target has an `auth_token` setting ([MinIO webhook notifications](https://docs.min.io/aistor/administration/bucket-notifications/publish-events-to-webhook/)); Tumnis generates a random token per connection, shows the `mc admin config set` and `mc event add` commands, and the endpoint accepts a request only if its `Authorization` header matches the token (constant-time compare; MinIO sends it as a bearer token, verify on the pinned version). **Deviation, flagged for Scott:** the YAML says "MinIO notification signatures are verified", but MinIO's webhook target does not sign the body; it only sends the configured token. The plan verifies that token and treats it as the signature; if a real body signature is required, the fallback is a small signing relay beside MinIO, which the plan does not build. A valid notification never trusts its body: it only enqueues a `HEAD` plus re-list of the named key, so a forged event can cause a stat and nothing else.

| T-P3-13-02 | `backend/tumnis/modules/knowledge/tests/contract/test_b2_capability.py::test_recorded_b2_keys` | contract | Recorded authorize responses for a read-only and a read-write key map to the right capabilities | FR-15.11 |

**Implementation notes**
- Backblaze B2 uses `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, an application key (never the master key) and Signature V4 (FR-15.11); the form rejects a key ID that looks like a master key ID (B2 master key IDs are the account ID, 12 hex characters, plan default heuristic, verify).
- aioboto3 client config: `signature_version="s3v4"`, `s3={"addressing_style": "path"}` when path-style is on ([aioboto3](https://aioboto3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage.html), [botocore config](https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html)).
- The webhook route is exempt from session auth and CSRF but is in the route registry with auth policy `webhook_token` and a body size limit (P0-10 sweep).
- The notification path is optional; the 15-minute listing is the source of truth.

#### P3-14 · Existing folders, shares and SFTP

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M3.3 Wider knowledge (weeks 13 to 14) |
| Size | L (3 to 4 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl + impl-2 |
| Needs | P1-15 |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-15.7, FR-15.12 |

**Goal.** Let a project live in a folder the user already keeps, on a mounted SMB or NFS share, on SFTP, or on S3, with Tumnis writing only inside a `Tumnis/` subfolder and never renaming, moving, overwriting or deleting a file it did not create unless the user confirms a delete; add the SFTP backend with a pinned host key; and move a project between locations safely.

**Scope.** In: SFTP backend passing P1-14's storage contract suite; share support as a server path with scan-based change detection and the marker check; existing-folder setup and write rules; the delete-confirmation flow; host-key pinning; the move job. Out: Mac folders (P1, runner daemon), archive packing (P2-18 already covers existing folders by archiving the index only).

**Interfaces**

```python
# knowledge/rules.py (pure)
class ActorKind(StrEnum): user = "user"; agent = "agent"; system = "system"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WritePolicy:
    mode: Literal["tumnis_made", "existing"]
    tumnis_subdir: str = "Tumnis/"          # FR-15.12

def may_write(p: WritePolicy, path: str, origin: Literal["tumnis", "external"] | None) -> bool:
    """existing mode: only paths under Tumnis/, and never over a file whose origin is external.
       tumnis_made: anywhere in the root, never over an external file."""

def may_rename(p: WritePolicy, src_origin: str) -> bool: ...       # external files: never
def may_delete(p: WritePolicy, origin: str, actor: ActorKind, confirmed_by_user: bool) -> Literal["trash", "delete_at_source", "index_only", "refuse"]:
    """tumnis origin: trash (.tumnis/trash/ in a Tumnis-made folder; Tumnis/.trash/ in an existing folder,
       so nothing is written outside Tumnis/). external origin: agent -> refuse;
       user without confirmation -> index_only; user with confirmation -> delete_at_source."""
```

SFTP backend ([asyncssh API](https://asyncssh.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html); verify argument forms against the pinned version):

```python
class SftpStorage(StorageBackend):
    def __init__(self, host: str, port: int, username: str, private_key_pem: bytes,
                 pinned_host_key: str, root: str) -> None: ...

    async def _connect(self) -> asyncssh.SSHClientConnection:
        known = asyncssh.import_known_hosts(f"[{self.host}]:{self.port} {self.pinned_host_key}\n")
        return await asyncssh.connect(
            self.host, self.port, username=self.username,
            client_keys=[asyncssh.import_private_key(self.private_key_pem)],
            known_hosts=known, password=None, agent_path=None,     # key auth only (FR-15.7)
            connect_timeout=10)
    # write: upload to "<dir>/.tumnis-tmp-<uuid>", compare size+mtime+hash of the target with if_match
    #        just before, then sftp.posix_rename(tmp, target) (atomic replace where the server supports
    #        the posix-rename extension; else refuse with a conflict)
    # every path: normalized, confined to root, and lstat'd; symlinks are refused (never followed)

async def probe_host_key(host: str, port: int) -> ProbedKey:
    key = await asyncssh.get_server_host_key(host, port)
    return ProbedKey(openssh=key.export_public_key().decode().strip(),
                     sha256=key.get_fingerprint("sha256"))
```

Host-key pinning flow: `POST /v1/storage/locations {kind: "sftp", host, port, username, private_key}` stores the location as `pending_host_key` and enqueues `probe_host_key` (through the SSRF guard's resolved address); the UI polls and shows `SHA256:…`; the user compares it with the server's own fingerprint (`ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`, shown as a hint) and confirms with `POST /v1/storage/locations/{id}/host-key {sha256}`; only an exact match pins it. Any later connection presenting another key fails, marks the location `host_key_changed`, writes audit `storage.host_key_mismatch`, adds a review item and never re-pins automatically; re-pinning is the same confirm flow with a reason.

Existing folder setup: `POST /v1/projects/{id}/folder {mode: "existing", location_id, path}` indexes everything found (as `origin=external`, tainted until trusted per FR-15.5 and FR-15.12), creates `Tumnis/` with `uploads/`, `notes/`, `agent-outputs/` and `.trash/` inside it, and writes nothing else. On a share, the `.tumnis-root` marker at the share root is placed by the user and only checked by Tumnis (FR-15.12).

Move job:

```python
@DBOS.workflow()
def move_project_folder(workspace_id: UUID, project_id: UUID, to_location: UUID, to_path: str) -> None:
    files = list_source_step(...)                      # snapshot with hashes
    for batch in chunks(files, 100):                   # plan default batch
        copy_batch_step(batch)                         # write to target, compute hash on the fly
    verify_step(files)                                 # re-read target hashes; any mismatch -> fail, source untouched
    switch_step(project_id, to_location, to_path)      # one transaction: project folder pointer, folder_files rows
    record_old_copy_step(project_id)                   # old location kept; review item "Remove old copy?"
```
