**Implementation notes**
- Review kinds, registered with `register_review_kind` (R-03): `storage_host_key_changed` (actions `accept` = re-pin through the confirm flow, `snooze`) and `folder_move_old_copy` (actions `accept` = keep, `reject` = remove the old copy after a typed confirmation, `snooze`).
- `posix_rename` needs the server's `posix-rename@openssh.com` extension; OpenSSH has it. If a server lacks it, plain `rename` fails when the target exists, which is the safe outcome (conflict, then retry through the sync engine), never delete-then-rename.
- Never follow symlinks: resolve with `lstat` on each path segment, refuse a symlink anywhere under the root (FR-15.12). This costs round trips; cache directory `lstat`s for one scan.
- Hash on SFTP means reading the file; scans compare size and mtime first and hash only when those differ (FR-15.12).
- A chrooted SFTP user scoped to the folder is the recommended credential (FR-15.12); the form says so, and the connection test lists the root to confirm the scope.
- Deletes of external files happen only from a user's session with an explicit confirmation token issued by the dialog (`POST /v1/knowledge/documents/{id}/delete-at-source {confirm_token, reason}`); the MCP surface has no such tool, and `knowledge.api` refuses agent actors regardless of scope.
- Existing folders are not in the nightly B2 copy unless the user opts in per project (FR-15.12, P1-15).
- Hosted mode: server paths and shares are hidden; SFTP and S3 only (FR-15.7).

**Fixtures, fakes and data**
- P0-02's `sftp_server` fixture (R-17) is reused; this WP adds two helpers to it: `rotate_host_key()` and `plant_symlink(path, target)`.
- Share simulation: server path in `tmp_path` with `kind="share"`; dropped mount simulated by removing the marker and unmounting nothing.
- Fault injection hook in `copy_batch_step` for T-P3-14-15 (test-only setting).

- [ ] Storage contract suite green on SFTP and share

- [ ] Outside files never renamed, moved, overwritten or deleted without confirmation
- [ ] Move job verified by hash and old copy kept
- [ ] Full coverage on the write-policy rules

**Risks and fallbacks**
- SMB mounts report coarse mtimes: the scan falls back to hashing when size is equal and mtime granularity is 2 seconds or worse.
- SFTP servers without `posix-rename`: writes over existing Tumnis files become conflict copies; the location health shows "limited writes".
- A user mounts a share at the wrong path: the marker check keeps Tumnis from writing into the server's own disk; setup refuses a share without the marker.

**A4.4 · README install reaches a healthy app on a clean VM**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |

| Runs | on PRs touching `README.md`, `deploy/**` or `scripts/readme_test.py`; nightly; and as a required check on the release tag |
| Turns green with | P4-06 |

Preconditions: a GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runner (a fresh VM for every job, plan default for "clean VM"); nothing installed beyond the runner image; the repository checked out at the commit under test and served to the README steps as if cloned.

Steps:
1. The harness extracts every block tagged `readme:install` in document order and fails if any shell block inside the "Install" section is untagged.
2. It runs each block in a fresh `bash -euo pipefail` with the block's timeout, substituting only the variables the README itself defines (for example `TUMNIS_HOST=localhost` from a `readme:env` block).
3. After the last block it polls `https://localhost/health/ready` (the README's own URL, with the certificate created by the README's TLS step) until 200 or 10 minutes.
4. It runs the Playwright `@smoke` spec against the installed app at phone width: the first-run setup page loads.
5. It runs `readme:first-run` blocks (non-interactive setup with a generated password and TOTP secret) and asserts sign-in works through the API.

Assertions: every block exits 0; `/health/ready` returns 200 with every core module `ok` and connector modules `not_configured` (not `degraded`); total time is recorded as a job summary.

```python
# focus/rules.py
def current_guardrail_task(plan: Sequence[PlanItemLite], tasks: Mapping[UUID, TaskLite]) -> UUID | None:
    """The In progress task if one is in Today; else the first accepted plan item (by position)
       whose task is not Done and not waiting on the human; else None."""

def next_guardrail_task(plan, tasks, current: UUID | None) -> UUID | None:
    """The plan item after `current` by the same rule; used for preloading."""

def is_detour(to_task_id: UUID | None, today_task_ids: frozenset[UUID]) -> bool:
    """True for free text (no task) or a task not in Today."""
```

```python
# focus/api.py: P2-15's respond body gains one optional field
class DetourIn(BaseModel):
    title: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    project_id: UUID                         # user picks; required (J2 rule: only agents skip the project)

class RespondIn(BaseModel):                  # P2-15's model: {event_id, response, to_task_id?}
    ...
    detour: DetourIn | None = None           # only with response="switched"; exclusive with to_task_id

class ReturnIn(BaseModel):
    decision: Literal["return", "stay"]
    version: int

# respond(): at Guardrail with response "switched" and is_detour(...): create the task through
# tasks.api.create_task (actor user, source "detour", status backlog, label from Jev per P1-07), move it to
# In progress with tasks.api.change_status (R-10), emit focus.event(kind="switched", detour_task_id,
# return_to_task_id, rule="guardrail.detour"); the previous task goes back to Today (not Backlog).
```

Dashboard UI rules at Guardrail:

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| One card | Title, project, label, estimate, first action, linked context expanded, Start or Done, Switched, Stuck |
| Hidden | Other Today items (only a count, "2 more today"), project cards, activity feed, the review badge count stays (FR-8.1 source of truth) |
| Visible | Calendar strip (time blindness, FR-1.3), quick-add, focus bar, "Show everything for now" (lowers today's level one step, FR-10.9) |
| Reveal | On Done the next card slides in; no list animation when reduced motion is on |
| Empty | "Nothing planned. Re-plan?" with the Re-plan button (FR-4.3) |
| Phone | Same card full width; Start and Done in the bottom third |

Keyboard (plan default): `Enter` Start or Done (context-sensitive), `w` Switched, `!` Stuck (`k` is list navigation elsewhere), `Esc` closes the picker. "Show everything for now" and "less of this" call P2-15's `POST /v1/focus/less`.

**Implementation notes**
- Capture happens in Tumnis at the user's request, and the master phrases the return question (FR-10.3: Tumnis detects, the master speaks). This keeps capture working when the master is offline; the prompt then uses a fixed template with rule attribution.
- A detour task is created by the user, so it is untainted and gets a normal Jev label; it lands in Backlog when the user returns, never in Today (Today stays at most 5, UX 3).
- Prefetch uses TanStack Query's `prefetchQuery` with the same query keys the drawer uses, so the next card renders from cache ([TanStack Query prefetching](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/prefetching)).
- The review badge count stays visible at Guardrail because the badge is the source of truth for items needing the human (FR-8.1); its list is one tap away.
- Nothing at any level blocks the UI or requires an answer (FR-10.9): the return prompt dismisses itself after 2 minutes (plan default) and counts as Stay.

#### P4-02 · Stuck handling

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M4.1 Finish the loop (weeks 15 to 16) |
| Size | S (up to 1 agent-assisted day), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | none |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-10.5 |

**Goal.** When the user answers "stuck", the project agent either splits off a first step of 10 minutes or less as a Human subtask or takes the next AI-able step itself and reports back, and the user sees the new step within a minute.

**Scope.** In: `handle_stuck` subscriber and workflow, which requests the run through P2-04's `agents.api.request_run(task_id, RunKind.STUCK, priority=…)` (R-23; allowed for any task label, including Human) with the packet from `build_packet(RunKind.STUCK)` (R-24), the stuck body fields, server-side 10-minute rule, priority on the runs queue, the template's `stuck` skill, UI update through `/ws`, the fallback when no answer arrives in 60 seconds. Builds on P2-04 (dispatch), P2-15 (the `stuck` response and event) and P2-12 (template skills). Out: master involvement (FR-10.5 routes to the project agent).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/agents/workflows.py` | edit | `handle_stuck` workflow |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/agents/events.py` | edit | Subscribe to `focus.event` with `kind="stuck"` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/agents/packet_builder.py` | edit | Stuck body fields in `build_packet(RunKind.STUCK)`: recent comments and the `stuck_step` limits (P2-02's builder, R-24) |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/tasks/api.py` | edit | Stuck-run `create_task` rule |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/focus/api.py` | edit | `current()` includes `next_step` |
| `profiles/project-template/skills/stuck/SKILL.md` | new | Skill |
| `profiles/tests/cases/stuck_*.yaml` | new | Cases |
| `frontend/src/components/focus/StuckPanel.tsx` | new | "Working on a first step…" then the step |

**Interfaces**

```python
STUCK_MAX_MINUTES = 10        # FR-10.5
STUCK_DEADLINE_S = 60         # FR-10.5 "within a minute"; default of settings.stuck_deadline_seconds, short in tests (R-30)

STUCK_PRIORITY = 1           # plan default; highest priority in the project's partition (verify the priority order and
                             # the queue's priority flag against the pinned DBOS version, R-30)

# started by the focus.event(kind="stuck") subscriber with SetWorkflowID(f"stuck:{focus_event_id}"), so a
# double tap starts one workflow
@DBOS.workflow()
def handle_stuck(workspace_id: UUID, task_id: UUID, focus_event_id: UUID) -> StuckOutcome:
    run_id = request_stuck_run_step(workspace_id, task_id, focus_event_id)
    #   step body: await agents.api.request_run(task_id, RunKind.STUCK, priority=STUCK_PRIORITY)
    #   request_run creates the runs row and enqueues dispatch_run(run_id) with SetWorkflowID(run_id)
    #   and the project partition key (R-23); a 409 run_already_active returns that run's id instead
    outcome = DBOS.recv("stuck_outcome", timeout_seconds=stuck_deadline_s())   # workflow body only (R-30);
    #   configurable, 60 s by default (FR-10.5), short in tests
    if outcome is None:
        mark_fallback_step(task_id)          # focus bar: "Agent still working"; shows the task's first action with a 10-minute timer
    return outcome or StuckOutcome.pending
```

The hooks in `create_task` and `post_result` for a `stuck` run call `DBOS.send(f"stuck:{focus_event_id}", outcome, topic="stuck_outcome")`; sending from a handler is allowed, receiving is not (R-30).

Stuck packet: built by `build_packet(RunKind.STUCK, task_id=…, run_id=…, token=…, nonce=…)` inside `dispatch_run`, never by hand (R-24). It has P2-02's schema: the `TaskRunRequest` body with the task (title, first action, acceptance criteria, estimate) and linked context in nonce'd `<untrusted-data id="u-<nonce>">` blocks (taint per SAF-1); `policy` with P2-02's action classes split into `gated` and `allowed`, plus `max_tasks_per_run: 1`; `callback` with `mcp_url`, `rest_base_url` and the task token. P4-02 adds two fields to the stuck body: `recent_comments` (last 5, plan default) and `stuck_step: {max_minutes: 10}`.

Server rule inside `create_task` when the caller's run has `kind="stuck"`: `parent_id` must equal the stuck task; label Human or Hybrid needs `estimate_minutes <= 10` (422 `stuck_step_too_long` otherwise); AI steps carry no estimate (FR-3.1) and are allowed; only one subtask per stuck run (SAF-5 style limit of 1).

**Implementation notes**
- "Within a minute" depends on a free agent slot (SAF-5: 2 runs per project). Priority gets the stuck run to the head of the partition; if both slots stay busy past 60 seconds, the fallback shows and the step lands when a slot frees.
- The project agent may be offline: the fallback is immediate (no 60-second wait) when the profile's health is down, mirroring FR-4.6's degraded mode.
- The stuck run inherits the task's taint; on a tainted task the agent can still post a subtask (creating a task is not a gated action), but any other action needs approval (SAF-1).
- The response "stuck" is already recorded by P2-15 and reaches the digest there.

#### P4-03 · Speech slot and voice mode

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M4.1 Finish the loop (weeks 15 to 16) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | none |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-10.8, FR-11.7 |

**Goal.** Focus messages can be spoken. The PWA speaks with the browser's speech synthesis by default; a local Piper engine on the agent server is available through the Speech slot for better voices; hosted speech exists but is off by default. A `voiceMode` machine queues messages so two never talk over each other.

**Scope.** In: Speech slot TTS adapters (Piper HTTP, hosted optional, fake), TTS contract suite, voice settings (on per level, engine), server-side clips for the Piper path, the `voiceMode` XState machine and engines in the PWA. Builds on P1-01's slot framework and P2-16's delivery. Out: speech-to-text and voice replies (v1.1, FR-10.8), desktop voice (v1.1).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/decisions/adapters/speech/{piper.py,hosted.py,fake.py,base.py}` | new | `SpeechTTS` adapters |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/decisions/api.py` | edit | `speak(text, voice, workspace) -> Clip` |

**Interfaces**

```python
class SpeechTTS(Protocol):
    name: str; hosted: bool
    async def synthesize(self, text: str, voice: str | None = None) -> bytes: ...   # WAV
    async def health(self) -> Health: ...

MAX_SPOKEN_CHARS = 1_000     # plan default
TTS_TIMEOUT_S = 5            # plan default
CLIP_TTL_MIN = 60            # plan default

class VoiceSettings(BaseModel):
    enabled_levels: set[FocusLevel] = set()                 # opt-in per level (FR-10.8); empty = off
    engine: Literal["browser", "server"] = "browser"        # browser is the zero-config default (FR-11.7)
    server_provider: Literal["piper", "hosted"] = "piper"
    hosted_allowed: bool = False                            # off by default; refused for local-only projects
```

Piper adapter: `POST {endpoint}/synthesize` with JSON `{"text": …, "voice": …}` returning WAV, per Piper's HTTP server (`python3 -m piper.http_server -m <voice>`, default port 5000) ([Piper HTTP API](https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl/blob/main/docs/API_HTTP.md), verify against the pinned version). The endpoint is on the agent server and goes through the SSRF guard with a private-range allow-list entry.

`voiceMode` machine (XState v5 `setup(...).createMachine`, [XState setup](https://stately.ai/docs/setup)):

```ts
type VoiceMessage = { id: string; text: string; clipUrl?: string };
type Ctx = { queue: VoiceMessage[]; current?: VoiceMessage; spokenIds: string[] };
type Ev =
  | { type: 'ENABLE' } | { type: 'DISABLE' }
  | { type: 'SAY'; message: VoiceMessage }
  | { type: 'SKIP' };

export const voiceMode = setup({
  types: {} as { context: Ctx; events: Ev },
  actors: { speak: fromPromise<void, VoiceMessage>(async ({ input, signal }) => engine.speak(input, signal)) },
  guards: { hasQueued: ({ context }) => context.queue.length > 0 },
  actions: {                                   // every action the machine names is declared here (R-38)
    enqueueIfNew: assign({
      queue: ({ context, event }) => {
        if (event.type !== 'SAY') return context.queue;
        const id = event.message.id;
        const seen = context.spokenIds.includes(id) || context.current?.id === id || context.queue.some((m) => m.id === id);
        return seen ? context.queue : [...context.queue, event.message];
      },
    }),
    takeHead: assign({ current: ({ context }) => context.queue[0], queue: ({ context }) => context.queue.slice(1) }),
    markSpoken: assign({
      spokenIds: ({ context }) => (context.current ? [...context.spokenIds, context.current.id].slice(-50) : context.spokenIds),
      current: () => undefined,
    }),
    clearQueue: assign({ queue: () => [], current: () => undefined }),
  },
}).createMachine({
  id: 'voiceMode', initial: 'off', context: { queue: [], spokenIds: [] },
  states: {
    off: { on: { ENABLE: 'idle' } },                                   // SAY ignored while off
    idle: {
      always: { guard: 'hasQueued', target: 'speaking' },
      on: { SAY: { actions: 'enqueueIfNew' }, DISABLE: 'off' },
    },
    speaking: {
      entry: 'takeHead',
      invoke: { src: 'speak', input: ({ context }) => context.current!,
                onDone: { target: 'idle', actions: 'markSpoken' },
                onError: { target: 'idle', actions: 'markSpoken' } },   // an engine error never blocks the queue
      on: { SAY: { actions: 'enqueueIfNew' }, SKIP: { target: 'idle', actions: 'markSpoken' },   // leaving stops the actor, whose signal aborts the engine
            DISABLE: { target: 'off', actions: 'clearQueue' } },
    },
  },
});
```

Engines: `browserEngine.speak` wraps `speechSynthesis.speak(new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(text))` and resolves on `onend` or `onerror`, cancels on abort ([MDN SpeechSynthesis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SpeechSynthesis)); `clipEngine.speak` plays `clipUrl` in an `HTMLAudioElement`, resolving on `ended`. The machine, not the engine, guarantees one message at a time.

#### P4-04 · Unattended run windows

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M4.1 Finish the loop (weeks 15 to 16) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | none |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-4.5, SAF-1, J7 |

**Goal.** Let the user queue AI tasks to run while they sleep. A window set in the workspace timezone opens, the scheduler dispatches only green-light, untainted AI tasks within the project limits, refuses the rest with a reason, and the results wait for the morning review instead of interrupting anyone. The day close shows what is queued.

**Scope.** In: the window setting (workspace, with a per-project override in the Schedule rail), the per-task "run unattended" queue flag, the green-light rule, `unattended_tick`, batching of results and notifications, day-close listing. Builds on P2-08's pure `may_run_unattended(task)`, P2-04's `agents.api.request_run` (R-23), P2-09's pause and limits, P1-18's day close and P2-16's notifications. Out: budgets (v1.1).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/planning/rules.py` | edit | `window_open`, `window_bounds`, `green_light`, `batch_release_at` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/planning/models.py` | edit | `unattended_windows(project_id null, weekdays int[], start_local, end_local)` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/tasks/models.py` | edit | `tasks.unattended_queued_at`, `unattended_queued_by` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/tasks/api.py` | edit | `queue_unattended`, `may_run_unattended_for(task_id)` wrapping P2-08's rule |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/planning/workflows.py` | edit | `unattended_tick` |
| `backend/tumnis/worker.py` | edit | Schedule `*/5 * * * *` for `unattended_tick` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/notifications/rules.py` | edit | `overnight` batch |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/planning/router.py` | edit | `GET/PUT /v1/unattended/window`; P1-18's `GET /v1/day/{date}/summary` gains `queued_unattended` (R-37) |
| `frontend/src/components/project/ScheduleRail.tsx`, `task/RunUnattendedToggle.tsx`, `dayclose/*` | edit or new | UI |

**Interfaces**

```python
# planning/rules.py (pure; now and tz passed in)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Window: weekdays: frozenset[int]; start_local: time; end_local: time   # end < start means it crosses midnight

def window_bounds(w: Window, now: datetime, tz: ZoneInfo) -> tuple[datetime, datetime] | None:
    """The window instance containing `now` (UTC bounds), or None. A crossing window belongs to the weekday it starts on.
       On DST days bounds come from local wall times, so a 22:00 to 06:00 window is 7 or 9 hours long."""

def window_open(w: Window, now: datetime, tz: ZoneInfo) -> bool: ...

class Refusal(StrEnum):
    tainted = "tainted"; not_ai = "not_ai"; paused = "paused"; kill_switch = "kill_switch"
    no_acceptance_criteria = "no_acceptance_criteria"; not_queued = "not_queued"; done = "done"
    waiting_on_human = "waiting_on_human"

def green_light(t: TaskLite, *, may_run_unattended: bool, project_paused: bool, kill_switch: bool) -> Refusal | None:
    """None means it may run. Order: kill_switch, paused, not_queued, done, not_ai, tainted (from may_run_unattended,
       SAF-1), waiting_on_human, no_acceptance_criteria."""

def batch_release_at(window_end: datetime, working_hours_start: datetime) -> datetime:
    """Results notify at the first working-hours start after the window, minus 15 minutes (plan default)."""
```

Green light definition (plan default reading of FR-4.5 "AI-eligible tasks with a green light"): label AI, queued by the user for unattended running, acceptance criteria present, not tainted, project not paused, kill switch off. Hybrid and Human tasks cannot be queued (`queue_unattended` returns 422 `not_ai`).

```python
# Registered in worker.py: {"schedule_name": "unattended-tick", "workflow_fn": unattended_tick,
#                          "schedule": "*/5 * * * *", "context": None} in DBOS.apply_schedules (see A9)
@DBOS.workflow()
def unattended_tick(scheduled: datetime, context: object) -> None:
    for ws in workspaces_with_open_window_step(scheduled):          # per workspace timezone
        for t in queued_tasks_step(ws):                          # ordered by queued time
            refusal = green_light(...)
            if refusal: record_refusal_step(ws, t, refusal)      # review item once per task per night
            elif remaining_before_end(t, window_end) < project.max_run_minutes / 2: continue   # plan default: do not start a run that cannot finish
            else:
                start_unattended_step(ws, t.id)
                # step body, one transaction: clear tasks.unattended_queued_at (the flag is consumed, so a later
                # tick cannot start it again), then await agents.api.request_run(t.id, RunKind.TASK, unattended=True)
                # (R-23). request_run creates the runs row and enqueues dispatch_run(run_id) with
                # SetWorkflowID(run_id) and the project partition key; its 409 run_already_active and
                # agents_paused refusals are recorded as refusals, not errors.
```

SAF-5 and R-29 apply unchanged: at most 2 concurrent runs per project, an active-time cap of 60 minutes that excludes time waiting on a human, and a 24-hour wall-clock ceiling (plan default, flagged for Scott). A gated action during an unattended run parks on `request_approval` until the human answers in the morning; the approval has no deadline (P2-05), and the parked time does not count against the 60-minute cap.

**Implementation notes**
- The refusal item is the `unattended_refused` review kind, registered with `register_review_kind` (R-03; actions `accept` = unqueue, `snooze`) and raised with `dedupe_key=f"unattended:{task_id}:{window_start}"`; overnight results keep P2-04's `result` kind with `payload.batch = "overnight"`.
- P2-08 owns `may_run_unattended(task)` as a pure rule; planning reaches it through `tasks.api.may_run_unattended_for` (module boundary rule 1).
- The tick runs every 5 minutes like `planner_tick`, so a window opens at most 5 minutes late (plan default); DST can never shift it because bounds are computed from local wall time on each tick.
- Nothing about unattended runs relaxes approval: gated actions still wait for a human, which is why results "batch into the morning review".
- The success metric "unattended overnight runs completed, at least 3 per week" is counted from runs with `unattended: true` and status finished; add the counter to P1-18's metrics page.

**Risks and fallbacks**
- A run parks on an approval all night and holds one of the project's two slots: the 60-minute active cap does not end it, because waiting on a human is excluded (R-29); the 24-hour wall-clock ceiling is the backstop. The other slot keeps serving the project, and the day close lists parked runs so the morning review starts with them.
- The user queues many tasks: 2 per project at a time, in queued order; the day close shows the order.

#### P4-05 · Browser push

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M4.1 Finish the loop (weeks 15 to 16) |
| Size | S (up to 1 agent-assisted day), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | none |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | FR-8.3 |

**Goal.** Send the same events that reach Discord as browser push notifications from the PWA, each deep-linking to its review item through validated route params, and following the focus level's volume rules.

**Scope.** In: VAPID key generation per workspace, subscription endpoints, the `WebPush` adapter, push as a channel in `notifications` with P2-16's level and batching rules, the service worker's push and click handlers, the permission prompt UX. Out: native notifications (v1.1 desktop client).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/notifications/adapters/webpush/{client.py,fake.py}` | new | pywebpush wrapper |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/notifications/models.py` | edit | `push_subscriptions(user_id, endpoint, p256dh, auth, user_agent, last_success_at, failures)` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/notifications/rules.py` | edit | `push_payload`, `deep_link_for`, `endpoint_allowed` |
| `backend/tumnis/modules/notifications/router.py` | edit | `GET /v1/push/vapid-public-key`, `POST /v1/push/subscriptions`, `DELETE /v1/push/subscriptions/{id}` |
| `frontend/src/sw.ts` | edit | `push` and `notificationclick` handlers (vite-plugin-pwa `injectManifest`) |
| `frontend/src/lib/push.ts` | new | Subscribe flow |
| `frontend/src/routes/review.tsx` | edit | Existing zod search schema reused by the service worker build |

**Interfaces**

```python
class PushPayload(BaseModel):          # minimal text: push services are third parties (Data flow rule 6)
    schema_version: Literal[1] = 1
    kind: str                          # a registered review kind (R-05): approval, question, result, proposal, ...
    title: str                         # "Waiting on you: approval in Acme site"
    body: str                          # plain words, no email, chat or note content (plan rule)
    url: str                           # "/review?kind=approval&item=<uuid>"
    tag: str                           # review item id, so a newer push replaces an older one

def deep_link_for(item: ReviewItemLite) -> str: ...
def endpoint_allowed(endpoint: str) -> bool:
    """https only and host in the push-service allow-list (plan default: fcm.googleapis.com,
       updates.push.services.mozilla.com, *.push.apple.com, *.notify.windows.com)."""

class WebPushAdapter(Protocol):
    async def send(self, sub: PushSubscription, payload: PushPayload, ttl_s: int) -> PushResult: ...
```

Real adapter: `pywebpush.webpush(subscription_info=…, data=payload.model_dump_json(), vapid_private_key=<workspace key>, vapid_claims={"sub": "mailto:<workspace owner email>"}, ttl=…)` in `asyncio.to_thread` with a timeout ([pywebpush](https://github.com/web-push-libs/pywebpush), verify the key argument form against the pinned version). A `WebPushException` with status 404 or 410 deletes the subscription; others count failures and retry through the delivery attempts table.

VAPID keys: generated on first enable with `cryptography` (EC P-256), private key encrypted in `workspace_settings`, public key served base64url-encoded for `pushManager.subscribe({ userVisibleOnly: true, applicationServerKey })`.

Service worker handlers:

```ts
self.addEventListener('push', (e: PushEvent) => {
  const p = PushPayloadSchema.safeParse(e.data?.json());
  if (!p.success) return;
  e.waitUntil(self.registration.showNotification(p.data.title, { body: p.data.body, tag: p.data.tag, data: { url: p.data.url } }));
});
self.addEventListener('notificationclick', (e: NotificationEvent) => {
  e.notification.close();
  e.waitUntil(openOrFocus(safeReviewUrl(e.notification.data?.url)));
});
// safeReviewUrl: same-origin path only; parses search params with the /review route's zod schema;
// anything invalid becomes "/review" (the P0-22 rule: invalid deep links land on a valid default)
```

**Implementation notes**
- Push on iPhone works only for a PWA added to the Home Screen (iOS 16.4 and later) ([WebKit: Web Push for web apps on iOS](https://webkit.org/blog/13878/web-push-for-web-apps-on-ios-and-ipados/)); Settings detects standalone mode and explains the step.
- The permission prompt appears only after the user presses "Enable push" in Settings, never on load (UX 6).
- Push leaves the private network through the browser vendor's push service; the payload carries no client content, only the kind and a short label (Data flow rule 6).
- The api cannot call out: subscription endpoints only store; the worker sends.

#### P4-06 · README, docs and the v1 release

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone | M4.1 Finish the loop (weeks 15 to 16) |
| Size | M (1 to 2 agent-assisted days), PRs: spec + impl |
| Needs | none |
| Unblocks | none |
| Traces | REL-4, SEC-7 |

**Goal.** A second freelancer can install Tumnis from the README alone. The README's install commands are tagged and executed on a clean VM by CI, so they cannot drift; install and operations docs cover backups, restore, upgrade and rollback; and v1.0.0 is tagged with its SBOM and OpenAPI spec attached after the release checklist passes.

**Scope.** In: README structure and tagged blocks, `scripts/readme_test.py`, the `readme.yml` workflow, operations and install docs, the second person's install checklist, the release checklist and the v1.0.0 tag through P0-30's release workflow. Out: marketing copy, hosted-mode docs (v2).

**Files**

| Path | Change | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `README.md` | rewrite | What it is, requirements, install (tagged), first run, connect sources, phone setup, operate, develop |
| `docs/OPERATIONS.md` | new | Backups, restore drill, upgrade, rollback, rotating the master key, alerts |
| `docs/INSTALL-CHECKLIST.md` | new | The second person's checklist with timing and friction notes |
| `docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md` | new | v1.0.0 steps (below) |
| `scripts/readme_test.py` | new | Harness |
| `backend/tests/meta/test_readme_test.py` | new | Harness unit tests |
| `.github/workflows/readme.yml` | new | README job on a clean VM |
| `.env.example`, `deploy/compose.yaml` | edit | Only what the README needs to be literal |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | edit | v1.0.0 entry |

**Interfaces**

Tagged block grammar (the fence info string; GitHub renders the first word as the language and ignores the rest):

````
```bash readme:install:30 timeout=900
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml up -d
```
````

| Token | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `readme:<suite>:<order>` | Suite (`install`, `first-run`, `upgrade`, `manual`) and a sort key; blocks run by (document order, order) |
| `timeout=<s>` | Per-block timeout, default 300 (plan default) |
| `expect=<regex>` | Optional: stdout must match |
| `env` suite | `readme:env` blocks are `KEY=value` lines exported to later blocks; the only substitution the harness does |
| `manual` | Never run by CI (for example "install Tailscale on your phone"); listed in the install checklist |

```python
# scripts/readme_test.py
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Block: suite: str; order: int; lang: str; code: str; timeout: int; expect: re.Pattern | None; line: int

def extract(markdown: str) -> list[Block]: ...
def check_section_coverage(markdown: str, section: str = "Install") -> list[int]:
    """Line numbers of untagged shell blocks inside the section; must be empty."""
def run(blocks: Sequence[Block], env: Mapping[str, str], workdir: Path) -> Report: ...
# each block: bash -euo pipefail -c <code>, fresh process, cwd = repo root, env = base + readme:env exports
def wait_healthy(url: str, timeout_s: int = 600, ca_file: Path | None = None) -> None: ...
```

README install section outline (each step one tagged block): check Docker and Compose versions; clone; create the root-owned master key and pepper files (`install -m 600 -o root` from `openssl rand`); copy `.env.example` to `.env` with the listed variables; create the TLS certificate (self-signed for the test, Tailscale certificate for real installs, both shown); `docker compose up -d`; wait for `/health/ready`; `tumnis setup` (first run: user, password, TOTP secret printed once); sign in. Operations covers pgBackRest's B2 repository and write-no-delete key, the restore drill, upgrades (`docker compose pull`, migrate runs first) and rollback (redeploy the previous image, REL-4).

**TDD sequence**
1. T-P4-06-01, 02 red: `extract` and `check_section_coverage`; green.
2. T-P4-06-03, 04 red: `run` with per-block processes and env export; green.
3. T-P4-06-05 red: write the README install section block by block, running the harness locally in a throwaway VM (Proxmox template) until green; then the workflow on the GitHub-hosted runner.
4. T-P4-06-08 red: OPERATIONS.md upgrade and rollback blocks; nightly upgrade suite; green.
5. T-P4-06-07 red: extend P0-30's release workflow with asset verification; green.
6. Second person installs (manual): they follow only the README on their own machine, record time and friction in `docs/INSTALL-CHECKLIST.md`; every blocker becomes a README fix plus, where possible, a new tagged check.
7. T-P4-06-06 red: checklist evidence test on the release branch; fill the checklist; green; tag v1.0.0.

**Implementation notes**
- The GitHub-hosted runner is a fresh VM per job, which is what "clean VM" means here (plan default); the homelab runner is never used for this job because it is not clean.
- The README must not rely on Coolify: a plain `docker compose up` works for anyone without it (NFR Deployment). The Coolify path is a separate section tagged `readme:manual`.
- Private network only (FR-9.1): the README's first-run section explains Tailscale or VPN access and never suggests opening a port; the compose file's config test (P0-04) still guards it.
- Secrets in the test: the harness generates the master key and pepper like a user would, inside the VM; nothing from repository secrets is used, so a leaked log shows nothing reusable.
- The second person's install is the real exit criterion (PRD phase 4); the CI job keeps it true afterwards.

**Fixtures, fakes and data**
- `backend/tests/meta/data/readme_fixture.md` covering every token.
- Proxmox VM template for local dry runs (manual).

**Commands**
```bash
uv run --project backend pytest backend/tests/meta/test_readme_test.py -q
python scripts/readme_test.py --suite install --report out/readme-report.json    # in a throwaway VM
gh workflow run readme.yml --ref wp/P4-06-impl
gh release view v1.0.0 --json assets
```

**Done checklist**
- [ ] A4.4 passes and v1 is tagged (YAML done-when)
- [ ] A second freelancer installed from the README alone; checklist filed with no open blockers
- [ ] Release checklist rows all have evidence
- [ ] SBOM and OpenAPI attached to v1.0.0 (SEC-7, SAAS-1)
- [ ] Upgrade and rollback docs tested nightly (REL-4)

**Risks and fallbacks**
- The clean VM lacks something a real machine has (or the reverse): the second person's install is the ground truth; each surprise becomes a tagged check.
- TLS setup differs per network: the README shows the self-signed path (tested) and the Tailscale path (manual), and the health check accepts the README's own CA file.
- Tagging slips because of one open blocker: the phase 4 buffer week absorbs it; nothing else waits on the tag.

## Part H · Schedule and capacity

The PRD's week counts are sequencing, not commitments. Detailing every WP makes the effort measurable, and the numbers say phase 0 will not fit in four weeks with one reviewer. Plan on it.

### H1 · Effort against the calendar

Effort uses the WP sizes (S 0.5 to 1, M 1 to 2, L 3 to 4 agent-assisted days). "Streams" is how many WPs must be in flight at once to finish inside the phase's PRD calendar at 5 working days a week.

| Phase | Weeks (PRD) | WPs (S / M / L) | Effort, days | Working days | Parallel streams needed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 Foundation | 1 to 4 | 30 (3 / 19 / 8) | 44.5 to 73 | 20 | 2.2 to 3.7 |
| 1 AI core loop | 5 to 7 | 18 (2 / 10 / 6) | 29 to 46 | 15 | 1.9 to 3.1 |
| 2 Agent layer | 8 to 11 | 18 (1 / 11 / 6) | 29.5 to 47 | 20 | 1.5 to 2.4 |
| 3 Capture | 12 to 14 | 14 (3 / 10 / 1) | 14.5 to 27 | 15 | 1.0 to 1.8 |
| 4 Hardening | 15 to 16 | 6 (2 / 4 / 0) | 5 to 10 | 10 | 0.5 to 1.0 |
| **v1** | **16** | **86** | **122.5 to 203** | **80** | **1.5 to 2.5** |

**Critical path.** Following `needs` with the upper sizes, the longest chain is 44 working days: P0-01, P0-02, P0-04, P0-06, P0-08, P0-13, P0-14, P0-17, P0-18, P0-24, P0-25, P1-07, P1-08, P1-11, P2-15, P2-16. Its phase 0 segment alone is 20 working days at the lower sizes and 32 at the upper sizes, so phase 0 has no slack even at best.

**Simulated with two streams.** Scheduling every WP on two parallel lanes (Scott reviewing both), respecting `needs`, finishing each phase's WPs before starting the next phase's, and adding the real dependencies the YAML leaves implicit (P4 on P2-08, P2-15, P2-16 and P1-18; P3-01 on P2-04; everything after P0-05 on the CI guards and the acceptance suite):

| Sizes assumed | Phase 0 ends | Phase 1 ends | Phase 2 ends | Phase 3 ends | v1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lower (S 0.5, M 1, L 3) | week 5 | week 8 | week 11 | week 12 | week 13 |
| Middle (S 0.75, M 1.5, L 3.5) | week 7 | week 11 | week 14 | week 16 | week 17 |
| Upper (S 1, M 2, L 4) | week 8 | week 13 | week 18 | week 20 | week 21 |

**What that means**

- Two review-bound agent streams is the realistic ceiling for one person, and v1 lands in 13 to 21 weeks; 17 is the planning number. The summary plan's 16 weeks holds only if most WPs come in at the lower size.
- Phase 0's cut line (summary plan, change 6) is the pressure valve: passkeys, Lighthouse and the rollback rehearsal can move to phase 4; row-level security, the audit log, idempotency, backups and the CI guards cannot.
- Spec PRs are the cheapest thing to parallelize: writing phase N+1's acceptance suite and spec tests while phase N's implementation runs keeps both streams busy without adding code review.
- The usage gates (two weeks of daily planning, two weeks of agent tasks, two weeks of capture) run in parallel with the next phase's build, as the PRD intends; a gate that fails pauses the next phase's merges, not its spec work.

### H3 · Order inside each phase

- **Phase 0:** harness before features (P0-01 to P0-05), then tenancy and events (P0-06, P0-07) because every table and module depends on them, then identity and security sweeps before any business route exists, then projects and tasks, then the web app, then operations. P0-28 can start in week 2 because it depends only on the compose file; its first drill result answers architecture open question 3 early.
- **Phase 1:** the provider layer and the agent path run in parallel and meet in P1-07 and P1-08; the knowledge base (P1-14 onward) is the natural second stream.
- **Phase 2:** MCP surface and the packet first (everything calls them), then runs and approvals, then safety, then skills and focus. Draft P2-11's hostile set during P2-02, since packet escaping and the skills face the same inputs.
- **Phase 3:** learning tests before any connector (P3-01), because the connectors depend on provider behavior nobody has confirmed.
- **Phase 4:** the YAML lists no `needs` for P4 WPs, but they depend on P2-08, P2-15, P2-16 and P1-18; start them only after those merge.

## Part I · Risk register

Each WP carries its own risks and fallbacks. These are the ones that can move a gate or change the design, with the earliest signal to watch. Review weekly; a risk whose signal fires gets a review item on the Tumnis project itself.

| # | Risk | Where | Early signal | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Phase 0 runs past week 7 (critical path has no slack) | Phase 0 | P0-06 or P0-13 still open at the end of week 3 | Apply the cut line: passkeys, Lighthouse and the rollback rehearsal move to phase 4 |
| 2 | Agents weaken or delete tests to reach green | Every WP | spec-guard blocks; mutmut survivors rise on `rules.py` | `spec-change` stays Scott-only; review the survivors report weekly |
| 3 | DBOS API differs from the sketches (queues, schedules, partitions, dedup) | P0-07, P2-04, A9 | Contract tests on `worker.py` registration fail on the pinned version | Pin DBOS early in P0-07 and update A9 and every "(verify)" note in one PR |
| 4 | RLS leaks through a SECURITY DEFINER function or a new table outside `public` | P0-06, P0-13 | Table-registry or definer allow-list test fails | Nothing merges with those red; R-01 keeps every table in `public` |
| 5 | Hermes cannot be dispatched through a remote endpoint | P1-04 | Hermes release notes; the fake-only endpoint transport never goes green against a real profile | The daemon transport is the only v1 path (B5 point 1); FR-5.11's endpoint runner waits for Hermes |
| 6 | Jev thresholds wrong or drifting | P1-02, P3-08 | Override rate above the calibration page's accuracy; model version bump | Conservative defaults send most items to review; local fallback; recalibrate before raising thresholds |
| 7 | Skills tests are flaky on a live model | P1-05, P2-11, P2-12 | A case that passes 2 of 3 runs | Tighten the skill; pin the model; a flaky injection case blocks the profile change, never gets skipped |
| 8 | Prompt injection gets through a skill | P2-02, P2-11 | Any hostile case produces a requested tool call | Server-side gates still hold (taint, approval_required, no send); fix the skill and add the case |
| 9 | Two-way folder sync loses a file | P1-15, P3-14 | Folder-sync fixture failure; a conflict review item nobody expected | Never overwrite or delete what Tumnis did not create; keep both copies; pause writes when the marker is missing |
| 10 | Docling extraction is too slow or memory hungry on the homelab | P1-16 | `worker-extract` memory limit hit; extraction backlog alert | One extraction at a time, OCR only when a page has no text, VLM only on low-confidence pages |
| 11 | pgBackRest cannot run with a write-no-delete B2 key | P0-28 | First drill fails on archive-push or expire | B2 Object Lock with a delete-capable key (architecture fallback) |
| 12 | Coolify previews and deploys cannot be triggered by GitHub on a private network | P0-04 | Preview never appears on a PR | The homelab runner calls the Coolify API, or runs `docker compose -p pr-<n>` itself (B5 point 15) |
| 13 | Inbox Zero or Granola will not give Tumnis refresh tokens | P3-01 | Learning test fails | Hermes profile pushes items through `ingest_items`, a PRD deviation needing sign-off |
| 14 | Coolify tokens cannot be limited per app | P2-10 | Health check reports cross-project reach | One Coolify team per project (B5 point 6) |
| 15 | Focus support feels like nagging | P2-15, P2-16 | "Less of this" taps, Quiet chosen after a week at Nudge | Back-off, per-project cadence, activity suppression; measure before adding rules |
| 16 | The run time cap reading (active time plus 24 h ceiling) is not what SAF-5 meant | P2-04 | Scott's review of B5 point 4 | Switch to a pure wall-clock cap; approvals then time out at 60 minutes |
| 17 | Tiptap's Markdown extension changes output between versions | P1-17 | Round-trip suite fails on a Renovate PR | Pin; upgrade only with the suite green; CodeMirror 6 was the recorded alternative (ADR-0008) |
| 18 | Performance budgets fail on phone hardware over the VPN | P0-29 | Lighthouse or cold-open test over budget | Route splitting, lazy editor, smaller initial payload; budget changes need Scott |
| 19 | Scope creep into an agent framework | Phases 2 and 3 | A WP not traceable to J1 to J8 | Traceability job; new work enters as a WP with a requirement or not at all |

## Part K · Decisions and sources

### K1 · Decisions needed

Every row has a default the plan already builds on. Rows 1 to 4 are due in week 1.

| # | Decision | Needed by | Default in the plan |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Proposed libraries and styling (architecture open questions 1 and 2) | P0-01, P0-22 | Architecture defaults; Tailwind with headless primitives |
| 2 | Test tooling this plan adds: Hypothesis, fast-check, Schemathesis, squawk, mutmut, fake-indexeddb, pytest-socket, pytest-randomly, pytest-xdist | P0-02 | Adopt all, one ADR line each |
| 3 | Python type checker | P0-01 | mypy, strict on core and every `rules.py` |
| 4 | Plan for 17 weeks with two review-bound streams, not 16 | Now | 17 (Part H) |
| 5 | Pull the minimal agent path into phase 1 | M1.2 | Yes |
| 6 | Daemon as the only real Hermes transport until Hermes can serve runs over MCP (B5 point 1) | P1-04 | Yes |
| 7 | Jev MCP wrapper in `profiles/shared/jev-mcp` (B5 point 2) | P1-05 | Yes |
| 8 | Run time: 60 min of active time plus a 24 h wall-clock ceiling (B5 point 4) | P2-04 | Yes |
| 9 | Max concurrent runs fixed at 2 per project in v1 (B5 point 5) | P2-04 | Yes |
| 10 | One Coolify team per project for SAF-3 (B5 point 6) | P2-10 | Yes |
| 11 | Discord relays answers to questions and focus replies, not approvals or results (B5 point 7) | P2-16 | Yes |
| 12 | `pause_agents` for the master key, pause only | P2-09 | Yes |
| 13 | Keys without a run default to read scopes; their writes are tainted (B5 point 11) | P2-02 | Yes |
| 14 | Hidden carrier task for proposal runs (B5 point 12) | P3-07 | Yes |
| 15 | MinIO webhook bearer token plus object re-check instead of a signature (B5 point 8) | P3-13 | Yes |
| 16 | Green-light definition for unattended runs (B5 point 9) | P4-04 | As defined |
| 17 | Human tasks go Today, Start, Done (no direct Today to Done edge) (B5 point 16) | P0-18 | Keep the diagram |
| 18 | Coolify deploys and previews triggered from the homelab runner (B5 point 15) | P0-04 | Yes |
| 19 | GitHub status by polling; webhook relay later (B5 point 17) | P2-13 | Polling |
| 20 | Discord notifications on the Hermes gateway or a Tumnis chat connector (PRD open question 3) | P2-16 | Hermes gateway |
| 21 | Minimal A2A endpoint in v1 | Phase 2 | Not in v1 |
| 22 | First chat provider (PRD open question 2) | P3-01 | Decided in P3-01 |
| 23 | Fallback if Inbox Zero or Granola refuse refresh tokens | P3-01 | `ingest_items` push from Hermes, a PRD deviation |
